AK.name: Alaska

definition.quote: “motor vehicle” means a vehicle which is self-propelled except a vehicle moved by human or animal power;
definition.motor_watts_basis: No e-bike statute. Closest text: “motor vehicle” means a vehicle which is self-propelled
definition.notes: Alaska Statutes 2025 contain no e-bike definition. The regulation defines 'bicycle' as 'a vehicle propelled exclusively by human power' (13 AAC 40.010(a)(5)), so an e-bike is not a bicycle. It appears to be a 'motor vehicle' (self-propelled), and with a seat and no more than 3 wheels it fits 'motorcycle' (AS 28.90.990(a)(21)). 'Motor-driven cycle' covers a 'motorized bicycle, or similar conveyance with a motor attached and having an engine with 50 or less cubic centimeters of displacement' (a)(22), a cc test that does not map to electric motors. Which category DMV applies to a 750 W e-bike was not confirmed from an official source. HB 8 (2023), which would have created the three classes and excluded e-bikes of 750 W or less from 'motor vehicle', passed 39-1 and 18-1 but was vetoed Jul 20, 2023.

label_required.notes: No e-bike label law, since there is no e-bike statute.

license_registration_insurance.quote: The department may issue a special driver's permit to a person who is at least 14 years of age with the consent of the person's parents, guardians, or spouse ... for the purpose of driving a motor-driven cycle.
license_registration_insurance.notes: If an e-bike is a motor vehicle under AS 28.90.990(a)(20), licensing (AS 28.15), registration (AS 28.10) and insurance (AS 28.22) rules would apply by default. That conclusion is an inference and was not confirmed from DMV guidance or case law, so all three are null. News coverage of HB 8 (2023) described current law as treating e-bikes as motor vehicles. If treated as a motor-driven cycle, a 14-year-old could ride with a special permit and parental consent (AS 28.15.051(d)), unless a municipality bans under-16 motor-driven cycle drivers.

where_allowed.roads: Unclear. Depends on whether the e-bike is a motor vehicle, motorcycle or motor-driven cycle.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Unclear at state level. Land managers and municipalities set their own rules (not researched).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Unclear.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: No class system.

local_authority.quote: The permit is not valid in a municipality that by ordinance prohibits the driving of a motor-driven cycle by a person under the age of 16 years
local_authority.details: Municipalities can bar under-16 drivers of motor-driven cycles. Whether that reaches e-bikes depends on the unresolved classification. Anchorage and other cities may define e-bikes in their own codes (not researched).

non_ebike_devices.quote: “motor-driven cycle” means a motorcycle, motor scooter, motorized bicycle, or similar conveyance with a motor attached and having an engine with 50 or less cubic centimeters of displacement;
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorcycle or motor-driven cycle (same as e-bikes, since Alaska has no e-bike category)
non_ebike_devices.notes: Alaska draws no legal line between an e-bike and an e-moto, so the app cannot give a confident 'legal' answer for any electric bike in Alaska from state law. Motorcycle license, helmet and registration rules were not verified.

open_questions: How Alaska DMV and police actually classify a 750 W pedal e-bike (motor vehicle, motorcycle or motor-driven cycle) and what license, registration and insurance they require. No official guidance was read.

Resolved by verifier: no 34th Legislature (2025 to 2026) bill has 'bicycle' or 'bike' in its short title on akleg.gov, and no e-bike bill is filed under the Motor Vehicles, Transportation or Highways subjects. The only enacted motor vehicle bill, SB 239 (ch. 39 SLA 26), has no bicycle text, and AS 28.90.990 still has no e-bike definition.
Whether 'a vehicle moved by human or animal power' (excluded from 'motor vehicle') covers pedal-assist e-bikes. Not resolved by text.
Municipal rules (Anchorage, Juneau, Fairbanks) not researched.
AK.never_return_legal_reason: No Alaska statute defines an e-bike (HB 8 of 2023 was vetoed). An e-bike appears to be a motor vehicle or motorcycle under AS 28.90.990, and DMV practice is unconfirmed.
AK.verifier_notes: Quotes match the akleg.gov statute text. No 2025 or 2026 e-bike bill exists, so the never-legal flag stands.

AL.name: Alabama

definition.quote: ELECTRIC BICYCLE. A bicycle equipped with fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat for the rider, and an electric motor of less than 750 watts that meets the requirements of one of the following three classes:
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than 750 watts
definition.notes: Motor must be LESS THAN 750 W, so a bike labeled exactly 750 W does not meet the text. Requires a saddle or seat. 32-5A-267(f) requires the motor to disengage when the rider stops pedaling or the brakes are applied. 32-5A-267(k) requires a speedometer on Class 3. Enacted by Act 2021-134 (HB 99). The ALISON code page shows no later amendment to 32-5A-267. An e-bike must also be a 'bicycle' (32-1-1.1(4)), which needs two tandem wheels, either more than 14 inches in diameter. An electric trike, or a bike whose wheels are all 14 inches or smaller, does not fit the text and would fall under 'motorcycle'. 'Motorcycle' and 'motor-driven cycle' exclude electric bicycles (32-1-1.1(36), (37), 32-12-20).

label_required.quote: manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed in a prominent location to each electric bicycle. The label shall contain the classification number, top assisted speed, and motor wattage

min_age.quote: An individual under the age of 16 years may not operate a Class 3 electric bicycle. An individual under the age of 16 years may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 electric bicycle
min_age.exceptions: Under-16 passengers allowed on a Class 3 designed for passengers. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2. SB 73 (2023) would have set age 14 for Class 1 and 2, but it died and the current code does not contain it.

helmet.quote: All operators and passengers of Class 3 electric bicycles shall wear a properly fitted and fastened protective bicycle helmet
For any person under the age of 16 years to operate or be a passenger on a bicycle unless at all times the person wears a protective bicycle helmet of good fit, fastened securely upon the head
helmet.notes: 32-5A-281(1) defines 'bicycle' for this article as human-powered, so this reaches Class 1 and 2 e-bikes only through 32-5A-267(a), which gives e-bike riders all the duties of a bicycle operator. Treat as required for safety. Parents who knowingly permit a violation are also liable (32-5A-283(3)).

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric bicycle or individual operating an electric bicycle is not subject to the requirements of this title relating to driver’s licenses, registration, certificates of title, off-road vehicles, all-terrain vehicles ... financial responsibility, or motor vehicle insurance.

where_allowed.quote: An electric bicycle may be ridden in places where bicycles are allowed, including, but not limited to, streets, roadways, highways, shoulders, bicycle lanes, and bicycle or multi-use paths.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed where bicycles are, with bicycle rights and duties (32-5A-267(a), (g)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Allowed on bicycle and multi-use paths. After notice and a public hearing, a county, municipality or other subdivision may ban Class 1 or 2 on its paths if needed for safety or legal compliance (32-5A-267(h)(1)a). This path-ban power does not cover nonmotorized natural-surface trails (32-5A-267(h)(2)), and the statute is silent on e-bikes there.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No state e-bike sidewalk rule found.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: After notice and a public hearing, a local entity may ban Class 3 on its bicycle or multi-use paths without a safety finding (32-5A-267(h)(1)b). Under 16 may not operate. Helmet at all ages. Speedometer required.

local_authority.quote: Following notice and a public hearing, a county, municipality, or other political subdivision of the state that has jurisdiction over a bicycle or multi-use path may do both of the following:
local_authority.details: Path bans are expressly allowed. General local traffic powers in Title 32 were not located or checked, so local age limits are unverified. Gulf Shores reported a city ordinance regulating e-bike operation passed Jan 26, 2026 (city web page, not read).

non_ebike_devices.quote: MOTOR-DRIVEN CYCLE. Every motorcycle, including every motor scooter, with a motor that produces not more than five brake horsepower ... and weighs less than 200 pounds fully equipped, and every bicycle with a motor attached.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motor-driven cycle (5 bhp or less, under 200 lb, includes any bicycle with a motor attached) or motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device that fails the e-bike definition is a 'motor vehicle' (self-propelled, 32-1-1.1(35)), and a bicycle with a motor attached is a motor-driven cycle. Motor vehicle license, registration and insurance rules then apply. A motor-driven cycle needs a Class M license, and one with a motor-driven cycle restriction can be issued from age 14 after a knowledge test or an approved rider course (32-12-22(b)(1)). min_age 14 applies to motor-driven cycles only. Helmet and registration details for motor-driven cycles were not verified in statute text.

open_questions: Whether the under-16 bicycle helmet rule (32-5A-283) reaches Class 1 and 2 e-bikes, since 'bicycle' is defined as human-powered there.
Whether cities and counties can set e-bike age limits. Only path bans are expressly authorized.

Partly resolved by verifier: a Class M license with a motor-driven cycle restriction is available from age 14 (32-12-22(b)(1)). Helmet and registration rules for motor-driven cycles were not verified.

Resolved by verifier: an ALISON full-text search of bills for 'electric bicycle' finds nothing from the 2025 or 2026 regular sessions. The latest hits are SB 73 of 2023, which died, and 2024 acts that changed other definitions. 32-5A-267 still cites only Act 2021-134.

verdict_cautions.reason: An electric bicycle must first be a 'bicycle', which needs two tandem wheels, either more than 14 inches in diameter (32-1-1.1(4)). A kids' e-bike with 14 inch or smaller wheels falls under 'motorcycle' instead.
Alabama's 'bicycle' has two tandem wheels (32-1-1.1(4)), so an electric trike may not be an 'electric bicycle'. No source settles it.

AL.verifier_notes: All quotes match the official ALISON code and no 2025 or 2026 e-bike bill exists. Added cautions for the 14-inch wheel rule and electric trikes, plus the age-14 motor-driven cycle license.

AR.name: Arkansas

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a bicycle equipped with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty watts (750 W) that meets one (1) of the classifications
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty watts (750 W)
definition.notes: Motor must be LESS THAN 750 W. Text read from the enacted Act 956 of 2017 (approved Apr 7, 2017) and checked against FindLaw's reproduction of 27-51-1706 and 27-20-101 ('current as of March 28, 2024'). 27-51-1704(d): Class 2 motor must cut off when the brakes are applied, and Class 1 and 3 motors when the rider stops pedaling. Class 3 needs a speedometer (27-51-1706(c)).

label_required.quote: On and after January 1, 2018, a manufacturer or distributor of electric bicycles shall apply a label in at least nine-point type that is permanently affixed in a prominent location to each electric bicycle
label_required.notes: Label must identify classification number, top assisted speed and motor wattage.

min_age.quote: A person under sixteen (16) years of age shall not operate a Class 3 electric bicycle.
min_age.quote_note: Wording confirmed in the official Act 956 of 2017 (sec. 3), which created 27-51-1706 and prints 'class 3' in lowercase. arkleg Code Sections Amended lists show no later amendment through the 2026 sessions.
min_age.exceptions: Under 16 may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 designed for passengers (27-51-1706(a)(2)). No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2.

helmet.quote: A person under twenty-one (21) years of age who is an operator of or a passenger on a Class 3 electric bicycle shall wear a helmet
helmet.quote_note: Wording confirmed in the official Act 956 of 2017 (sec. 3), which created 27-51-1706(b) and prints 'class 3' in lowercase. No later amendment through the 2026 sessions.
helmet.notes: No statewide helmet rule for Class 1 or 2, or for ordinary bicycles, was found.

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric bicycle is not a motor vehicle; and (3) An electric bicycle or an operator of an electric bicycle is not subject to the provisions of this title relating to insurance, licensing, registration, operator’s licenses, and certificates of title.

where_allowed.quote: A class 3 electric bicycle shall not be operated on a bicycle path or multi-use path unless it is within or adjacent to a highway or roadway, or unless the local authority having jurisdiction over the path permits
where_allowed.roads: Bicycle rights and duties (27-51-1703(1), 27-49-111). Act 650 of 2019 added the bicycle stop-as-yield rules (27-51-1801 and following), which name electric bicycles.
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Treated as a bicycle. No e-bike-specific rule found.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 and 2 may use bicycle and multi-use paths where bicycles are permitted, but the local authority with jurisdiction may prohibit them (27-51-1705(a)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: No state e-bike sidewalk rule found.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Class 3 is barred from bicycle and multi-use paths unless within or adjacent to a highway or roadway, or the local authority permits it (27-51-1705(b)). Under 16 may not operate. Under 21 must wear a helmet.

local_authority.quote: the local authority having jurisdiction over a bicycle path or multi-use path may prohibit the operation of a class 1 electric bicycle or a class 2 electric bicycle on that path.
local_authority.details: Path bans are expressly allowed. General municipal traffic powers were not checked, so local age limits are unverified.

non_ebike_devices.quote: any person fourteen (14) years of age or older who is under the lawful age to obtain a motorcycle operator's license may operate a motor-driven cycle if that person has obtained a special license
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorized bicycle (automatic transmission, motor 50 cc or less), motor-driven cycle (250 cc or less) or motorcycle (over 250 cc); the cc-based tests do not map cleanly to electric motors
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device failing the e-bike definition is a motor vehicle. Arkansas defines motorized bicycles, motor-driven cycles and motorcycles by engine displacement (cc), so how an electric e-moto is classified is unclear. A motor-driven cycle requires a motorcycle operator license, or a special license from age 14 to 16 after a State Police exam (27-20-106(b)). min_age 14 applies to motor-driven cycles only. Motorized bicycle license, helmet and registration rules were not verified.

open_questions: Resolved by verifier: arkleg 'Code Sections Amended' lists for the 2019, 2021, 2023 and 2025 regular sessions and the 2026 fiscal and extraordinary sessions show no act touching 27-51-1701 to 1706, and a full-text bill search of the 2025 and 2026 sessions for the phrase 'electric bicycle' returns no results. The official Lexis code was still not opened.
How Arkansas classifies electric devices over 750 W given cc-based definitions in 27-20-101.
Whether cities may set e-bike age limits.
No statewide bicycle helmet law was found for Class 1 and 2 riders. Confirm there is none.
AR.verifier_notes: Quotes match the enacted Act 956 of 2017, and arkleg lists show no later amendment through the 2026 sessions. The 27-20-106 quote could not be machine-checked because FindLaw and Justia show a bot check.

AZ.name: Arizona

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a bicycle or tricycle that is equipped with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty watts
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty watts
definition.notes: Motor must be LESS THAN 750 W, so a label reading exactly 750 W does not meet the text. Class 1 and 3 assist only while pedaling (cut off at 20 and 28 mph). Class 2 'may be used exclusively to propel' the bike and cannot assist at 20 mph. No Class 3 speedometer requirement in the definition. Bicycle or tricycle only. An e-bike must also be a 'bicycle' or 'tricycle'. 28-101(11) defines 'bicycle' as having two tandem wheels, either more than 16 inches in diameter, or three wheels, any more than 16 inches. A two-wheel e-bike whose wheels are all 16 inches or smaller (many kids' and folding bikes) does not fit the text and would fall under 'motorcycle' or 'motor driven cycle' (license, registration, insurance).

label_required.quote: manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each electric bicycle. The label shall contain the classification number, top assisted speed and motor wattage

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric bicycle or an electric standup scooter is not subject to the provisions of this title relating to certificates of title, registration, vehicle license tax, driver licenses or vehicle insurance.

where_allowed.quote: A class 1 electric bicycle, a class 2 electric bicycle or an electric standup scooter may be used on bicycle and multiuse paths.
where_allowed.roads: Same rights and duties as a bicycle rider (28-819(A)).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Treated as a bicycle (28-819(A)). No state e-bike-specific bike lane rule found.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 and 2 allowed on bicycle and multiuse paths, but the state agency or local authority with jurisdiction may prohibit them (28-819(D)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: No state e-bike sidewalk rule found. Left to local regulation under 28-627(A)(8) and (14).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Class 3 may not be ridden on a bicycle or multiuse path unless it is within or adjacent to a highway or roadway, or the agency with jurisdiction allows it (28-819(E)).

local_authority.quote: Regulating electric bicycles and electric standup scooters.
local_authority.details: The grant in 28-627(A)(14) is broad and unqualified, and 28-819(A) says e-bikes follow bicycle rules 'except ... as otherwise regulated by a local authority.' Cities use it to set age limits. Scottsdale Revised Code 17-77.1 (Ordinance 4680, effective Jul 31, 2025) bars riders under 16 from Class 3 e-bikes and similar devices that reach 21 mph on city property, confirmed on the city's website. Secondary sources (not verified) report Tempe has an under-16 Class 3 rule, Phoenix sets age 16 and bans sidewalk riding, and Maricopa County scheduled a Nov 4, 2026 hearing on an unincorporated-area ordinance. The engine must check city rules in Arizona.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Moped" means a bicycle, not including an electric bicycle ... that is equipped with a helper motor if the vehicle has a maximum piston displacement of fifty cubic centimeters or less, a brake horsepower of one and one-half or less
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (helper motor, 1.5 bhp or less, 25 mph or less) or motor driven cycle / motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device that fails the e-bike definition (750 W or more, no operable pedals, or exceeds the class speeds) is a 'motor vehicle' (self-propelled and not excluded) and falls under the moped, motor driven cycle (5 hp or less) or motorcycle definitions. 28-3101(A)(6) says a class M license 'is valid for operating a motorcycle, motor driven cycle or moped.' 28-964 requires helmets for motorcycle and motor driven cycle riders under 18. I did not confirm whether a moped also needs registration and insurance, or the minimum license age. Off-road, 28-1171(6) defines an off-highway vehicle to include 'any other means of land transportation deriving motive power from a source other than muscle or wind' and 28-1179(B) requires a DOT helmet for OHV riders under 18.

open_questions: Resolved by verifier: SB 1073 (2026) was held in committee and its companion SB 1008 was held awaiting second reading (azleg bill status API), so neither passed. None of the 529 chaptered laws of the 2025 and 2026 sessions contains the word 'bicycle'.

28-3151(C), added by SB 1567 (2024 ch. 240), says 'A person may not drive an off-highway vehicle in this state without a valid driver license', and 28-1171(6) does not exclude e-bikes. But 28-819(B) exempts e-bikes from the Title 28 driver-license provisions, so the license rule likely does not reach a compliant e-bike. Whether an e-mountain bike ridden off-highway is an 'off-highway vehicle' (OHV decal, DOT helmet under 18 under 28-1179(B)) is still unsettled.
Whether a 750 W labeled bike is an e-bike given the 'less than seven hundred fifty watts' text.
Moped registration, insurance and minimum license age not verified.
Scottsdale's rule was confirmed on the city's website (Revised Code 17-77.1). Phoenix, Tempe, Tucson, Glendale and Pima County rules were not verified from municipal code text.

verdict_cautions.reason: An electric bicycle must be a 'bicycle' or 'tricycle', and a two-wheel 'bicycle' needs a wheel more than 16 inches in diameter (28-101(11)). A smaller-wheel bike falls under 'motorcycle' or 'motor driven cycle'.

AZ.verifier_notes: Quotes match azleg.gov, and none of the 529 chaptered laws of 2025 and 2026 mentions bicycles. Added a caution for the 16-inch wheel rule, and Scottsdale's under-16 Class 3 rule confirms local age limits.

CA.name: California

definition.quote: An “electric bicycle” is a bicycle equipped with fully operable pedals and an electric motor that does not exceed 750 watts of power.
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor that does not exceed 750 watts of power
definition.notes: 750 W exactly qualifies ('does not exceed'). CORRECTION to ideas_red_team.md, which said 'under 750 watts'. Current text is as amended by SB 1271 (Stats. 2024, ch. 791), effective Jan 1, 2025. Class 1 and 3 may not be 'capable of exclusively propelling the bicycle' except a walk mode up to 3.7 mph (312.5(a)(4)). Class 3 must have a speedometer. 312.5(d): not an e-bike if built to be modifiable past 20 mph on motor alone or 750 W, modified that way, or pedals removed. 24016(a)(2): motor must cut off when brakes are applied or a switch is released. From Jan 1, 2027 SB 1167 rewrites 312.5 (adds 'e-bike' as a term and lists non-e-bikes: over 750 W, over 20 mph on motor alone, assist past 28 mph, no operable pedals, any motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, moped, motorized scooter, off-highway electric motorcycle, pocket bike).

label_required.citation: Cal. Veh. Code 312.5(c); from Jan 1, 2027 Veh. Code 28170(a) (AB 2346) and 28180 (SB 1167)
label_required.quote: manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each electric bicycle. The label shall contain the classification number, top assisted speed, and motor wattage
label_required.notes: On Jan 1, 2027 the label rule moves from 312.5(c) to new 28170(a) (AB 2346, Stats. 2026, ch. 842), same content. SB 1167 (ch. 846) adds 28180: label must also show brand and manufacturer, importer or distributor, be on the frame or fork, and be visible without flipping the bike. 28182: class labels may only be sold and installed at a physical retailer or bike shop that verifies the class. 28170(b) adds point-of-sale disclosures, including continuous and peak wattage.

min_age.quote: A person under 16 years of age shall not operate a class 3 electric bicycle.
min_age.exceptions: Rule covers operating, not riding as a passenger. 21212.5 (AB 965, effective Jan 1, 2026) also bars selling a Class 3 to anyone under 16. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2. Cities and counties in the San Diego and Marin County pilots, and in San Mateo County from Jan 1, 2027, may set their own age limits.

helmet.quote: A person under 18 years of age shall not operate a bicycle ... upon a street, bikeway ... or any other public bicycle path or trail unless they are wearing a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet
helmet.notes: Applies to e-bikes because 312.5(b) puts e-bike riders under Article 4 (21200 and following). Fine up to $25, parent jointly liable. Version effective Jan 1, 2026 (AB 544) lets a CHP e-bike safety course clear an e-bike helmet citation (21212(f)).

helmet.quote: A person shall not operate a class 3 electric bicycle, or ride upon a class 3 electric bicycle as a passenger ... unless that person is wearing a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet

license_registration_insurance.quote: A person operating an electric bicycle is not subject to the provisions of this code relating to financial responsibility, driver’s licenses, registration, and license plate requirements, and an electric bicycle is not a motor vehicle.
license_registration_insurance.notes: Version amended by AB 545 (effective Jan 1, 2026), which also bars selling products or apps that push a bike out of the e-bike definition (24016(e)). Local bicycle registration ordinances are allowed under 21206.

where_allowed.quote: The local authority or governing body of a public agency having jurisdiction over an equestrian trail, or hiking or recreational trail, may prohibit, by ordinance, the operation of an electric bicycle or any class of electric bicycle on that trail.
where_allowed.roads: E-bike riders follow the bicycle rules in Article 4 (312.5(b)).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: No e-bike-specific ban. 21207.5(a) restricts 'motorized bicycles' (mopeds, VC 406), not e-bikes.
where_allowed.paths_trails: No state ban on any class on bike paths since AB 1909 (effective Jan 1, 2023). Local agencies may ban e-bikes or any class on equestrian, hiking or recreational trails (21207.5(b)). State Parks may ban them on its bike paths (21207.5(c)). Locals may regulate operation on pedestrian or bicycle facilities (21206). From Jan 1, 2027 locals may set 15 or 20 mph limits on bike paths and multiuse trails, or 10 mph in limited high-pedestrian or low-visibility areas, with posted signs (new 21214.8, AB 2346).
where_allowed.sidewalks: No statewide e-bike sidewalk ban. Local ordinances may regulate or prohibit (21206). From Jan 1, 2027 the prima facie sidewalk speed limit is 10 mph (new 22352.1, AB 2346).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Under 16 may not operate. Helmet for all riders and passengers. Speedometer required. No state path ban since 2023, but local trail bans can target Class 3.

local_authority.quote: A local authority within the County of San Diego, or the County of San Diego in unincorporated areas, may, by ordinance or resolution, prohibit a person under 12 years of age from operating a class 1 or 2 electric bicycle.
local_authority.details: Local age limits exist only through named county pilots. (1) San Diego County cities and the County may ban under-12 riders from Class 1 and 2 (21214.7, AB 2234 (2024), amended by AB 1170 (2025), repealed Jan 1, 2029). (2) Marin County cities and the County may ban under-16 riders from Class 2 and may require helmets on Class 2 (21214.5, AB 1778, inoperative Jan 1, 2029). (3) From Jan 1, 2027, San Mateo County cities and the County may ban under-12 riders from Class 1 and 2 (21214.9, AB 2595, Stats. 2026, ch. 843, repealed Jan 1, 2031). All pilots: 60-day warning period, then a $25 infraction, cleared by a safety course, parent jointly liable. Outside these counties no local age-limit authority was found. Locals may also ban e-bikes on equestrian, hiking and recreational trails (21207.5(b)) and regulate operation and registration on pedestrian and bicycle facilities (21206). The City of San Diego adopted the under-12 rule in O-22123 N.S. (SDMC 84.19 to 84.21), effective Aug 13, 2026, with citations from Oct 12, 2026, and Carlsbad adopted it in Ord. CS-509 (CMC 10.56.030(A)), effective Mar 26, 2026. Both were read in enacted text on Oct 19, 2026, and data/rules/san_diego_local.json holds those records.

non_ebike_devices.quote: A “motorized bicycle” or “moped” is a two-wheeled or three-wheeled device having fully operative pedals ... or having no pedals if powered solely by electrical energy ... and a motor that produces less than 4 gross brake horsepower
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorized bicycle / moped (under 4 gross bhp, 30 mph or less), motor-driven cycle, or motorcycle; off-road pedal-less e-motos are off-highway electric motorcycles (SB 586, 2025)
non_ebike_devices.notes: Over 750 W, no operable pedals, or over 20 mph on motor alone: not an e-bike. Current law: a moped needs a special DMV plate (5030) and a helmet at all ages on highways (27803). License class (M1 or M2) and minimum age were not verified in statute here (red team notes cite DMV: under-21 must finish a motorcycle safety course). From Jan 1, 2027 (SB 1167, Stats. 2026, ch. 846): 'motorized bicycle' is renamed 'moped', redefined as an electric or gas device under 4 gross bhp (3,000 W), 30 mph or less, designed for highway use, FMVSS compliant with a 17-digit VIN (pedals optional). A motor-driven cycle becomes an electric motorcycle of 5 gross bhp (3,750 W) or less with FMVSS and VIN. Amended 23135 (SB 1167 SEC. 42) bans operating any 2- or 3-wheeled electric device capable of over 20 mph on motor alone on a highway or public right-of-way unless it fits a vehicle class explicitly defined and authorized for road use, including devices with multiple speed modes and off-road models. 22651.08 is already in force (added by AB 875, Stats. 2025, ch. 168, effective Jan 1, 2026), not a 2027 change. It lets officers remove a vehicle with fewer than four wheels that is not an e-bike, can exceed 20 mph on motor power alone and is ridden by an unlicensed operator, or a Class 3 ridden by someone under 16. SB 1167 extends removal to devices barred by amended 23135 from Jan 1, 2027.

pending_changes.summary: Non-urgency, so effective Jan 1, 2027. Moves the class label rule to new 28170 and adds point-of-sale disclosures (class, max speed, continuous and peak watts, age and helmet rules, a recommendation that under-16 riders stay under 15 mph). Sets a 10 mph prima facie sidewalk speed limit (22352.1, no violation point). Lets locals set 15 or 20 mph limits on bike paths and multiuse trails, and 10 mph only in limited areas with high pedestrian volumes or sight-distance problems, with signs at each end (21214.8). From Jan 1, 2029, Class 2 must have a speedometer and every e-bike sold must have front and rear lamps (28172).

CO.name: Colorado

definition.citation: C.R.S. 42-1-102(28.5), as amended by HB25-1197 (2025 Colo. Sess. Laws ch. 279, sec. 2)
definition.quote: "Electrical assisted bicycle" means a vehicle having two or three wheels, fully operable pedals, and an electric motor not exceeding seven hundred fifty watts of power.
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor not exceeding seven hundred fifty watts of power
definition.notes: 750 W exactly qualifies ('not exceeding'). Class 2 'provides assistance regardless of whether the rider is pedaling' to 20 mph. HB25-1197 (approved May 28, 2025, effective Aug 6, 2025 per the OLLS 2025 Red Book) added 42-1-102(28.5)(b): the term excludes a vehicle modified so it no longer meets any class, and one 'designed, manufactured, or intended ... to be easily configured' out of the classes by switch, software setting or app. It also defines a 'multiple mode electrical assisted bicycle' (42-1-102(60.2)) that can operate as two or more classes and must meet the rules for each class it can run as (42-4-221(10)(d)).

label_required.quote: every manufacturer or distributor of new electrical assisted bicycles ... shall permanently affix to each electrical assisted bicycle, in a prominent location, a label that contains the classification number, top assisted speed, and motor wattage
label_required.notes: From Jan 1, 2027, multiple-mode e-bikes must also show the highest class or each class they can run as (42-4-221(9)(c), HB25-1197). 42-4-221(13) requires sellers to disclose watts, top speed and class, and that riders under 16 may not ride Class 3.

min_age.quote: A person under sixteen years of age shall not ride a class 3 electrical assisted bicycle upon any street, highway, or bike or pedestrian path; except that a person under sixteen years of age may ride as a passenger
min_age.exceptions: Under 16 may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 designed for passengers. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2. A multiple-mode bike that can run as Class 3 must meet Class 3 rules.

helmet.quote: A person shall not operate or ride as a passenger on a class 3 electrical assisted bicycle unless: (I) Each person under eighteen years of age is wearing a protective helmet

license_registration_insurance.quote: except that the term does not include electrical assisted bicycles, electric scooters, low-power scooters except as provided in subsection (58)(b) of this section, wheelchairs, or vehicles moved solely by human power
license_registration_insurance.notes: E-bikes are excluded from 'motor vehicle', so state license, registration and insurance rules for motor vehicles do not apply. But 42-4-111(1) lets local authorities regulate e-bikes 'and require the registration and licensing of same, including the requirement of a registration fee', so local registration is possible.

where_allowed.quote: A person shall not ride a class 3 electrical assisted bicycle on a bike or pedestrian path unless: (I) The path is within a street or highway; or (II) The local authority permits
where_allowed.roads: Bicycle rights and duties, subject to local ordinances within cities and towns (42-4-1412(1)).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Treated as a bicycle. No e-bike-specific restriction found.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 and 2 may ride on a bike or pedestrian path where bicycles may travel, but a local authority may prohibit them (42-4-1412(14)(a)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Allowed unless prohibited by official traffic control devices or local ordinance. Riders must yield to pedestrians and give an audible signal before passing (42-4-1412(10)).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Class 3 is barred from bike or pedestrian paths unless the path is within a street or highway or the local authority permits it (42-4-1412(14)(b)). Under 16 may not ride. Under 18 must wear a helmet.

local_authority.quote: Regulating the operation of bicycles or electrical assisted bicycles and requiring the registration and licensing of same, including the requirement of a registration fee, consistent with the provisions of this article
local_authority.details: Local authorities may regulate e-bike operation, require registration and licensing, and authorize or prohibit e-bikes on bike and pedestrian paths (42-4-111(1), 42-4-1412(14)). Rules must be 'consistent with' article 4, so a local age limit for Class 1 or 2 is plausible but not expressly authorized. A Columbine Valley trustee bill (2026) proposed local age and helmet rules (adoption not confirmed).

non_ebike_devices.quote: “Low-power scooter” means a self-propelled vehicle ... with not more than three wheels in contact with the ground, no manual clutch, and ... A wattage not exceeding four thousand four hundred seventy-six if powered by electricity.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: low-power scooter (electric up to 4,476 W, no manual clutch) or motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device over 750 W, without operable pedals, outside the class speeds, or built to be easily switched out of class is not an e-bike. Up to 4,476 W with no manual clutch it is a low-power scooter, otherwise a motorcycle. Sellers must give a written 'This vehicle is not an electrical assisted bicycle' disclosure and may not label such vehicles with a class (42-4-221(12)). License, registration, insurance and helmet rules for low-power scooters were not verified in statute text. The 'low-power scooter' definition is 42-1-102(48.5)(a) on colorado.public.law.

pending_changes.summary: From Jan 1, 2027 the class label on a multiple-mode e-bike must identify the highest class or each class it can operate as.

open_questions: Resolved by verifier: the quoted text matches both colorado.public.law and the official CRS 2024 PDF on leg.colorado.gov. A text search of every 2025 and 2026 session law found e-bike rule changes only in HB25-1197. HB26-1237 (crash wording in 42-4-1412(13) and 42-4-221(12)), HB26-1426 (consumer-protection wording in 42-4-221(12)(c)) and HB25-1281 (kei vehicles added to 'motor vehicle') leave the e-bike rules unchanged. SB25-264, SB25-317, HB26-1289 and HB26-1362 only touch the e-bike tax credit and its cash fund.

Resolved by verifier: HB26-1079, the Cole Bradley Act (2026 Colo. Sess. Laws ch. 149, effective Aug 12, 2026), only requires a minor to have written permission to get a motorcycle instruction permit. It does not change e-bike rules.
HB26-1125 (parent penalties for minors illegally riding e-bikes and e-motos) was postponed indefinitely per news and the bill page summary. Not law.
Whether a Colorado city can set a minimum age for Class 1 or 2 is not settled by the text.
Low-power scooter license, registration and helmet rules not verified.

verdict_cautions.reason: Since Aug 6, 2025 the term excludes a vehicle modified out of every class or designed to be easily configured out of them by switch, software or app (42-1-102(28.5)(b)). A throttle above 20 mph fits no class, so the bike is a low-power scooter or motorcycle.

CO.verifier_notes: Quotes match the official CRS 2024 and HB25-1197, and the Jan 1, 2027 label change is confirmed. Added a caution for bikes that are switchable out of class or have a throttle above 20 mph.

CT.name: Connecticut

definition.citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. 14-1(13), (14), (15), (31), as amended by P.A. 26-24 sec. 26
definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a bicycle equipped with operable foot pedals and an electric motor of [fewer] not more than seven hundred fifty watts of power that is either a class 1, class 2 or class 3 bicycle.
definition.quote_note: Quoted from the public act, where [fewer] is struck text and 'not more than' is new text.
definition.motor_watts_basis: not more than seven hundred fifty watts of power
definition.notes: P.A. 26-24 (approved May 27, 2026, effective Oct 1, 2026) changed the motor limit from 'fewer than' to 'not more than' 750 W, so a 750 W bike now qualifies. Before Oct 1, 2026 the text was 'fewer than seven hundred fifty watts.' The definition excludes dirt bikes and ATVs. Class 2 motor must disengage when the brakes are applied or at 20 mph (14-1(14)). 14-289l(a)(3) requires a speedometer on Class 3. 14-289n (P.A. 25-159) says a vehicle is NOT an e-bike if it has a throttle and can exceed 20 mph on motor power alone in any mode, or is built or modified (switch, software, app) to fall outside the definition. Source for the current 14-1 text other than (31): https://www.cga.ct.gov/2026/sup/chap_246.htm

label_required.quote: affix a conspicuous label to each electric bicycle that contains the classification, maximum speed and motor wattage of such electric bicycle in print not smaller than nine-point type size

min_age.quote: No person under the age of sixteen shall ride a class 3 electric bicycle. Any person under the age of sixteen may sit as a passenger on a class 3 electric bicycle
min_age.exceptions: Under-16 riders may be passengers on a Class 3 built or equipped for a passenger. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2.

helmet.quote: No person shall ride or sit as a passenger on an electric bicycle unless such person is wearing protective headgear that conforms to the minimum specifications established for bicycle helmets

No child seventeen years of age or under shall operate a bicycle, electric bicycle, nonmotorized scooter, skateboard or electric scooter ... unless such child is wearing properly fitted and fastened protective headgear

license_registration_insurance.quote: "Motor vehicle" means any vehicle propelled or drawn by any nonmuscular power ... "Motor vehicle" does not include ... electric bicycles
license_registration_insurance.notes: No state license, registration or insurance, because e-bikes are excluded from 'motor vehicle'. But 14-289 lets a town, city or borough adopt ordinances 'requiring annual licensing of bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters', so local registration is possible.

where_allowed.quote: Except as provided in this section or where prohibited by local ordinance, an electric bicycle may be ridden where bicycles are permitted to travel.
where_allowed.roads: Where bicycles may travel, with bicycle rights and duties (14-289k(a), (b); 14-286a).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 allowed where bicycles are. Class 2 may not be ridden on a nonmotorized bicycle or multiuse trail with a natural surface tread and no added surfacing, unless a local ordinance permits (14-289k(d)). Local ordinances may prohibit e-bikes where bicycles are otherwise allowed (14-289k(b)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Allowed unless a city, town or borough ordinance or a State Traffic Administration regulation prohibits it. Riders must yield to pedestrians and give an audible signal before passing (14-286(a)).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Class 3 'shall not be ridden on a bicycle trail or path or multiuse trail or path' (14-289k(c)), with no local opt-in. Under 16 may not ride Class 3.

local_authority.quote: Each town, city and borough shall have authority to make any ordinance not inconsistent with section 14-286 or 14-288 ... respecting governing and controlling the use of bicycles, electric bicycles and electric scooters
local_authority.details: Local ordinances can prohibit e-bikes in places where bicycles may otherwise ride (14-289k(b)), regulate sidewalk riding (14-286(a)) and require annual e-bike licensing (14-289). The statutes do not expressly mention local age limits, so whether a town can set a minimum age for Class 1 or 2 is unclear.

non_ebike_devices.quote: a gasoline, electric or hybrid motor that has a capacity of less than fifty cubic centimeters piston displacement or a wattage not exceeding three thousand seven hundred watts
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motor-driven cycle (electric motor up to 3,700 W, seat height 26 inches or more) or motorcycle (above that)
non_ebike_devices.notes: A bike over 750 W, without operable pedals, or with a throttle that can exceed 20 mph is not an e-bike (14-1(31), 14-289n). Up to 3,700 W with a seat height of at least 26 inches it is a motor-driven cycle: 14-286(b) says 'no person shall ride a motor-driven cycle unless that person holds a valid motor vehicle operator's license', and it may not be ridden on sidewalks, limited access highways or turnpikes. 14-289g requires a DOT helmet for motorcycle and motor-driven cycle riders and passengers under 21 (raised from 18 by P.A. 25-65). Above 3,700 W it is a motorcycle (motor vehicle rules apply). Sellers must give a written 'This vehicle is not an electric bicycle' disclosure (14-289n(c)). Minimum license age and whether motor-driven cycles must be registered were not verified.

open_questions: Whether a town can set a minimum age for Class 1 or 2 e-bikes under its general 14-289 power (not stated in the statute).
The seat-height condition (26 inches or more) in the motor-driven cycle definition leaves a gap for electric devices with lower seats that are not e-bikes. Their classification is unclear.
Motor-driven cycle registration and insurance rules and the minimum operator license age were not verified.
14-1(60) excludes 'motor-driven cycles, as defined in section 14-286' from 'motor vehicle', but 14-286(e)(3) now points back to 14-1. How DMV applies registration to e-motos is unclear.
Resolved by verifier: P.A. 25-159 marks sec. 36 (14-289n) and sec. 37 (14-289k) 'Effective October 1, 2025', and the act was approved July 1, 2025.

verdict_cautions.reason: 14-289n says a vehicle with a throttle that can exceed 20 mph on motor power in any mode, or one built or sold to be switched out of the definition, is not an electric bicycle. It is likely a motor-driven cycle needing a driver's license.

CT.verifier_notes: Quotes match the 2026 Supplement and P.A. 26-24, which took effect Oct 1, 2026, and OLR lists no other 2026 e-bike change. Added a caution for bikes that 14-289n excludes (throttle above 20 mph or switchable out of class).

DC.name: District of Columbia

definition.quote: "Motorized bicycle" means a 2 or 3 wheeled vehicle with ... Fully operative pedals for human propulsion; and ... A motor incapable of propelling the device at a speed of more than 20 miles per hour
definition.motor_watts_basis: A motor incapable of propelling the device at a speed of more than 20 miles per hour
definition.notes: DC has no three-class e-bike law. E-bikes fall under 'motorized bicycle': a post-mounted seat for each rider, 2 or 3 wheels AT LEAST 16 INCHES in diameter, fully operative pedals, and a motor that cannot propel it above 20 mph. There is no wattage limit. Class 1 and 2 bikes that cut off at 20 mph fit. Class 3 does not fit cleanly. 18 DCMR 9901.1 says 'A motorized bicycle shall be a motor-driven cycle when operated by motor at speeds in excess of twenty miles per hour (20 mph) and the operator shall be required to have ... a valid driver's license.' Kids' e-bikes with wheels under 16 inches are not motorized bicycles.

label_required.notes: No e-bike class label requirement found in the DC Code definitions or 18 DCMR chapter 12. Absence not proven by a full-code search.

min_age.quote: No motorized bicycle shall be operated upon any public space in the District by any person who is less than sixteen (16) years old.
min_age.quote_note: The DCMR text is offered only as a download, so the verifier did not re-read it. DC DMV's Non-Traditional Motor Vehicle Chart (rev. Mar 24, 2021) says a motorized bicycle operator 'must be at least 16 years of age', citing 18 DCMR 1200.10, and DCRegs lists 18-1200 as unchanged since May 1, 2008.
min_age.exceptions: None stated. Applies to all motorized bicycles (Class 1 and 2 type e-bikes) on any public space. Effective date is the latest amendment to 1200 listed in the DCMR source note.

helmet.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person under 16 years of age to operate or to be a passenger on a bicycle ... unless that person wears a protective helmet
helmet.notes: 50-1609(1) defines 'bicycle' as a 'human-powered vehicle', so it is unclear whether this reaches motorized bicycles. Because 18 DCMR 1200.10 bars riders under 16 from motorized bicycles entirely, this helmet rule matters mainly for passengers. No helmet requirement for motorized bicycle riders 16 and older was found.

license_registration_insurance.quote: The term "motor vehicle" shall not include ... motorized bicycles, as the term is defined in § 50-2201.02(11A)
license_registration_insurance.notes: Motorized bicycles are excluded from 'motor vehicle' for operator permits (50-1401.01(f)), registration (50-1501.01(1)) and traffic definitions (50-2201.02(11)). Insurance is inferred from the same exclusion and was not checked against the insurance statute. A license IS required once a motorized bicycle is operated by motor above 20 mph (18 DCMR 9901.1).

where_allowed.quote: A person may ride a bicycle, motorized bicycle, or personal mobility device upon a sidewalk within the District ... provided, that no person shall ride ... upon a sidewalk within the Central Business District
where_allowed.roads: Allowed with bicycle duties (18 DCMR 1201.1, 1201.8).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: 'A motorized bicycle may be operated on any part of a roadway designated for the use of bicycles' (18 DCMR 1201.19).
where_allowed.paths_trails: 18 DCMR 9901.1 defines public bicycle paths and shared use paths as for 'bicycles, motorized bicycles, and pedestrians'. 1201.18 is repealed (Dec 9, 2022 rulemaking). National Park Service land in DC follows federal rules, not checked here.
where_allowed.sidewalks: Allowed outside the Central Business District unless a Mayor's order and signs prohibit it. Banned in the Central Business District except on designated sidewalks. Riders must yield to pedestrians and keep to the adjacent roadway's posted speed (1201.9, 1201.10).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: A Class 3 used by motor above 20 mph is treated as a motor-driven cycle and the rider needs a valid driver's license (18 DCMR 9901.1).

local_authority.details: DC is a single jurisdiction with no counties or cities below it. The Mayor can designate or prohibit sidewalk riding by order (18 DCMR 1201.9). Federal land (National Park Service, e.g. the National Mall and Rock Creek Park) has its own e-bike rules, which were not researched.

non_ebike_devices.quote: A motorized bicycle shall be a motorcycle when operated by motor at speeds in excess of thirty miles per hour (30 mph) and the operator shall be required to have on his or her possession a valid motorcycle endorsement.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motor-driven cycle (motor up to 50 cc or equivalent, 30 mph or less unassisted, automatic drive) or motorcycle (above 30 mph)
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device without pedals, with wheels under 16 inches, or with a motor that can exceed 20 mph is not a motorized bicycle. A motor-driven cycle is a 'motor vehicle' (driver's license and, presumably, registration and insurance). Above 30 mph it is a motorcycle needing a motorcycle endorsement. Wheels under 16 inches with no pedals may instead fit 'electric mobility device' (under 75 lb, standing or seated, 24 x 55 inches max), which has its own rules not captured here. Registration, insurance and helmet rules for motor-driven cycles were not verified.

open_questions: How DC enforces Class 3 e-bikes in practice. The text makes a Class 3 a motor-driven cycle (driver's license) whenever it is ridden by motor above 20 mph.
Whether the under-16 bicycle helmet law (D.C. Code 50-1605) applies to motorized bicycles, given 'bicycle' is defined as human-powered.

Resolved by verifier: none of D.C. Laws 26-1 to 26-195 or D.C. Acts 26-1 to 26-416 on code.dccouncil.gov changes motorized bicycle rules. Their bicycle mentions are budget, fee-schedule, streatery and plaza items. In DCMR, 18-1200 was last amended effective May 1, 2008 and 18-1201 on Dec 9, 2022, and the May 1, 2026 change to 18-9901 was the Intelligent Speed Assistance rulemaking.
D.C. Law 25-161 (STEER Act, 2024) amended 50-2201.02, but the Code notes that change 'has not been implemented' pending funding. It does not appear to affect e-bikes.
National Park Service rules on federal land in DC were not researched.
Absence of a label requirement was not confirmed by a full-code search.

verdict_cautions.reason: 18 DCMR 9901.1 makes a motorized bicycle a motor-driven cycle, needing a driver's license, when ridden by motor above 20 mph.
A 'motorized bicycle' needs every wheel to be at least 16 inches in diameter (50-2201.02(11A)). A smaller-wheel e-bike is a motor vehicle, most likely a motor-driven cycle needing a driver's license.

DC.verifier_notes: Code quotes match code.dccouncil.gov, and the under-16 ban is confirmed by DC DMV's chart and an unchanged 18 DCMR 1200. Added a caution for wheels under 16 inches, and no Council Period 26 law changes motorized bicycle rules.

DE.name: Delaware

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a bicycle with 2 or 3 wheels that is equipped with fully-operable pedals, a saddle or seat for the rider, and an electric motor of less than or equal to 750 watts
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than or equal to 750 watts
definition.notes: 750 W exactly qualifies ('less than or equal to'). Requires a seat or saddle and 2 or 3 wheels. Class 3 cutoff is 'no less than 20 ... and no more than 28 miles per hour'. 4198P(f) says the motor must disengage when the rider stops pedaling or the brakes are applied. 4198P(j) requires a speedometer on Class 3. Enacted by HB 19 (83 Del. Laws c. 505, approved Oct 26, 2022).

label_required.quote: manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each electric bicycle. The label shall contain the classification number, top assisted speed, and motor wattage

min_age.quote: No person under the age of 16 may operate a class 3 electric bicycle. A person under the age of 16 may ride as a passenger on a class 3 electric bicycle that is designed to accommodate passengers.
min_age.exceptions: Under-16 passengers allowed on a Class 3 designed for passengers. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2.

helmet.quote: All operators and passengers of class 3 electric bicycles must wear an approved, properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet.
A person under 18 years of age shall not operate or ride as a passenger upon any bicycle unless that person is wearing an approved, properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet.
helmet.notes: 4198K names bicycles, and 101(5) defines a bicycle as exclusively human-powered. It reaches Class 1 and 2 e-bikes only through 4198P(a), which gives e-bike riders 'all the duties' of a bicycle operator. Treat as required for safety. The fine falls on the parent or guardian (4198K(b)).

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric bicycle or a person operating an electric bicycle is not subject to the provisions of this Code relating to financial responsibility or insurance, driver’s licenses, registration, certificates of title, off-highway vehicles, and license plates.

where_allowed.quote: An electric bicycle may be ridden anywhere bicycles are allowed, including streets, highways, roadways, shoulders, bicycle lanes, bikeways ... and bicycle or multi-use paths except for all the following:
where_allowed.roads: Allowed where bicycles are allowed, with bicycle rights and duties (4198P(a), (g)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Allowed on bicycle and multi-use paths unless the local authority or state agency bans it after notice and a public hearing for safety or legal reasons (4198P(g)(1)). May be banned on designated nonmotorized natural-surface trails (4198P(g)(2)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Not allowed while using the electric motor, even on sidewalks open to bicycles (4198P(g)(3)).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: No path restriction specific to Class 3. Under 16 may not operate. Helmet at all ages. Speedometer required.

local_authority.quote: Local authorities, except as expressly authorized by law, shall not enact or enforce any rules or regulations contrary to this chapter.
local_authority.details: Local authorities may ban e-bikes on paths they control (after notice and a public hearing) and on nonmotorized natural-surface trails. The statute does not expressly authorize local age limits, and 4101(b) bars local rules contrary to the chapter, so a local minimum age for Class 1 or 2 looks doubtful but is not settled.

non_ebike_devices.citation: 21 Del. C. 101(40), (41) and 4198M, as amended by 85 Del. Laws c. 532 (HS 1 for HB 439)
non_ebike_devices.quote: an electric motor that produces less than 2,000 watts that may be used exclusively to propel the vehicle at a speed of more than 20 miles per hour
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (2 wheels, electric under 2,000 W, throttle over 20 mph or assist over 28 mph), triped (3 wheels, 751 to 2,000 W), otherwise motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A moped or triped needs a motor vehicle operator license but no motorcycle endorsement (4198M(b)), must be registered with a plate (4198M(d), (f)), needs no motor vehicle insurance (4198M(h)), and riders under 18 must wear a helmet (4198M(i)). From Sep 24, 2026 mopeds may not be ridden on any bike lane, sidewalk or pathway closed to motor vehicle traffic, and the OHV definition now includes mopeds. Sellers may not call e-mopeds or e-motorcycles e-bikes and must give a written disclosure (new 21 Del. C. 8701). A device of 2,000 W or more is a motorcycle. Gap: a bike over 750 W that cannot exceed 20 mph on throttle or 28 mph with assist is neither an e-bike nor a moped by the text, so it falls to the general 'motorcycle' definition. Minimum license age not verified.

pending_changes.bill: HS 1 for HB 439 (153rd GA), Truth in E-Bike Marketing Act, 85 Del. Laws c. 532
pending_changes.summary: Already in effect. Redefines moped as a motor vehicle with an electric motor under 2,000 W, bars mopeds from bike lanes, sidewalks and pathways closed to motor vehicles, bans selling e-mopeds and e-motorcycles as e-bikes or with class labels, and requires written seller disclosures.

open_questions: Does the under-18 bicycle helmet rule (4198K) apply to Class 1 and 2 e-bikes? Only through 4198P(a), since 'bicycle' is defined as human-powered.
Can a municipality set a minimum age for Class 1 or 2? Not expressly authorized, and 4101(b) preempts contrary local rules.
delcode.delaware.gov may not yet show the Sep 24, 2026 amendments to 101(40) and 4198M. The amended text was read from the enrolled bill page, not the code site.
4198M(h) says no insurance is required for mopeds, while the new seller disclosure says these vehicles are subject to insurance requirements. The engine should follow 4198M(h) but flag it.
Classification of a bike over 750 W that cannot exceed 20 mph (throttle) or 28 mph (assist) is unclear.

verdict_cautions.reason: Since Sep 24, 2026 a vehicle whose electric motor alone can propel it above 20 mph is a 'moped' (101(40)), which needs a driver's license, a plate and a helmet under 18, and may not use bike lanes, sidewalks or paths.

DE.verifier_notes: All quotes match delcode and the enrolled HS 1 for HB 439 (85 Del. Laws c. 532, signed and effective Sep 24, 2026). Added a caution that a bike whose throttle exceeds 20 mph is now a moped.

FL.name: Florida

definition.quote: A bicycle or tricycle equipped with fully operable pedals, a seat or saddle for the use of the rider, and an electric motor of less than 750 watts which meets the requirements of one of the following three classifications:
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than 750 watts
definition.notes: Motor must be LESS THAN 750 W. Definition also requires a seat or saddle. 316.20655(6) adds that the motor must disengage 'when the rider stops pedaling or when the brakes are applied' for every e-bike, which sits awkwardly with the Class 2 throttle class. No Class 3 speedometer requirement found.

label_required.quote: Beginning January 1, 2021, manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed in a prominent location to each electric bicycle. The label must contain the classification number, top assisted speed, and motor wattage

helmet.citation: Fla. Stat. 316.2065(3)(d), applied to e-bikes by 316.20655(1)
helmet.quote: A bicycle rider or passenger who is under 16 years of age must wear a bicycle helmet that is properly fitted and is fastened securely upon the passenger’s head by a strap

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric bicycle or an operator of an electric bicycle is not subject to the provisions of law relating to financial responsibility, driver or motor vehicle licenses, vehicle registration, title certificates, off-highway motorcycles, or off-highway vehicles.

where_allowed.quote: An operator may ride an electric bicycle where bicycles are allowed, including, but not limited to, streets, highways, roadways, shoulders, bicycle lanes, and bicycle or multiuse paths.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed where bicycles are allowed, with bicycle rights and duties (316.20655(1), (7)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Allowed on bicycle and multiuse paths, but a municipality, county or state agency with jurisdiction may restrict or prohibit e-bikes on a path, trail network, beach or dune (316.20655(1)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Unclear default. E-bikes have bicycle rights, and 316.2065(10) sets duties for people riding bicycles on sidewalks. 316.008(7)(a) lets a county or municipality 'permit, control, or regulate' e-bikes on sidewalks, with a 15 mph cap in such an ordinance. Check local ordinances.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: No state Class 3 restriction found. Same rules as Class 1 and 2.

local_authority.quote: A local government may adopt an ordinance providing one or more minimum age requirements to operate an electric bicycle and may adopt an ordinance requiring an operator of an electric bicycle to possess a government-issued photographic identification
local_authority.details: Added by ch. 2025-149 (CS/SB 462, approved Jun 19, 2025, effective Jul 1, 2025). Local governments may set minimum ages and require photo ID, regulate e-bikes on streets, highways and sidewalks under 316.008, and ban or restrict e-bikes on paths, trail networks, beaches and dunes (316.20655(1)). Florida has no statewide minimum age, so the engine must check the city or county.

non_ebike_devices.quote: MOPED.—Any vehicle with pedals to permit propulsion by human power ... with a motor rated not in excess of 2 brake horsepower and not capable of propelling the vehicle at a speed greater than 30 miles per hour
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (pedals, 2 bhp or less, 30 mph or less), motorized scooter (any seat, 3 or fewer wheels, cannot exceed 20 mph), or motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A pedal bike with 750 W or more, up to 2 bhp and 30 mph, is a moped. 316.211(4) requires a DOT helmet for moped riders under 16. A motor-powered device on three or fewer wheels that cannot exceed 20 mph is a 'motorized scooter' (pedals not required), and 316.2128(2)-(3) exempt it from registration, insurance and driver licensing, with local age limits allowed (316.2128(7)). Anything faster without pedals is a motorcycle, and 322.03(5) says 'A person may not operate a motorcycle unless he or she holds a driver license that authorizes such operation'. license_needed is null because the answer depends on which category the device falls in. Moped license class, minimum age and registration were not verified.

open_questions: SB 382 (2026) would have added a 10 mph speed rule near pedestrians and a micromobility task force. The Florida Senate bill page shows 'Vetoed by Governor' (news reports the veto as Jun 25 or Jun 30, 2026). Nothing from it is law.
Default sidewalk rule for e-bikes (allowed like bicycles unless a local ordinance says otherwise, or only where an ordinance permits) is ambiguous in the text.
Moped driver license class, minimum age and registration requirements were not verified.
Many Florida cities and counties adopted local age limits after Jul 1, 2025. None are captured here.
FL.verifier_notes: All quotes found in the 2026 Florida Statutes. No 2026 e-bike law (SB 382 vetoed). No corrections.

GA.name: Georgia

definition.quote: "Electric assisted bicycle" means a device with two or three wheels which has a saddle and fully operative pedals for human propulsion and also has an electric motor having a power output of not more than 750 watts.
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor having a power output of not more than 750 watts
definition.notes: Two or three wheels, a saddle and fully operative pedals are required. § 40-6-300: Class I assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph. Class II 'may be used exclusively to propel the vehicle but is not capable of reaching a speed of 20 miles per hour' (literally under 20 mph). Class III assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph. § 40-6-302(c): the motor must disengage when the rider stops pedaling or brakes. § 40-6-302(d): Class III must have a speedometer in mph. E-bikes are excluded from 'motor vehicle' (§ 40-1-1(33)). § 40-6-301: e-bike riders have the rights and duties of bicycle riders. Text read from FindLaw's copy of the O.C.G.A. (current as of March 28, 2024), cross-checked against the enrolled HB 454 (2019). The official free O.C.G.A. is hosted on LexisNexis and could not be read by machine.

label_required.quote: Any electric assisted bicycle manufactured on and after January 1, 2020, shall be equipped with a permanently affixed label in a prominent location which identifies such device as a class I, II, or III electric assisted bicycle
label_required.notes: Applies to bikes manufactured on or after Jan 1, 2020. The duty falls on manufacturers, distributors and anyone who alters the bike so its class changes (§ 40-6-302(b)). A pre-2020 bike with no label is not automatically illegal.

min_age.quote: No person under the age of 15 shall operate a class III electric assisted bicycle; provided, however, that such person shall be authorized to ride as a passenger upon a class III electric assisted bicycle designed to accommodate passengers.
min_age.exceptions: Under-15 riders may be passengers on a Class III bike designed for passengers. No statewide minimum age for Class I or II: HB 454 (2019) removed e-bikes from the age-15 rule in § 40-6-351, which now covers mopeds only.

helmet.quote: No person shall operate or be a passenger on a class III electric assisted bicycle without wearing a bicycle helmet.

helmet.citation: O.C.G.A. § 40-6-296(d)(1) (bicycle helmet rule), applied to e-bikes through § 40-6-301
helmet.quote: No person under the age of 16 years shall operate or be a passenger on a bicycle on a highway, bicycle path, bicycle lane, or sidewalk under the jurisdiction or control of this state
helmet.notes: This rule is written for 'bicycles'. It reaches e-bikes because § 40-6-301 gives e-bike riders all the duties of bicycle riders. Under § 40-6-296(d)(6), riders under 16 who break it are not fined.

license_registration_insurance.citation: O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(33) (e-bike excluded from 'motor vehicle'); § 40-6-371(a)(7) (local bicycle registration)
license_registration_insurance.quote: "Motor vehicle" means every vehicle which is self-propelled other than a personal delivery device, an electric assisted bicycle, or an electric personal assistive mobility device (EPAMD).
license_registration_insurance.notes: No state license, registration or insurance, because the driver's license, registration and insurance rules apply to 'motor vehicles' and e-bikes are excluded from that term. This is an inference from the definition. The explicit sentence 'No license or permit shall be required for the operation of an electric assisted bicycle' is not in the current § 40-6-351. Caution: § 40-6-371(a)(7) lets local authorities require 'registration and inspection of bicycles, including the requirement of a registration fee'. A city could require registration.

where_allowed.quote: No class III electric assisted bicycle shall be operated on a bicycle path or shared use path unless such path is within or adjacent to a highway or unless operation of such device is permitted on such path
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. Riders have the same rights and duties as bicycle riders (§ 40-6-301) and ride as far right as practicable (§ 40-6-294).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Allowed. § 40-1-1(6.1) defines a bicycle lane as being for 'bicycles and electric assisted bicycles'.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class I and II may use any bicycle path or shared use path where bicycles are allowed, unless a local authority or state agency bans them (§ 40-6-303(a)(1)). Class III only if the path is within or next to a highway, or the managing authority permits it (§ 40-6-303(a)(2)). Natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized are outside these rules. Their managers decide which devices may use them (§ 40-6-303(a)(3)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Generally prohibited. § 40-6-144: no person shall drive any vehicle upon a sidewalk, except where a local ordinance allows bicycles on sidewalks for riders 12 or younger. Whether that local exception covers e-bikes is not stated.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Minimum age 15 (passengers excepted), helmet for every rider and passenger, speedometer required, and kept off paths unless they are next to a highway or the managing authority allows them.

local_authority.quote: provided, however, that a local authority or state agency may prohibit the operation of a class I electric assisted bicycle or class II electric assisted bicycle on any bicycle path or shared use path within its jurisdiction.
local_authority.details: Local authorities and state agencies can ban Class I and II from paths under their control and can open paths to Class III. They regulate natural-surface nonmotorized trails, can allow bicycles on sidewalks for riders 12 or under (§ 40-6-144), and can require bicycle registration and inspection (§ 40-6-371(a)(7)). No statute expressly lets them set e-bike age limits.

non_ebike_devices.quote: No person shall operate a moped upon the highways in this state unless he or she has in his or her possession a valid driver's license, instruction permit, or limited permit
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (if power is 2 brake horsepower or less and top speed 30 mph or less), otherwise motor driven cycle or motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: Age rule, same section: 'No person under 15 years of age shall operate a moped upon the highways in this state.' A device over 750 W, or with no operable pedals, is not an 'electric assisted bicycle' and becomes a self-propelled 'motor vehicle'. § 40-1-1(28) defines a moped as a motor driven cycle 'with or without foot pedals' with up to 2 brake horsepower (about 1,491 W) that cannot exceed 30 mph unassisted. Moped riders need a driver's license or permit (any class), must be at least 15 and must wear a DPS-approved helmet (§ 40-6-352). Faster or more powerful devices are motorcycles needing a motorcycle license and registration. Mopeds are exempt from registration (40-2-20(b)). Moped insurance was not verified.

open_questions: Resolved by verifier: all 1,056 bills on the governor's 2024, 2025 and 2026 signed-legislation pages were text-searched. None contains 'electric assisted bicycle' or amends 40-6-300 to 40-6-303, 40-6-296, 40-6-351 or 40-6-144, and the 40-1-1 changes in those years (SB 448 of 2024, SB 58 of 2025, HB 1268 of 2026) do not touch paragraphs (15.3) or (33). FindLaw's March 2024 text is therefore still current. The Lexis-hosted official code was not opened, and bills that became law without a signature were not checked.
Can a local ordinance that allows children 12 and under to ride bicycles on sidewalks (§ 40-6-144) also cover e-bikes? The statute does not say.

Partly resolved by verifier: mopeds are exempt from registration under 40-2-20(b) ('To any moped'), an exemption SB 384 (2026) keeps when it renumbers the list from July 1, 2027. Moped insurance was not verified.

The Class II definition says 'not capable of reaching a speed of 20 miles per hour'. Verifier's reading: the base definition in 40-1-1(15.3) has no class or speed test, so a 20 mph throttle bike is still an 'electric assisted bicycle', excluded from 'motor vehicle' (40-1-1(33)), even if it misses the literal Class II wording. No rule restricts Class II beyond Class I, so a Class 2 label can stay legal.

Verifier checked the signed HB 454 text. It has no effective-date section (its last section only repeals conflicting laws), so Georgia's default July 1 rule (O.C.G.A. 1-3-4) gives July 1, 2019. 1-3-4 itself was not re-read.
GA.verifier_notes: Quotes match FindLaw (current to Mar 28, 2024) and the signed HB 454, and none of the 1,056 bills signed in 2024 to 2026 touches the e-bike sections. The Class II wording does not take a Class 2 bike out of the base definition.

HI.name: Hawaii

definition.citation: HRS § 291C-1 (definitions 'electric bicycle', 'class 1/2/3 electric bicycle', 'high-speed electric device'), as amended by Act 259 (2026), HB 2021 CD1, Section 9
definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a bicycle equipped with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than seven hundred fifty watts. "Electric bicycle" does not include a high-speed electric device.
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of no more than seven hundred fifty watts
definition.notes: Act 259 (2026) took effect when the governor approved it on July 15, 2026. It replaced the old 'low-speed electric bicycle' (which cross-referenced 15 U.S.C. 2085) with the three classes. Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph. Class 2 may be throttle-only and gives no assistance at 20 mph. Class 3 assists only while pedaling, stops at 28 mph and must have a speedometer (it is part of the Class 3 definition). An electric bicycle is a 'bicycle' under § 291C-1, so bicycle rules apply. New safe-riding rules: all wheels on the ground, seated facing forward, and no wheelies or stunts on public ways. Read from the enrolled CD1 text, which Act 259 enacted. The HRS 'current' pages may not show Act 259 yet.

label_required.citation: Act 259 (2026), HB 2021 CD1, Section 2 (new HRS § 291C- in part XIII); effective date in Section 22
label_required.quote: Manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each electric bicycle. The label shall contain the electric bicycle's: (1) Classification number (class 1, 2, or 3)
label_required.notes: Section 22 says section 2 takes effect 120 days after the Act's effective date (about Nov 12, 2026), or earlier if DOT adopts rules. As of Oct 16, 2026 it may not be in force yet. The section also says 'No person shall alter, deface, or remove a label' and requires point-of-sale signs and seller disclosures. Separately, § 249-15(b)-(c) as amended lets police seize 'nonconforming' e-bikes, meaning ones that fail classification, labeling, equipment or operational rules.

min_age.citation: HRS § 291C-143.5, as amended by Act 259 (2026), Section 12
min_age.quote: No person under the age of sixteen shall operate a class 2 or class 3 electric bicycle unless under the direct supervision of a parent or guardian.
min_age.exceptions: Allowed under 16 with 'direct supervision': a supervising parent, guardian or person 18 or older who is physically present and close enough to observe and control the operation (§ 291C-143.5(b)). Class 1 has no state minimum age (the old under-15 ban on all low-speed e-bikes was replaced).

min_age.citation: HRS § 291C-143.5, as amended by Act 259 (2026), Section 12
min_age.quote: No person under the age of sixteen shall operate a class 2 or class 3 electric bicycle unless under the direct supervision of a parent or guardian.
min_age.exceptions: Same supervision exception as Class 2. A parent, guardian or person 18 or older must be physically present and in reasonable proximity.

helmet.citation: HRS § 291C-150(a), as amended by Act 259 (2026), Section 14 (e-bikes are 'bicycles' under § 291C-1)
helmet.quote: No person under eighteen years of age shall operate a bicycle upon a street, a bikeway, or any other public property unless that person is wearing a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet
helmet.notes: Act 259 raised the age from under 16 to under 18. It also covers child passengers in bike seats and trailers, and rentals.

license_registration_insurance.citation: HRS § 249-14(b), as amended by Act 259 (2026), Section 5; insurance exemption in new HRS § 291C- (Act 259, Section 1)
license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric bicycle shall be required to be registered, and shall be subject to a permanent registration fee of $30, to be paid by the owners thereof to the director of finance.
license_registration_insurance.notes: REGISTRATION REQUIRED. The amended § 249-14(b) adds 'No person shall operate an electric bicycle on a public roadway, sidewalk, or bicycle facility unless it has been properly registered'. Unregistered bikes can be cited or temporarily impounded. Insurance: 'Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to require insurance for the operation of a road-legal, permitted, and classified electric bicycle.' No statute was found requiring a driver's license for an e-bike, since e-bikes are bicycles, not 'motor vehicles' in a licensing category of § 286-102.

where_allowed.citation: HRS § 291C-145(g) as amended by Act 259, Section 13; § 291C-123(a) as amended by Act 259, Section 10
where_allowed.quote: a person may ride a class 1 electric bicycle, class 2 electric bicycle, or class 3 electric bicycle on a sidewalk at a speed not exceeding ten miles per hour, except in business districts or where prohibited by county ordinance
where_allowed.roads: Allowed as a bicycle, but the bike must be registered first (§ 249-14(b)).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Allowed. § 291C-123(a) lets bicycles use bicycle lanes and paths. Counties may post lanes and paths to bar 'persons riding a bicycle equipped with a motor' (§ 291C-145(g)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Bicycle paths are allowed under § 291C-123 unless a county posts them closed to motorized bicycles (§ 291C-145(g)). No state rule on natural-surface trails was found. State and county park rules may apply.
where_allowed.sidewalks: All three classes allowed at 10 mph or less, except in business districts or where a county ordinance prohibits it. Counties may add reasonable restrictions (§ 291C-145(g)).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: No path ban for Class 3 specifically. Class 3 must have a speedometer, and riders under 16 need direct supervision.

local_authority.citation: HRS § 291C-145(g) as amended by Act 259 (2026), Section 13; Act 259 Section 1 (safe riding rules)
local_authority.quote: The counties may, by ordinance, post bicycle lanes and bicycle paths to prevent persons riding a bicycle equipped with a motor from using them.
local_authority.details: Counties can ban or restrict e-bikes on sidewalks and post bicycle lanes and paths closed to motorized bicycles. DOT and each county may adopt rules defining more unsafe or reckless riding behaviors. No express power for county e-bike age limits was found. Separately, HIDOE has 2025 rules for e-bikes on school campuses, which were not reviewed.

non_ebike_devices.citation: HRS § 291C-1 ('high-speed electric device') and new § 291C- (operating a high-speed electric device), Act 259 (2026), Sections 1 and 9; HRS § 286-2 (moped); § 286-102(b)(1) (moped license)
non_ebike_devices.quote: No person shall operate a high-speed electric device on a public roadway, a bicycle lane, a travel path, a bicycle facility, or other public area, such as a street, highway, or sidewalk.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: high-speed electric device (banned from all public ways) if the motor is over 750 W and it can exceed 28 mph; otherwise possibly a moped (2 hp / 1,492 W or less, 30 mph or less) needing a driver's license and moped registration
non_ebike_devices.notes: 'High-speed electric device' means a device with a motor over 750 W and capable of more than 28 mph, unless registered as a moped or motor vehicle. Such devices may not be ridden anywhere public, and police may seize them (§ 249-15(b)). A device that fails only one test (over 750 W but 28 mph or less, or no pedals) is neither an e-bike nor a high-speed device. It may be a moped under § 286-2, which needs a moped-category license (§ 286-102(b)(1)). Mopeds are now barred from bike lanes and paths. A new 'electric motorcycle' category (over 28 mph, road-registered) is also barred from bike facilities.
