Since Act 222 (SLH 2025, effective June 25, 2025), no one under 16 may drive a moped on any public way, and every moped driver must wear a helmet (HRS 291C-195(a)). min_age 16 applies to mopeds.

pending_changes.bill: HB 2021 (2026), Act 259, Section 2 (labels, point-of-sale signs, seller disclosures)
pending_changes.summary: Manufacturers and distributors must put a permanent class, top-speed and wattage label on each e-bike. Sellers must post signs and say in writing whether a bike is street legal. DOT may fine up to $500 per violation. Takes effect 120 days after July 15, 2026, or earlier if DOT adopts rules.

open_questions: Read from the enrolled HB 2021 CD1 text (Act 259). The governor's message GM1362 and the final printed Act were not read separately. The status page shows 'Act 259, on 07/15/2026' with no veto or line-item note.
Has DOT adopted the Chapter 91 rules that would start the label rule before Nov 12, 2026? Not checked.

Registration: an e-bike bought before the Act may already carry the $30 permanent registration (registration was required under the old 'low-speed electric bicycle' wording). Each county DMV handles it, and the logistics were not checked.

Resolved by verifier: Act 222 (SLH 2025, SB 30, effective June 25, 2025) amended HRS 291C-195(a) so that no one under 16 may drive a moped on public property and every moped driver must wear a helmet.
Is a device over 750 W but at most 28 mph, or a pedal-less device, a moped or simply unregulated? The Act leaves a gap. The app should treat such devices as not legal e-bikes.
Other 2025 bills (SB 98, SB 745) were proposals. Act 259 superseded them in 2026.
HI.verifier_notes: Act 259 (signed Jul 15, 2026) is confirmed, including mandatory registration and helmets under 18. Added the 2025 moped rule (no drivers under 16, helmets at all ages) for over-limit devices.

IA.name: Iowa

definition.citation: Iowa Code § 321.1(36A), as amended by 2026 Iowa Acts ch. 1053 (SF 490); § 321.1(40)(c) (bicycle)
definition.quote: and an electric motor that produces not more than seven hundred fifty watts
definition.quote_note: The quote is the amended wording as enacted. It appears in the enrolled SF 490 and 2026 Iowa Acts ch. 1053 only once the struck words 'of less than' are dropped (the PDF text layer shows 'motor of less than that produces not more than seven hundred fifty watts', with 'of less than' struck through). Iowa Code 2027, which will print the clean text, is not yet published.
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor that produces not more than seven hundred fifty watts
definition.notes: A low-speed e-bike needs a saddle or seat, two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and a motor of 750 W or less. SF 490 (signed April 30, 2026, Acts ch. 1053, effective July 1, 2026) changed the limit from 'less than' 750 W to 'not more than' 750 W, so exactly 750 W is now inside. The quote is the post-amendment wording. The enrolled PDF and 2026 Iowa Acts ch. 1053 do mark the change when rendered: 'of less than' is struck through and 'that produces not more than' is underlined (text extraction drops this formatting). The new lead-in ends 'and is classified in accordance with the following requirements:', and the three class paragraphs are unchanged. The amended Iowa Code text (Code 2027) was not yet published. Classes (Iowa Code 2026 § 321.1(36A)(a)-(c)): Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph. Class 2 may propel the bike alone and gives no assistance at 20 mph. Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph. A low-speed e-bike is a 'bicycle' (§ 321.1(40)(c)) and is excluded from 'vehicle' (§ 321.1(90)), 'motorcycle' and 'motorized bicycle'. § 321.235B: must meet 16 C.F.R. pt. 1512, assist must cut off when the rider stops pedaling or brakes, and Class 3 needs an mph speedometer.

label_required.quote: A manufacturer or distributor of low-speed electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed in a prominent location to each of the manufacturer's or distributor's low-speed electric bicycles.
label_required.notes: The label shows the class number, top assisted speed and motor wattage in 9-point Arial or larger. § 321.235B(2): no one may knowingly modify a bike so it no longer fits a class, and anyone who modifies speed or engagement must attach a new label.

min_age.quote: A person under the age of sixteen shall not operate a class 3 low-speed electric bicycle. A person under the age of sixteen may ride as a passenger on a class 3 low-speed electric bicycle
min_age.exceptions: Under 16 may ride as a passenger if the bike is designed for that many riders. No statewide minimum for Class 1 or 2.

license_registration_insurance.quote: low-speed electric bicycles are not subject to provisions of the Code applicable to vehicles, including provisions relating to all of the following: a. Licensure, registration, titling, inspection, and proof of financial liability coverage. b. Possession of a driver's license
license_registration_insurance.notes: No state license, registration, title, inspection or insurance. Caution: § 321.236(10) lets local authorities regulate 'the operation of bicycles and requiring the registration and licensing of the same, including the requirement of a registration fee'. Low-speed e-bikes are 'bicycles' under § 321.1(40)(c), so a city could require local registration. No statewide helmet law was found.

where_allowed.quote: A low-speed electric bicycle may be operated in any place where a bicycle is allowed to operate, including but not limited to streets, highways, roadways, shoulders, bicycle lanes, bikeways, and bicycle or multi-use paths.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed on streets, highways, roadways and shoulders. Riders have the rights and duties of bicycle riders (§ 321.235B(7)).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Allowed. Class 3 may not exceed the posted or applicable limit, or 20 mph where none is posted (§ 321.235B(9)(b)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Allowed on bikeways and bicycle or multi-use paths wherever bicycles are allowed. Same Class 3 speed cap (20 mph unless posted). No state natural-surface trail carve-out was found. DNR, county conservation and city park rules were not reviewed.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No statewide e-bike sidewalk ban found. Allowed where bicycles are allowed. Cities regulate bicycle use, including sidewalks, under § 321.236(10). Local rules apply.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Minimum age 16 (passengers excepted), mph speedometer required, and 20 mph cap (or posted limit) on bike lanes and multi-use paths.

local_authority.quote: Regulating the operation of bicycles and requiring the registration and licensing of the same, including the requirement of a registration fee. However, the regulations shall not conflict with the provisions of section 321.234.
local_authority.details: Local authorities may regulate bicycle operation and require bicycle registration and licensing with a fee. Because low-speed e-bikes are 'bicycles', this appears to reach e-bikes. How far a city may restrict e-bikes from places § 321.235B(9) opens to them is not settled in the statute. No express power for local e-bike age limits was found.

non_ebike_devices.quote: The department may issue a driver's license valid only for operation of a motorized bicycle to a person fourteen years of age or older
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorized bicycle (39 mph or less) or motorcycle, a motor vehicle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device over 750 W, or one without operable pedals or a seat, is not a low-speed e-bike and is a motor vehicle. SF 490's explanation says motor-vehicle, motorcycle and motorized-bicycle rules then apply. A 'motorized bicycle' (§ 321.1(40)(b)) has a seat, up to three wheels and cannot exceed 39 mph unassisted. It needs a motorized-bicycle license (age 14+, with an education course if under 16) or any class of driver's license, plus registration ($7/year fee in ch. 321). It may not carry a passenger (§ 321.275). Faster devices are motorcycles needing a motorcycle license. Insurance requirements were not verified.

open_questions: Resolved by verifier (Oct 16, 2026): the enrolled SF 490 and 2026 Iowa Acts ch. 1053 (approved April 30, 2026) were rendered as page images. 'of less than' is struck and 'that produces not more than' is added, so the codified text will read 'not more than seven hundred fifty watts'. The legislature's provisional list of sections amended in the 2025 and 2026 sessions shows no other change to § 321.1(36A), § 321.1(40), § 321.235B or § 321.236. Iowa Code 2027 is not yet published.
Can cities ban e-bikes from sidewalks or paths, or set age limits, under § 321.236(10)? Probably yes for sidewalks, but not tested against § 321.235B(9).

No statewide helmet or Class 1/2 age rule was found in the Iowa Code 2026 or in 2026 session bill titles. The legislature's 'all bills' list for GA 91 shows only SF 490 (and its companions) on e-bikes.
Insurance requirements for a motorized bicycle (the over-limit category) were not verified.

§ 321.235B(4) requires every low-speed e-bike to be built so that the motor assist stops 'when the rider stops pedaling, applies the brakes, or the electric motor is disengaged'. Read literally, this conflicts with a Class 2 throttle. Class 2 is kept legal here, as in the other states with this clause, but no source settles it.
IA.verifier_notes: The 'not more than 750 W' change was confirmed in the rendered SF 490 enrolled text and 2026 Iowa Acts ch. 1053 (approved Apr 30, 2026, effective Jul 1, 2026), and every other quote matches its source. No verdict change, only a quote note and three wording fixes, including a new open question on the stop-pedaling clause for Class 2.

ID.name: Idaho

definition.quote: "Electric-assisted bicycle" means a bicycle equipped with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty (750) watts and that meets one (1) of the following requirements:
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty (750) watts
definition.notes: WATT LIMIT IS STRICT: the motor must be 'less than' 750 W, so a motor labeled exactly 750 W falls outside the literal definition. Class 1 assists only while pedaling and cuts off when pedaling stops or at 20 mph. Class 2 may propel the bike alone and gives no assistance at 20 mph. Class 3 assists only while pedaling and cuts off at 28 mph. There is no speedometer requirement for Class 3. The base 'bicycle' definition is in Idaho Code § 49-102. E-bikes are excluded from 'moped', 'motorcycle', 'motor-driven cycle' and 'motorbike' (§ 49-114). Text read on the Idaho Legislature statutes site, which is updated each July 1 after the session. Section history shows the definition was last amended in 2019 (ch. 84). HB 76 (2019) effective date assumed July 1, 2019, Idaho's default.

label_required.quote: On and after September 1, 2019, manufacturers or distributors of electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each electric bicycle. The label shall contain the classification number, top assisted speed
label_required.notes: This duty falls on manufacturers and distributors. It is not an operating requirement for the rider.

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric-assisted bicycle and any person operating an electric-assisted bicycle are not subject to the provisions of this title relating to financial responsibility, driver's licenses, titles, registration, and license plate requirements.
license_registration_insurance.notes: No license, title, registration, plate or insurance is required. The section says an e-bike 'shall be considered a motor vehicle to the extent required by 23 U.S.C. 154' (the federal open-container rule).

where_allowed.quote: Electric-assisted bicycles may be used in places where bicycles are permitted to travel including but not limited to multiuse paths, unless excluded by local ordinance or by signage posted by the public agency with jurisdiction
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. E-bike riders have the rights and duties of bicycle riders (§ 49-725) and of vehicle drivers under chapters 6 and 8 (§ 49-714, as amended 2026). The 'Idaho stop' rules of § 49-720 apply to e-bikes at stop signs. The red-light yield rule in § 49-720(2) names only bicycles and human-powered vehicles, not e-bikes.
where_allowed.paths_trails: All classes, including Class 3, may use multiuse paths and other places bicycles may go, unless excluded by local ordinance or by signs posted by the agency with jurisdiction after public notice on a governing board agenda (§ 49-728). Highway-district side paths are also open to e-bikes unless locally prohibited (§ 40-616).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Allowed where bicycles are allowed. Riders must yield to pedestrians and give an audible signal before passing (§ 49-721(1)), and may not ride where traffic control devices prohibit bicycles (§ 49-721(2)). Local ordinances can exclude e-bikes (§ 49-725).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: No Class 3-specific state restrictions (no age, helmet, speedometer or path limits).

local_authority.quote: electric-assisted bicycles may be ridden where bicycles are permitted to travel, unless excluded by local ordinance or by signage posted by the public agency with jurisdiction after notice by inclusion on a governing board agenda.
local_authority.details: Local ordinances, and signs posted by the public agency with jurisdiction after public agenda notice, can exclude e-bikes from places bicycles may go. No express state power for local e-bike age limits was found, and none was checked city by city.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Moped" means a limited-speed motor-driven cycle having wheels less than twenty (20) inches in diameter and:
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (wheels under 20 in., 30 mph or less), or motor-driven cycle or motorcycle, or an off-highway motorbike that is not street legal
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device at or over 750 W, or with no operable pedals, is not an electric-assisted bicycle. It becomes a motor vehicle, and § 49-301 says no person 'shall drive any motor vehicle upon a highway unless the person has a current and valid Idaho driver's license'. A moped (under 20 in. wheels, 30 mph or less; electric mopeds without pedals need under 2 gross bhp and FMVSS compliance) needs no title or motorcycle endorsement. A motor-driven cycle (5 bhp or less, FMVSS-compliant) needs a title and a motorcycle endorsement. Most over-limit e-bikes have 20 in. or larger wheels and no FMVSS certification, so they fit no street-legal category. Moped registration, insurance and minimum license age were not verified.

open_questions: The 'less than 750 watts' wording excludes a motor rated exactly 750 W. Does Idaho enforce it that literally? Unknown. The app should flag a 750 W label in Idaho rather than call it legal.

HB 500 (2026, Session Law ch. 24, effective July 1, 2026) amended § 49-714 so e-bike riders have the duties of vehicle drivers and must use due care. This followed a Boise case. It is already in the current statute text.

Resolved by verifier: H 880 (2026) did not pass. On March 17, 2026 it was taken off General Orders and referred back to House Transportation & Defense, with no later action. The official 2025 and 2026 session bill lists show no other e-bike bill besides H 500 (2026 ch. 24).
No statewide minimum age or helmet rule exists for any class. City ordinances (e.g. Boise, Coeur d'Alene) were not checked.
Moped registration and insurance rules, and the license age for an over-limit device, were not verified.
ID.verifier_notes: The definition ('less than 750 watts'), label, license exemption and path rules match the official Idaho Code pages, and H 500 (2026 ch. 24) is already in the text. H 880 died in committee and no other 2025 or 2026 e-bike act exists, so the only fix is one resolved open question.

IL.name: Illinois

definition.citation: 625 ILCS 5/1-140.10; 625 ILCS 5/1-106 (bicycle, as amended by P.A. 104-141)
definition.quote: Low-speed electric bicycle. A bicycle equipped with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts that meets the requirements of one of the following classes:
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than 750 watts
definition.notes: WATT LIMIT IS STRICT: 'less than 750 watts', so exactly 750 W is outside the literal definition. Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph. Class 2 may propel the bike alone and gives no assistance at 20 mph. Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph. A low-speed e-bike 'is not a moped or a motor driven cycle' and is excluded from 'motor vehicle' (§ 1-146). Since P.A. 104-141 (eff. Jan 1, 2026), 'bicycle' (§ 1-106) covers low-speed e-bikes 'with 2 or more wheels not less than 12 inches in diameter, operable pedals, and designated seats'. § 11-1517(b): must meet CPSC 16 CFR 1512, and Class 3 needs an mph speedometer. § 11-1517(d): Class 2 motor cuts off when the brakes are applied, and Class 1 and 3 motors cut off when pedaling stops. From Jan 1, 2027 (P.A. 104-854), any electric bicycle that is not a low-speed e-bike 'shall be considered a motor driven cycle'. Text read on ilga.gov, which shows both the pre- and post-2027 versions.

label_required.quote: Beginning on or after January 1, 2018, every manufacturer and distributor of low-speed electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed to the bicycle in a prominent location.
label_required.notes: The label must show the class number, top assisted speed and motor wattage in 9-point Arial or larger. 'No person shall knowingly tamper or modify the speed capability or engagement of a low-speed electric bicycle without replacing the label'.

min_age.quote: A person may operate a Class 3 low-speed electric bicycle only if he or she is 16 years of age or older. A person who is less than 16 years of age may ride as a passenger
min_age.exceptions: Under-16 passengers are allowed on Class 3 bikes designed for passengers. Until Dec 31, 2026 there is no state minimum for Class 1 or 2. From Jan 1, 2027 (P.A. 104-854), Class 1 and 2 riders must be 15 or older, and riders under 18 may carry only a sibling, stepsibling, child or stepchild.

license_registration_insurance.citation: 625 ILCS 5/1-146 (low-speed e-bikes excluded from 'motor vehicle'); 625 ILCS 5/11-208(a)8 (local registration and licensing)
license_registration_insurance.quote: Every vehicle which is self-propelled and every vehicle which is propelled by electric power obtained from overhead trolley wires, but not operated upon rails, except for vehicles moved solely by human power, motorized wheelchairs, low-speed electric bicycles
license_registration_insurance.notes: No state license, registration or insurance, because those rules attach to 'motor vehicles'. Through Dec 31, 2026, § 11-208(a)8 lets local authorities regulate 'bicycles, low-speed electric bicycles, and low-speed gas bicycles, and requiring the registration and licensing of same, including the requirement of a registration fee'. A city could require registration. From Jan 1, 2027, § 11-1517(i) bars local regulation of low-speed e-bikes except as that section allows. No statewide helmet law was found.

where_allowed.quote: A person may operate a low-speed electric bicycle upon any highway, street, or roadway authorized for use by bicycles, including, but not limited to, bicycle lanes.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed on any highway, street or roadway authorized for bicycles (§ 11-1517(e)). Bicycle rules apply (§ 11-1517(a)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Allowed on any bicycle path unless the municipality, county or local authority with jurisdiction bans e-bikes or a class (§ 11-1517(f), through 2026). From 2027, only the State agency with jurisdiction, DNR (by rule) and park, forest preserve, conservation and transit districts may restrict paths.
where_allowed.sidewalks: Prohibited: 'A person may not operate a low-speed electric bicycle on a sidewalk' (§ 11-1517(g)).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Minimum age 16 (passengers excepted) and speedometer required. No statewide Class 3 path ban. Chicago and other cities may restrict Class 3 locally (city ordinances not verified).

local_authority.quote: Regulating the operation of mobile carrying devices, bicycles, low-speed electric bicycles, and low-speed gas bicycles, and requiring the registration and licensing of same, including the requirement of a registration fee;
local_authority.details: Through Dec 31, 2026, local authorities may regulate e-bike operation, require registration and licensing (§ 11-208(a)8) and ban e-bikes or a class from bicycle paths (§ 11-1517(f)). This is how Chicago and some suburbs regulate e-bikes. From Jan 1, 2027, P.A. 104-854 preempts local (including home-rule) regulation of low-speed e-bikes. Only park, forest preserve, conservation and transit districts keep power over their own paths, plus State agencies and DNR.

non_ebike_devices.quote: Motor driven cycle. Every motorcycle and every motor scooter with less than 150 cubic centimeter piston displacement including motorized pedalcycles.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motor vehicle: moped or motor driven cycle (from 2027, expressly a motor driven cycle if it is any e-bike that is not a low-speed e-bike, including an exactly 750 W e-bike, or has an electric motor over 750 W up to 8,000 W)
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device at or over 750 W, or one without operable pedals, is not a low-speed e-bike and is a self-propelled motor vehicle, needing a driver's license, registration and insurance. Today it most likely counts as a moped (§ 1-148.2: 20-30 mph, 2 bhp or less, pedals optional) or motor driven cycle. From Jan 1, 2027 (§ 11-1403.4, P.A. 104-854), motor driven cycles need a valid driver's license (instruction permit at 16-17), an mph speedometer, a VIN, FMVSS compliance and mandatory insurance. New ones need a title and registration. They are banned from sidewalks, bike lanes, bicycle paths, shared-use paths and bike trails, and may be impounded. Pedal-less stand-up devices (scooters, e-skateboards, e-unicycles) become 'electric micromobility devices': age 16+, no sidewalks, and any capable of over 28 mph banned from all public highways, bike lanes and paths (§ 11-1435).

pending_changes.summary: (1) Class 1 and Class 2 riders must be 15 or older, and Class 3 stays 16+ (§ 11-1517(h)). (2) Riders under 18 may carry a passenger only if it is their sibling, stepsibling, child or stepchild. (3) Path regulation moves from municipalities and counties to the State agency, DNR and park, forest preserve, conservation and transit districts. Other local (including home-rule) regulation of low-speed e-bikes is preempted (§ 11-1517(i)). (4) Any electric bicycle that is not a low-speed e-bike (so any e-bike at 750 W or more, because the definition stays 'less than 750 watts'), and any electric motor rated greater than 750 W up to 8,000 W, is a motor driven cycle (§§ 1-140.10, 1-145.001). It needs a driver's license and insurance, new ones need a title and registration, and it is banned from bike lanes, paths, trails and sidewalks (§ 11-1403.4). (5) New 'electric micromobility device' category with an age-16 minimum (§ 11-1435). (6) 'Adaptive electric bicycle' category for riders with mobility disabilities.

open_questions: The 'less than 750 watts' wording excludes exactly 750 W. Common 750 W Class 2 and 3 bikes may technically fall outside the definition, and from 2027 such a bike becomes a 'motor driven cycle'. This is the biggest practical risk for Illinois answers. Is there enforcement guidance? Unknown.
Local ordinances (e.g. Chicago's e-bike rules, suburban sidewalk or age rules) remain valid through Dec 31, 2026 under § 11-208(a)8. They were not reviewed. After Jan 1, 2027 most are preempted.

Through 2026, a device over the watt limit has no explicit electric category. It may be a 'moped' (20-30 mph, 2 bhp or less) or 'motor driven cycle'. The license class and minimum age for it were not verified.

P.A. 104-141 (SB 2285, eff. Jan 1, 2026) requires bicycles, including e-bikes, to have wheels at least 12 inches in diameter and designated seats. Very small-wheeled e-bikes may fall outside the definition.
IL.verifier_notes: P.A. 104-0854 (SB 3484) was confirmed on ilga.gov. It was approved Aug 26, 2026 and takes effect Jan 1, 2027, with Class 1 and 2 riders 15+ and non-qualifying e-bikes made motor driven cycles. 'Less than 750 watts' is unchanged in both versions, and the only fixes are two wording corrections to the 750 W to 8,000 W range.

IN.name: Indiana

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means any bicycle that: (1) is equipped with: (A) fully operable pedals; (B) an assistive, electric motor with a power output not greater than seven hundred fifty (750) watts
definition.motor_watts_basis: an assistive, electric motor with a power output not greater than seven hundred fifty (750) watts
definition.notes: 750 W is inclusive ('not greater than'). Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph. Class 2 'may be used to exclusively propel' the bike and 'ceases or is unable to provide assistance' at 20 mph. Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph. There is no speedometer requirement. IC 9-21-11-13.1(h)-(i): the bike must meet CPSC 16 CFR 1512, and every e-bike motor, of any class, must disengage or stop assisting when the operator stops pedaling or applies the brakes. Read literally, that conflicts with a Class 2 throttle (see open questions). An e-bike is 'not a motor vehicle' and is regulated as a bicycle. It is excluded from 'motor driven cycle' (IC 9-13-2-104.1) and 'motorcycle' (IC 9-13-2-108). Text read from the official 2026 Indiana Code PDF (iga.in.gov/ic/2026/Title_9.pdf), which includes 2026 session laws. IC 9-21-11-13.1 was last amended by P.L.156-2020. Effective date of P.L.206-2019 assumed to be July 1, 2019.

label_required.quote: On and after January 1, 2020, a manufacturer or distributor of an electric bicycle shall affix a permanent and conspicuous label to each electric bicycle.
label_required.notes: The label shows the class level, top assisted speed and rated motor wattage. If a modification changes the top assisted speed or motor engagement, the label must be replaced with an accurate one (subsection (g)).

min_age.quote: A person less than fifteen (15) years of age may not operate a Class 3 electric bicycle.
min_age.exceptions: Under 15 may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 bike designed for a passenger (k)(4). No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2. Cities may regulate bicycle operation under IC 9-21-1-3(a)(9).

helmet.quote: A properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet ... must be worn by any person who operates or rides as a passenger on a Class 3 electric bicycle and is less than eighteen (18) years of age.
helmet.notes: Applies to operators and passengers on a Class 3 e-bike who are under 18. No state helmet rule for Class 1 or 2, or for regular bicycles.

license_registration_insurance.quote: The operator of an electric bicycle is not subject to: (1) IC 9-24 (driver's licenses); or (2) IC 9-25 (financial responsibility). (e) An electric bicycle is not subject to: (1) IC 9-17 (certificates of title)
license_registration_insurance.notes: Subsection (e) also exempts e-bikes from 'IC 9-18.1 (motor vehicle registration)'. No state license, insurance, title or registration. Caution: IC 9-21-1-3(a)(9) lets local authorities 'regulate the operation of bicycles' and 'require the registration and licensing of bicycles'. Because e-bikes are 'regulated as a bicycle' (IC 9-21-11-13.1(c)), a city may require local registration.

where_allowed.quote: A Class 3 electric bicycle may not be operated on a bicycle path or multipurpose path unless one (1) or more of the following conditions apply: (A) The bicycle path or multipurpose path is within or adjacent to a highway
where_allowed.roads: Allowed wherever bicycles are permitted (subsection (j)). Riders have the rights and duties of bicycle riders.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 and 2 may use any bicycle or multipurpose path where bicycles are allowed, 'unless otherwise specified by a statute, rule, or local ordinance'. Class 3 only on paths within or next to a highway, or where the local authority or state agency allows it. On natural-surface nonmotorized trails, the managing local authority or state agency decides (subsection (l)). Indiana DNR property rules were not reviewed.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No statewide e-bike sidewalk rule was found. Sidewalk riding is governed by local ordinance. Motor driven cycles are banned from sidewalks (IC 9-21-11-12), but e-bikes are excluded from that category.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Minimum age 15 (passengers excepted), helmet under 18, and kept off paths unless they are next to a road or the managing authority allows them.

local_authority.quote: Regulate the operation of bicycles and electric foot scooters and require the registration and licensing of bicycles and electric foot scooters, including the requirement of a registration fee.
local_authority.details: Local ordinances may restrict Class 1 and 2 on paths, may open paths to Class 3, and regulate natural-surface trails. Under IC 9-21-1-3(a)(9) they may regulate bicycle operation, which includes e-bikes because they are regulated as bicycles, and may require registration and licensing with a fee. Some Indiana cities are reported to have local e-bike age or registration ordinances (not verified).

non_ebike_devices.citation: IC 9-13-2-104.1 (motor driven cycle); IC 9-21-11-12 (motor driven cycle operation)
non_ebike_devices.quote: A motor driven cycle may not be operated under any of the following conditions: (1) By an individual less than fifteen (15) years of age.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motor driven cycle (if it meets the FMVSS and registration conditions) or motorcycle, otherwise not street legal
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device over 750 W, or with no operable pedals, is not an electric bicycle. A 'motor driven cycle' must comply with FMVSS (49 CFR 571), have a cylinder capacity of 50 cc or less, and be registered as a motor driven cycle. Under IC 9-21-11-12 it needs an ID card with a motor driven cycle endorsement, a driver's license or a learner's permit. The rider must be at least 15. It is barred from interstates and sidewalks and limited to 35 mph. A device without FMVSS certification cannot register in either category and is not street legal. How a purely electric motor fits the 50 cc test was not verified.

open_questions: No 2021-2026 amendment to the e-bike sections was found. The 2026 Indiana Code (which includes 2026 P.L.s) shows IC 9-21-11-13.1 last amended in 2020. Bill-level searches of the 2025 and 2026 sessions were secondary and found nothing.
Local ordinances (sidewalk bans, age limits, registration under IC 9-21-1-3(a)(9)) were not reviewed. Several Indiana cities reportedly regulate youth e-bike riding.

IC 9-21-11-13.1(i) requires every e-bike motor, including a Class 2 throttle, to disengage when the rider stops pedaling. Read literally, a throttle-only Class 2 conflicts with this. Unclear how it is enforced.
DNR property e-bike rules were not reviewed.
IN.verifier_notes: IC 9-13-2-49.2 in the official 2026 Indiana Code reads 'not greater than seven hundred fifty (750) watts', so 750 W passes and 'at_most' is right (the words are split across a line break, which likely confused the automatic check). No 2025 or 2026 change or future-dated version exists for the e-bike sections, and the only fix is one inconsistent note about the stop-pedaling clause.

KS.name: Kansas

definition.quote: "Electric-assisted bicycle" means a bicycle with two or three wheels, a saddle, fully operative pedals for human propulsion, and an electric motor of less than 750 watts that meets the requirements of one of the following three classes:
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than 750 watts
definition.notes: WATT LIMIT IS STRICT: 'less than 750 watts', so exactly 750 W is outside the literal definition. The bike needs two or three wheels, a saddle and fully operative pedals. Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph. Class 2 may propel the bike alone and gives no assistance at 20 mph. Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph. There is no speedometer requirement. The bike must meet CPSC 16 C.F.R. 1512 (K.S.A. 8-1592b(e)). An e-bike is 'a vehicle to the same extent as a bicycle' and 'shall not be considered a motor vehicle'. It is excluded from 'motorized bicycle' (K.S.A. 8-1439a). Last amended by L. 2022 ch. 43 (SB 101), effective July 1, 2022. The 2026 Kansas Statutes on kslegislature.gov show the same text.

label_required.quote: On and after January 1, 2023, manufacturers and distributors of electric-assisted bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each electric-assisted bicycle.
label_required.notes: The label shows the class number, top assisted speed and motor wattage in 9-point Arial or larger. Under (d), no one may tamper with or modify an e-bike's motor-powered speed or engagement unless the class label is replaced afterward.

min_age.quote: No person under 16 years of age may operate a class 3 electric-assisted bicycle. A person under 16 years of age may ride as a passenger on a class 3 electric-assisted bicycle that is designed to accommodate passengers.
min_age.exceptions: Under 16 may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 bike designed for passengers. No statewide minimum for Class 1 or 2.

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric-assisted bicycle or a person riding an electric-assisted bicycle shall not be required to maintain: (1) Vehicle liability insurance coverage; (2) a driver's license; (3) registration
license_registration_insurance.notes: The same subsection also exempts e-bikes from a certificate of title and a license plate, and says an e-bike 'shall not be considered a motor vehicle'. No statewide helmet law was found.

where_allowed.quote: An electric-assisted bicycle may be ridden in places where bicycles are allowed, including, but not limited to, streets, highways, roadways, bicycle lanes, bicycle or multi-use paths, trails or trail networks.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. E-bike riders have the rights and duties of bicycle riders. Note K.S.A. 8-1590(d): 'Wherever a usable path for bicycles has been provided adjacent to a roadway, bicycle riders shall use such path and shall not use the roadway.' This bicycle duty appears to reach e-bike riders through 8-1592b(a).
where_allowed.paths_trails: All classes, including Class 3, are allowed on bicycle and multi-use paths, trails and trail networks. A municipality, county or state agency with jurisdiction may restrict or ban e-bikes or a class on its paths and trails (8-1592b(f)(2)). On natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized, the managing authority regulates e-bikes (8-1592b(f)(3)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: No statewide e-bike sidewalk rule. Cities may adopt home-rule ordinances governing e-bikes on 'sidewalks or sidewalk areas' (8-1592b(f)(2)). Local rules apply.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Minimum age 16 (passengers excepted). No statewide Class 3 path ban, but path managers may ban a specific class.

local_authority.quote: This subsection shall not be construed to prevent a city, through the exercise of its home rule powers, from adopting an ordinance governing the operation of electric-assisted bicycles on streets, highways, roadways, sidewalks or sidewalk areas under the city's jurisdiction
local_authority.details: Cities may use home-rule ordinances to govern e-bike operation on streets, roads and sidewalks. Municipalities, counties and state agencies may restrict or ban e-bikes, or a specific class, on paths and trails they control. Whether a city may set age limits is not addressed expressly, but home-rule 'governing the operation' language is broad. City ordinances (e.g. Wichita, Lawrence, Overland Park) were not checked.

non_ebike_devices.quote: No person shall drive any motorized bicycle upon a highway of this state unless such person: (1) Has a valid driver's license that entitles the licensee to drive a motor vehicle in any class or classes
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorized bicycle (3.5 bhp or less, 30 mph or less design speed) or motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device at or over 750 W, or without operative pedals, is not an electric-assisted bicycle. A 'motorized bicycle' (K.S.A. 8-1439a) has two or three wheels, may be propelled by human power and/or a helper motor of 3.5 bhp or less (about 2,600 W) with an automatic transmission, and has a maximum design speed of 30 mph or less. It needs a driver's license of any class, or a motorized-bicycle-only class C license at age 15+ after written and vision tests (K.S.A. 8-235(d)). Registration is likely required. K.S.A. 8-134a is titled 'Registration and reregistration of pickup trucks, motorcycles, motorized bicycles...', but only its title was reviewed. Faster devices are motorcycles needing a class M license. Insurance for motorized bicycles was not verified.

open_questions: The 'less than 750 watts' wording excludes exactly 750 W. Many 750 W bikes may technically fall outside the definition. Enforcement practice is unknown.

Resolved by verifier: the legislature's own 2025-26 search (kslegislature.gov search API) finds one e-bike bill, HB 2459 (helmets for riders 17 and under on electric-assisted bicycles and scooters, amending K.S.A. 8-126, 8-1498 and 8-15,113). It died in House Transportation. No 2025 or 2026 act changed K.S.A. 8-1489 or 8-1592b, whose histories end with L. 2022, ch. 43.
Does K.S.A. 8-1590(d), which requires riders to use an adjacent bike path instead of the roadway, apply to e-bikes? It probably does through 8-1592b(a). Not confirmed by case law.
Motorized bicycle insurance requirement not verified.
KS.verifier_notes: K.S.A. 8-1489 ('less than 750 watts'), 8-1592b, 8-1439a and 8-235(d) match ksrevisor.org, all last changed in 2022. The legislature's search found one 2025-26 e-bike bill, HB 2459 (helmets under 18), which died in committee, so the only fix is a resolved open question.

KY.name: Kentucky

definition.citation: No e-bike definition in KRS. Closest: 601 KAR 14:020 § 1(1) ('bicycle'); KRS 186.010(5) and 189.285(6)(b) ('moped'); KRS 189.010(26) ('electric low-speed scooter')
definition.quote: "Bicycle": (a) Means a device with an attached seat propelled primarily by human power upon which a person rides astride or upon, regardless of the number and size of the wheels in contact with the ground
definition.motor_watts_basis: No e-bike statute. Closest text: “Bicycle” ... propelled primarily by human power
definition.notes: Kentucky has no statute defining an electric bicycle and no Class 1/2/3 system. The current KRS 186.010 and 189.010 (both amended effective July 15, 2026) do not mention electric bicycles. An e-bike could fall into three categories. (1) 'Bicycle' under the Transportation Cabinet rule 601 KAR 14:020, which requires a device 'propelled primarily by human power'. This plausibly covers pedal-assist bikes, but not throttle-only riding. (2) 'Moped' (KRS 186.010(5)): 'a motorized bicycle whose frame design may include one (1) or more horizontal crossbars supporting a fuel tank so long as it also has pedals, or a motorized bicycle with a step-through type frame which may or may not have pedals rated no more than two (2) brake horsepower ... capable of a maximum speed of not more than thirty (30) miles per hour'. Mopeds need an operator's license (KRS 186.410(1)). (3) 'Electric low-speed scooter' (KRS 189.010(26)): under 100 lb, wheels, handlebars, brake, 'designed to be stood or sat upon', propelled by an electric motor, human power or both, with a 20 mph design maximum. Operators must be 16+ (KRS 189.289). No statute or court decision found says which category applies. The rules engine should NOT return 'legal' for Kentucky without a human-review caveat.

label_required.citation: None found in KRS or 601 KAR 14:020
label_required.notes: No labeling statute exists because there is no e-bike class law. Value is null (not applicable or unknown), not false.

license_registration_insurance.citation: KRS 186.410(1) (operator's license for mopeds); KRS 186.010(4) (mopeds excluded from 'motor vehicle')
license_registration_insurance.quote: every person not exempted by KRS 186.420 and 186.430 shall, before operating a motor vehicle, motorcycle, or moped upon a highway, secure an operator's license as provided in this chapter.
license_registration_insurance.notes: UNRESOLVED. If an e-bike is a bicycle: no license, registration or insurance. If it is a 'moped': an operator's license is required (KRS 186.410(1)). Registration appears not required, since KRS 186.010(4) says 'Motor vehicle' 'shall not include a moped'. If it is an 'electric low-speed scooter': it is excluded from 'motor vehicle' (KRS 189.010(19)(b)9), so no registration. All three booleans are null until clarified.

where_allowed.citation: 601 KAR 14:020 § 7(4) (bicycles on sidewalks); KRS 189.289(1) (electric low-speed scooters)
where_allowed.quote: A bicycle may be operated on a sidewalk or a crosswalk unless prohibited by law or ordinance.
where_allowed.roads: If treated as a bicycle, it is operated 'in the same manner as a motor vehicle' and may use highway shoulders (601 KAR 14:020 § 7). If treated as a moped or low-speed scooter, highway use is allowed under those rules.
where_allowed.bike_lanes: No e-bike-specific rule. Electric low-speed scooters may use bicycle lanes (KRS 189.289(1)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: No state e-bike path rule found. Local, state park and Kentucky Fish & Wildlife rules govern. Not reviewed.
where_allowed.sidewalks: Bicycles may use sidewalks 'unless prohibited by law or ordinance' and must yield to pedestrians (601 KAR 14:020 § 7(4)). Whether this covers e-bikes depends on the unresolved classification.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: None. Kentucky has no class system.

local_authority.citation: KRS 189.289(5) (scooters must follow local ordinances); 601 KAR 14:020 § 7(4) (local sidewalk bans)
local_authority.quote: An operator of an electric low-speed scooter and any company or entity that provides electric low-speed scooters for rental, shall comply with all local government ordinances.
local_authority.details: No statute addresses local e-bike regulation. Local ordinances can bar bicycles from sidewalks (601 KAR 14:020). Cities such as Louisville and Lexington may have e-bike or e-scooter ordinances (not reviewed).

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Moped" means either a motorized bicycle whose frame design may include one (1) or more horizontal crossbars supporting a fuel tank so long as it also has pedals
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (2 bhp or less, 30 mph or less) needing an operator's license, or a motorcycle (over 50 mph) or motor scooter needing registration and a motorcycle license
non_ebike_devices.notes: Because Kentucky has no e-bike category, even a 'legal' Class 1-3 bike elsewhere may be a moped here. Higher-power electric devices: a moped is capped at 2 bhp (about 1,491 W) and 30 mph. A 'motor scooter' (KRS 186.010(24)) is defined by an engine 'greater than fifty (50) cubic centimeters', which does not map cleanly to electric motors. A 'motorcycle' must exceed 50 mph. 'Electric motorcycle' (KRS 186.010(26), new July 15, 2026) covers motorcycles and motor scooters powered by a plug-in battery. Moped minimum age was not determined (it follows operator's license and permit age rules in KRS 186.450, not reviewed).

open_questions: Which category does a typical Class 1/2/3 e-bike fall into: 'bicycle' (601 KAR 14:020, 'propelled primarily by human power'), 'moped' (KRS 186.010(5)) or 'electric low-speed scooter' (KRS 189.010(26), 20 mph design max, under 100 lb, 16+)? No statute, regulation or case found resolves it. Ask the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet or KSP.

If e-bikes are mopeds, riders need an operator's license (KRS 186.410), which would effectively bar young riders. If they are low-speed scooters, riders must be 16+. If they are bicycles, there is no age or license rule. The app should return 'uncertain' for Kentucky, not 'legal'.

No 2024, 2025 or 2026 e-bike law was found. Kentucky bill titles are generic ('AN ACT relating to motor vehicles'), so the verifier also read the summaries and index headings of every enacted measure on the LRC 'Law' lists (162 for 2025 RS, 201 for 2026 RS). None mentions bicycles, e-bikes, mopeds or scooters. KRS 186.010 and 189.010 were amended effective July 15, 2026 (2026 Ky. Acts ch. 133, 135) without adding an e-bike definition.
Local ordinances (Louisville Metro, Lexington-Fayette) were not reviewed.
KRS 189.289(6) says the cabinet's scooter regulations 'shall not include any equipment or helmet use requirements'. No helmet law applies under any reading.
KY.never_return_legal_reason: Kentucky has no e-bike statute. An e-bike could be a bicycle, a moped needing an operator's license, or an electric low-speed scooter (16+), and no source resolves which.
KY.verifier_notes: Kentucky still has no e-bike statute. KRS 186.010 and 189.010 (as amended Jul 15, 2026) define moped and electric low-speed scooter but not e-bike, and none of the 162 enacted 2025 or 201 enacted 2026 measures mentions bicycles, mopeds or scooters, so never_return_legal stays true and the only fix is a stronger note on the bill search.

LA.name: Louisiana

definition.citation: La. R.S. 32:1(25) (enacted as 32:1(95) by Acts 2020, No. 152, then renumbered); R.S. 32:1(7) (bicycle)
definition.quote: equipped with fully operable pedals, and an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty watts that meets the requirement of one of the following classes:
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty watts
definition.notes: WATT LIMIT IS STRICT: 'less than seven hundred fifty watts', so exactly 750 W is outside the literal definition. WHEEL SIZE RULE: the bike needs a saddle or seat for each rider and either two tandem wheels, one of which is 16 inches or more in diameter, or three wheels, one of which is 20 inches or more. Small-wheel e-bikes may not qualify. Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph. Class 2 may propel the bike alone and gives no assistance at 20 mph. Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph. R.S. 32:204: must meet CPSC 16 CFR 1512. The motor must disengage 'when the rider stops pedaling or when the brakes are applied'. Read literally, this applies to Class 2 throttles too. Class 3 needs an mph speedometer. E-bikes are excluded from 'motor vehicle', 'motorcycle' and 'motorized bicycle' (R.S. 32:1(50)-(52)). Current R.S. 32:1 (last amended Acts 2025, No. 281) keeps the 2020 wording.

label_required.quote: On and after August 1, 2020, manufacturers and distributors of electric-assisted bicycles shall apply a label permanently affixed in a prominent location to each electric-assisted bicycle.
label_required.notes: The label shows the class number, top assisted speed and motor wattage. (C): no tampering that changes the class unless the label is replaced.

min_age.quote: No person under the age of twelve shall operate a Class three electric-assisted bicycle. A person under the age of twelve may ride as a passenger on a Class three electric-assisted bicycle designed to accommodate passengers.
min_age.exceptions: Under 12 may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 bike designed for passengers. No statewide minimum for Class 1 or 2. The stale index row and several blogs that say 16 reflect an earlier bill draft. The enacted text says twelve.

helmet.quote: All operators and passengers of a Class three electric-assisted bicycle shall wear an approved bicycle helmet.
helmet.notes: The fine is $50 and is waived on proof of buying an approved helmet. A citation is not prima facie evidence of negligence.

helmet.citation: La. R.S. 32:199(B)(1) (bicycle helmet rule), applied to e-bikes through R.S. 32:204(A)
helmet.quote: Such child under the age of twelve to operate or ride as a passenger on a bicycle without wearing an approved helmet of good fit fastened securely upon the head with the straps of the helmet.
helmet.notes: The duty is on the parent or guardian ('no parent, guardian, or person with legal responsibility ... shall knowingly allow'), and no civil penalty or court costs apply. § 199's own 'bicycle' definition is 'a human-powered vehicle with two tandem wheels designed to transport, by pedaling'. Reaching e-bikes depends on R.S. 32:204(A) giving e-bike operators all the duties of bicycle operators. That is a reasonable reading, but not express.

LA.helmet_notes: The under-17 helmet rule in R.S. 32:300.1.1(I) covers electric low-speed scooters only, not e-bikes. Some local police notices (for example Natchitoches, Aug 2026) cite that scooter statute next to the e-bike classes, so families may see an under-17 rule that does not apply to Class 1 or 2 e-bikes.

license_registration_insurance.citation: La. R.S. 32:1(50) (e-bike excluded from 'motor vehicle'); also R.S. 32:401(20), 32:851(5)
license_registration_insurance.quote: "Motor vehicle" means every vehicle which is self-propelled, and every vehicle which is propelled by electric power obtained from overhead trolley wires, but not operated upon rails, but excluding a motorized bicycle and an electric-assisted bicycle.
license_registration_insurance.notes: Act 152 also excluded e-bikes from 'motor vehicle' in the Driver's License Law (R.S. 32:401(20)) and the Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Law (R.S. 32:851(5)), per the enrolled Act text, so no license or insurance is required. Registration: Louisiana vehicle registration sits mostly in Title 47 (vehicle registration license tax), which was not checked for e-bike text. 'No registration' is inferred from e-bikes being treated as bicycles and excluded from 'motor vehicle'. No section says 'no license required' in so many words.

where_allowed.quote: an electric-assisted bicycle may be ridden in places where bicycles are allowed, including but not limited to streets, highways, roadways, bicycle facilities, bicycle lanes, shared-use trails, bicycle paths, or trails.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. Riders have the rights and duties of bicycle riders: ride as far right as practicable, and shoulders are allowed (R.S. 32:197).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Allowed. R.S. 32:203(C) allows e-bikes in bike lanes at a reasonable and prudent speed that does not endanger bicyclists.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Allowed on shared-use trails, bicycle paths and trails. After notice and a public hearing, the managing local or state authority may ban Class 1 or 2 for safety or legal reasons. It may ban Class 3 without that process (R.S. 32:204(F)(1)-(2)). Natural-surface nonmotorized trails are regulated by their managers (F)(3).
where_allowed.sidewalks: No statewide e-bike sidewalk rule found. Local ordinances govern (several parishes and cities restrict sidewalk cycling, not reviewed).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Minimum age 12 (passengers excepted), helmet for every operator and passenger, speedometer required, and path managers may ban Class 3.

local_authority.quote: A local municipal authority, local parish authority, or state agency having jurisdiction over a shared-use trail or bicycle path or trail may prohibit the operation of Class three electric-assisted bicycles on such path or trail.
local_authority.details: Local and state path managers may ban Class 3 from their paths and trails. They may ban Class 1 or 2 only after notice, a public hearing and a safety or legal finding. They regulate natural-surface trails. No express state power for local e-bike age limits. General municipal police powers over sidewalks were not reviewed.

non_ebike_devices.quote: A motorized bicycle shall only be operated upon the roadway of the highways of this state by a person fifteen years of age or older who possesses a valid Louisiana driver's license
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorized bicycle (1.5 bhp or less, 25 mph or less design speed, pedals), otherwise a motorcycle or motor vehicle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device at or over 750 W, with no operable pedals, or with too-small wheels is not an electric-assisted bicycle. If it has pedals, 1.5 bhp (about 1,119 W) or less and a design speed of 25 mph or less, it is a 'motorized bicycle'. That needs age 15+ and a valid Louisiana driver's license, roadway only, and no sidewalks or interstates. Anything faster or more powerful is a motorcycle or motor vehicle needing registration, insurance and a motorcycle endorsement (not verified in detail).

open_questions: The 'less than 750 watts' wording excludes exactly 750 W. Many 750 W Class 2 and 3 bikes may technically be 'motorized bicycles' requiring a driver's license, or motorcycles. Enforcement practice is unknown.
The 16-inch (two-wheel) and 20-inch (three-wheel) minimum wheel size can exclude small-wheel and folding e-bikes. The vision model may need wheel-size data.
Does the under-12 bicycle helmet duty (R.S. 32:199) reach e-bikes? Likely yes through R.S. 32:204(A). The duty is on parents, with no penalty.

Resolved by verifier: Act 951 of 2026 (HB 723) became law without the Governor's signature, effective Aug 1, 2026. It amends R.S. 32:232(3) so the rider of a motorcycle, moped, bicycle 'or any electric bicycle' may go through a steady red at a vehicle-actuated signal after a full stop for two signal cycles or two minutes, treating it as a stop sign and yielding. It does not change who may ride which class. The 2025 and 2026 citator indexes show no change to R.S. 32:1(25) or 32:204, whose history still shows only Acts 2020, No. 152.
City and parish sidewalk ordinances (New Orleans, Baton Rouge) were not reviewed.
LA.verifier_notes: R.S. 32:1(25) ('less than seven hundred fifty watts', wheel-size rule) and 32:204 (Class 3 age 12, Class 3 helmets at all ages) match legis.la.gov, and the 2025 and 2026 citator indexes show no change to either. Act 951 of 2026 is real but only adds a red-light rule, so the fixes are two notes and no verdict changes.

MA.name: Massachusetts

definition.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 90, § 1 (definitions of 'Electric bicycle', 'Class 1 electric bicycle', 'Class 2 electric bicycle')
definition.quote: ''Electric bicycle'', a bicycle or tricycle equipped with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of 750 watts or less that meets the requirements of a class 1 electric bicycle or a class 2 electric bicycle.
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of 750 watts or less
definition.notes: TWO-CLASS state. Massachusetts defines only Class 1 and Class 2 (added by St. 2022, c. 176, §§ 14-19, an emergency law approved Aug 10, 2022. MassBike says it took effect 90 days later, Nov 8, 2022, but the act carries an emergency preamble). There is no Class 3 in Massachusetts law. A 28 mph pedal-assist bike is NOT an 'electric bicycle' here and most likely falls under 'motorized bicycle' (pedal bicycle with helper motor, max speed 30 mph or less), which needs a driver's license or learner's permit, age 16+, a helmet, and RMV moped registration. Electric bicycles are excluded from 'motorized bicycle', 'motorized scooter' and 'motor vehicles'. E-bikes must meet CPSC bicycle standards (ch. 85, § 11B3/4(e)). E-bike riders get all rights and duties of bicyclists under ch. 85, § 11B, which includes the helmet rule for riders 16 or younger. No minimum age for Class 1 or Class 2.

label_required.quote: Manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall apply a label that shall be permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each electric bicycle containing the classification number, top assisted speed and motor wattage

helmet.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 85, § 11B(2)(iii), applied to e-bikes by ch. 85, § 11B3/4(b)
helmet.quote: Any person 16 years of age or younger operating a bicycle or being carried as a passenger on a bicycle on a public way, bicycle path or on any other public right-of-way shall wear a helmet.

license_registration_insurance.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 90, § 1 (definitions of 'Motor vehicles' and 'Motorized bicycle')
license_registration_insurance.quote: The definition of ''Motor vehicles'' shall not include electric bicycles or motorized bicycles.

where_allowed.quote: an electric bicycle or an operator of an electric bicycle shall be afforded all of the rights and privileges ... of the operator of a bicycle ... provided, however, that electric bicycles shall not be ridden or operated on sidewalks.
where_allowed.roads: Same as bicycles: all public ways except limited-access or express state highways posted against bicycles (ch. 85, § 11B).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Bike paths and bikeways allowed unless the municipality or agency with jurisdiction prohibits or regulates e-bikes after public notice and a hearing (§ 11B3/4(c)). Natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized are CLOSED to e-bikes unless the agency opens them after notice and hearing (§ 11B3/4(d)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Prohibited for e-bikes statewide (§ 11B3/4(b)), even though regular bicycles may use some sidewalks outside business districts.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: No Class 3 category exists. A 28 mph bike is likely a motorized bicycle: max 25 mph on ways, excluded from off-street recreational bicycle paths, bicycle lanes allowed (ch. 90, § 1B).

local_authority.quote: A municipality, local authority or state agency with jurisdiction over a bike path or bikeway after public notice and a public hearing may adopt ordinances or regulations prohibiting or otherwise regulating the operation of electric bicycles on such paths
local_authority.details: Local path bans and speed limits are allowed after notice and hearing. Locals may also open natural-surface trails. § 11B3/4(b) makes e-bike riders subject to local ordinances that apply to bicycles. No statute found that lets a town set an e-bike minimum age or ban e-bikes from roads, so 'true' reflects path bans only. DCR (state parks) sets its own e-bike rules for its paths.

non_ebike_devices.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 90, § 1 ('Motorized bicycle'); ch. 90, § 1B; ch. 90, § 1E
non_ebike_devices.quote: A motorized bicycle shall not be operated upon any way ... by any person under sixteen years of age ... A motorized bicycle shall not be operated on any way by any person not possessing a valid driver's license or learner's permit.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorized bicycle (moped) for pedal or non-pedal bikes with a helper motor capable of 30 mph or less, including any Class 3 or over-750 W bike. Faster devices are motorcycles. Stand-up or sit-down scooters are motorized scooters
non_ebike_devices.notes: Motorized bicycle: 'a pedal bicycle which has a helper motor, or a non-pedal bicycle which has a motor, with a cylinder capacity not exceeding fifty cubic centimeters, an automatic transmission, and which is capable of a maximum speed of no more than thirty miles per hour' (ch. 90, § 1). Needs license or learner's permit, age 16+, helmet for operator and passenger, 25 mph cap, no off-street recreational bike paths (ch. 90, § 1B). Mass.gov RMV pages say mopeds must be registered ($40 for 2 years, rear plate). I did not read the registration statute. Motorized scooters (ch. 90, § 1E) need a license or learner's permit, helmet, 20 mph cap, no night riding. A Class 3 e-bike, a throttle bike over 20 mph, or a bike over 750 W is therefore NOT legal for an unlicensed teen.

pending_changes.bill: S.3168 (194th General Court) An Act to enhance the safe use of micromobility devices (new draft of S.2347, S.2373, S.2432)
pending_changes.signed: no (reported by Transportation 7/6/2026, referred to Senate Ways and Means)
pending_changes.summary: Would add a Class 3 e-bike definition (pedal assist to 28 mph), redefine motorized bicycle to include electric equivalents, require annual moped registration and insurance, bar mopeds from bike lanes, create speed tiers for micromobility devices and UL 2271 battery standards. Not enacted as of 2026-10-16.

pending_changes.bill: H.3758 (194th) An Act relative to class 3 electric bicycles
pending_changes.signed: no (in Joint Committee on Transportation, reporting date extended to 7/31/2026)
pending_changes.summary: Would add Class 3 e-bikes. House companion to S.2373, which was folded into S.3168.

open_questions: How does the RMV or a court actually classify a Class 3 (28 mph) e-bike? The 'motorized bicycle' definition uses a 50 cc cylinder test that does not fit electric motors. It could instead be a 'motorized scooter' (any 2- or 3-wheeled device with handlebars, designed to be stood or sat upon, powered by an electric motor), which also needs a driver's license or learner's permit, a helmet and a 20 mph cap, with no night riding (ch. 90, § 1E). Either way an unlicensed rider cannot ride it legally, so the Class 3 not-an-e-bike caution holds. No statute names the category directly.
Moped registration requirement was taken from mass.gov RMV pages (seen only in search results, page blocked with 403), not from statute text.
Effective date: ch. 176 of 2022 has an emergency preamble (effective on approval, Aug 10, 2022), while MassBike says Nov 8, 2022. The label rule took effect Jan 1, 2023 under § 63.

Checked Oct 16, 2026: S.3168 is still 'Referred to Senate Committee on Ways and Means' (last action Jul 6, 2026), and H.3758 is still in the Joint Committee on Transportation. The verifier searched the text of all 339 session laws of 2025 and 2026 (Acts 2025 ch. 1-101, Acts 2026 ch. 1-239) and found no e-bike, motorized bicycle or motorized scooter change. S.3168 could still pass in informal sessions before the 194th General Court ends in early January 2027, so re-check before launch.
DCR e-bike rules for state parks and DCR paths were not reviewed.

verdict_cautions.reason: Massachusetts defines only Class 1 and 2. A 28 mph bike most likely is a 'motorized bicycle' (license or permit, 16+, helmet, registration).

MA.verifier_notes: Ch. 90 § 1 still defines only Class 1 and 2 at '750 watts or less', so the Class 3 not-an-e-bike caution stands. S.3168 has sat in Senate Ways and Means since Jul 6, 2026, H.3758 is still in Joint Transportation, and none of the 339 session laws of 2025 and 2026 mentions e-bikes, so the only fixes are two notes.

MD.name: Maryland

definition.quote: “Electric bicycle” means a vehicle that: ... (2) Is equipped with fully operable pedals; (3) Has two or three wheels; (4) Has a motor with a rating of 750 watts or less
definition.motor_watts_basis: Has a motor with a rating of 750 watts or less
definition.notes: Three classes in § 11-117.1(b): Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 assist whether or not pedaling to 20 mph, Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph. Enacted by 2019 Chapter 64 (SB 935 / HB 939), effective Oct 1, 2019. An electric bicycle is a 'bicycle' (§ 11-104(2)) and is excluded from 'motor vehicle' (§ 11-135(b)(3)). § 22-420 also requires CPSC 16 CFR 1512 compliance, motor cutoff when brakes are applied (and when pedaling stops for Class 1 and 3), and a speedometer on Class 3. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or Class 2 was found. Bicycle helmet rule for under 16 is enforced by warning only (§ 21-1207.1(d)).

label_required.quote: Beginning January 1, 2020, manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall apply in a prominent location a standardized label that is permanently affixed to each electric bicycle.

min_age.quote: (1) A person under the age of 16 years may not operate a Class 3 electric bicycle on a public highway. (2) A person under the age of 16 years may ride as a passenger
min_age.exceptions: The statute bars under-16 operation 'on a public highway'. Under 16 may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 designed for passengers.

helmet.quote: A person to whom this section applies may not operate or ride as a passenger on a bicycle unless the person is wearing a helmet

license_registration_insurance.quote: “Motor vehicle” does not include: ... (3) An electric bicycle, as defined in § 11–117.1 of this subtitle

where_allowed.quote: electric bicycles may be operated where bicycles are allowed to travel, including bike lanes.
where_allowed.roads: Where bicycles may travel. Bicycles may not use roadways posted above 50 mph (shoulder use allowed) or expressways, per § 21-1205.1(a). Must use a smooth-surface bike lane where one exists (§ 21-1205.1(b)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 and 2 allowed on bicycle paths unless the local authority or State agency with jurisdiction prohibits them. Natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized may be regulated for any class by the agency with jurisdiction.
where_allowed.sidewalks: § 21-1103(b)(2): 'Unless prohibited by local ordinance, a person may ride a bicycle ... on a sidewalk.' Because § 11-104 defines bicycle to include an electric bicycle, sidewalk riding appears allowed unless a local ordinance bans it. Rider must yield to pedestrians (§ 21-1202(b)(3)).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Class 3 may not be used on a bicycle path unless the path is within or adjacent to a highway right-of-way or the agency with jurisdiction allows it. Riders under 16 may not operate Class 3 on a public highway. Class 3 must have a speedometer (§ 22-420(e)).

local_authority.quote: A local authority or State agency that has jurisdiction over a bicycle path may prohibit the operation of a Class 1 or Class 2 electric bicycle on the bicycle path.
local_authority.details: Locals can ban Class 1 and 2 on bicycle paths they control, allow Class 3 on paths, regulate natural-surface trails, ban sidewalk riding by ordinance, and under § 25-102(a)(8) may engage in 'Regulating the operation of bicycles, requiring them to be registered, and imposing a registration fee' on highways under their jurisdiction. No statute found that expressly lets locals set a different minimum age, so 'true' reflects path bans and general bicycle regulation power, not a confirmed age power.

non_ebike_devices.quote: “Moped” means a bicycle that: ... (2) Is equipped with pedals that mechanically drive the rear wheel or wheels; ... (4) Has a motor with a rating of 1.5 brake horsepower or less
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (with pedals, up to 1.5 bhp) or motor scooter (no pedals, seat, step-through, up to 2.7 bhp). Larger devices likely motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A pedal device that fails the e-bike test (motor over 750 W, or assist above 20/28 mph) but has a motor of 1.5 bhp (about 1,119 W) or less is a moped. § 11-134.1(b) says a moped does not include an electric bicycle. Moped and motor scooter riders on a highway must carry a driver's license of any class or a moped operator's permit (§ 16-101(b)). The permit requires age 16 or older (§ 16-104.2(a)(1)). DOT-standard helmet (49 CFR 571.218) and eye protection or windscreen are required for all ages (§ 21-1306.1). Motor scooters are capped at 30 mph (§ 21-1205.1(c)). The MVA says mopeds and motor scooters must be titled and insured. I did not read the titling statute itself. A non-pedal device that is not step-through (for example a throttle-only electric motorbike) was not traced and may be a motorcycle needing registration and a Class M license.

pending_changes.bill: SB 743 (2026) Workgroup to Study State Laws on Electric Bicycles
pending_changes.signed: no (stayed in Senate Judicial Proceedings after a 3/10/2026 hearing. Session ended 4/13/2026)
pending_changes.summary: Would have created a workgroup to study e-bike laws and report by Jan 1, 2028. Did not pass. No rule change.

open_questions: Resolved by verifier: §§ 21-1205.2, 21-1207.1 and 22-420 (read Oct 16, 2026) contain no all-ages Class 3 helmet rule. The only helmet rule is § 21-1207.1, for riders and passengers under 16 on any bicycle, which includes an e-bike under § 11-104, and it is enforced by warning.

Sidewalk riding: § 21-1103(b) allows bicycles (which include e-bikes under § 11-104) on sidewalks unless a local ordinance bans it. Several counties and cities (for example Baltimore City and parts of Montgomery County) have local bans that the app does not model.
Moped titling and insurance were taken from MVA pages, not from the titling statute text.

Resolved by verifier: the General Assembly's open-data bill lists for the 2025 and 2026 sessions were searched. SB 14 (2025, e-bike title, registration and insurance) got an unfavorable report and was withdrawn, and SB 743 (2026 workgroup) never left Judicial Proceedings. The only enacted related law is Jay's Law (HB 375, Ch. 558 of 2025), which allows bicycle riding on sidewalks unless a local ordinance bans it. That is the § 21-1103(b)(2) text this record already uses. Ch. 418 of 2026 only funds sidewalk and bike path construction.
MD.verifier_notes: Transp. §§ 11-117.1 ('750 watts or less'), 21-1205.2, 21-1207.1, 22-420 and 21-1103 match mgaleg.maryland.gov. The pending change, SB 743 (2026), died in committee, and the 2025 and 2026 bill lists show no enacted e-bike law except Jay's Law (Ch. 558 of 2025, sidewalks), which the record already reflects, so the only fixes are two resolved open questions.

ME.name: Maine

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a 2-wheel or 3-wheel bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts that is a Class 1 electric bicycle, a Class 2 electric bicycle or a Class 3 electric bicycle
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than 750 watts
definition.notes: WATT LIMIT IS STRICT: 'less than 750 watts'. Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph. Class 2 'is capable of being used exclusively to propel the bicycle but is not capable of propelling the bicycle at a speed of 20 miles per hour'. Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph. § 2063(14)(C): if a bike is modified so the motor assists above 20 mph on motor alone or above 28 mph with pedaling, 'that vehicle is no longer an electric bicycle'. § 2063(14)(D)-(E): must meet CPSC 16 CFR 1512. The motor must cut off when the brakes are applied, and Class 1 and 3 motors also when pedaling stops. § 2063(14)(G): Class 3 needs an mph speedometer. E-bikes are excluded from 'motor vehicle', 'moped', 'motorized bicycle or tricycle' and 'motorized scooter' (§ 101(36), (41), (41-B), (42)). The Revisor's online statutes are 'current through October 1, 2026' (through the Second Regular Session of the 132nd Legislature). PL 2019, c. 349, effective date assumed Sept 19, 2019 (Maine's general effective date for the 2019 session, not verified).

label_required.quote: Beginning October 1, 2019, a manufacturer, distributor or seller of electric bicycles in this State shall apply a label that is permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each electric bicycle.
label_required.notes: The duty also falls on sellers. The label shows the class number, top assisted speed and motor wattage in 9-point Arial or larger. No tampering that changes speed or engagement unless the label is replaced.

min_age.quote: A person under 16 years of age may not operate a Class 2 or Class 3 electric bicycle.
min_age.exceptions: Under 16 may be a passenger on a Class 2 or 3 bike only if it is designed for passengers. No minimum age for Class 1. NOTE: the stale index said Class 3 only, but the statute covers Class 2 too.

min_age.quote: A person under 16 years of age may not operate a Class 2 or Class 3 electric bicycle.
min_age.exceptions: Under 16 may be a passenger only if the bike is designed for passengers.

helmet.quote: A person under 16 years of age who is an operator or passenger on an electric bicycle shall wear a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet
helmet.notes: Applies to operators and passengers of any class. Under § 2063(7), riders under 17 are not fined under § 2063, but under § 2063(8) police may impound a juvenile's bicycle (which by § 2063(1) includes an e-bike) for violations of that section.

license_registration_insurance.quote: A person operating an electric bicycle is not subject to the provisions of this Title relating to financial responsibility, driver's licenses, registration and license plate requirements.
license_registration_insurance.notes: E-bikes are also excluded from 'motor vehicle' (§ 101(42)(C)). OUI rules still apply (§ 2063(14)(I) cross-references § 2112-A and 23 U.S.C. 154).

where_allowed.quote: A Class 3 electric bicycle may not be operated on a bicycle path unless it is within a highway or roadway or the bicycle path has been authorized for the operation of Class 3 electric bicycles
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. For § 2063, 'bicycle' includes an e-bike, so bicycle road rules apply: ride to the right, paved shoulders allowed, and the rights and duties of a vehicle operator.
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Allowed as a bicycle. No e-bike-specific bike lane rule.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 and 2 may go wherever bicycles may, including bicycle paths, unless the municipality or agency with jurisdiction prohibits them. Class 3 only on paths within a highway or roadway, or where the managing authority authorizes it. No e-bike may use a nonmotorized path with significant natural surface (gravel, stones, wooden bridging) unless authorized (§ 2063(14)(F)(3)). Private owners may allow or restrict e-bikes on private ways and property.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No statewide e-bike sidewalk rule found in 29-A. Municipal ordinances govern. Not reviewed.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Minimum age 16 (passengers excepted), speedometer required, and barred from bicycle paths unless the path is in a roadway or authorized.

local_authority.quote: except that a municipality, local authority or governing body of a public agency that has jurisdiction over a bicycle path may prohibit the operation of a Class 1 electric bicycle or Class 2 electric bicycle on that bicycle path.
local_authority.details: Path managers may ban Class 1 or 2, open paths to Class 3 and authorize natural-surface paths. A municipality may, by an ordinance approved by DPS and DOT, change where bicycles ride on the roadway (§ 2063(2)). No express local e-bike age-limit power. Federal and state park rules (e.g. Acadia National Park carriage roads, reportedly Class 1 only) are separate and were not verified.

non_ebike_devices.quote: A moped or motorized scooter may not be operated: A. By a person who does not possess a valid license of any class or a license specially endorsed to operate a motorcycle or a moped
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (wheels 10 in. or larger, electric motor under 1,500 W), motorized bicycle or tricycle (1.5 bhp or less, 25 mph or less), or motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device at or over 750 W, without operable pedals, or modified to assist above 20 mph (motor only) or 28 mph (pedaling) is not an e-bike. A moped (10 in. or larger wheels, pedals optional, electric motor under 1,500 W, automatic drive) needs a driver's license of any class or a moped or motorcycle endorsement (§ 1252(3)), and is barred from interstates and anywhere bicycles are prohibited. A 'motorized bicycle or tricycle' (motor of 1.5 bhp or less, 25 mph or less unassisted) is treated as a bicycle for § 2063 and capped at 20 mph (§ 2063(6)). Its license status was not verified. More powerful devices are motorcycles. Moped registration and minimum license age were not verified.

open_questions: The 'less than 750 watts' wording excludes exactly 750 W. Enforcement practice is unknown.

The Class 2 definition ('not capable of propelling the bicycle at a speed of 20 miles per hour') could be read as requiring a top motor speed under 20 mph. Verifier note: the better reading is that the motor stops at 20 mph, because § 2063(14)(C)(1) bars modifications letting the motor assist 'above the speed of' 20 mph when the bike is propelled by the motor alone. So a Class 2 label of 20 mph fits, and Class 2 is kept legal for riders 16 and over. This is not the South Carolina 'less than twenty' wording, but no Maine source settles it.
Riders under 16 may not operate Class 2 (throttle) e-bikes in Maine. Many secondary sources and the stale index wrongly say Class 3 only.
No 2025-2026 amendment was found. The Revisor's statutes (current through Oct 1, 2026, including the 132nd Legislature's Second Regular Session) show § 2063 last amended by PL 2021, c. 86.
Do 'motorized bicycle or tricycle' operators need a license? § 1252(3) names only mopeds and motorized scooters. Not resolved.
Municipal sidewalk rules and Acadia National Park e-bike rules were not verified.
ME.verifier_notes: 29-A § 101(22-B) ('less than 750 watts') and § 2063(14) match the Revisor's text (current through Oct 1, 2026), and § 2063(14)(H)(1) does bar riders under 16 from Class 2 as well as Class 3. No 2025 or 2026 amendment exists, so the only fix is a note that § 2063(14)(C) supports reading Class 2 as a 20 mph cutoff.

MI.name: Michigan

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a device upon which an individual may ride that satisfies all of the following: (a) The device is equipped with ... (ii) Fully operable pedals for human propulsion. (iii) An electric motor of not greater than 750 watts.
definition.motor_watts_basis: An electric motor of not greater than 750 watts.
definition.notes: Added by 2017 PA 139 (HB 4782), effective Jan 28, 2018. Requires a seat or saddle, operable pedals and a motor of 750 W or less. Class 2 is defined as a motor that propels the bike to no more than 20 mph whether or not the rider pedals. MCL 257.662a(3): a device is not an e-bike if the motor is modified so it no longer meets § 13e, or if the motor exceeds 750 W. Electric bicycles are excluded from 'motor vehicle' (MCL 257.33) and 'moped' (MCL 257.32b(2)). E-bike riders follow bicycle rules (MCL 257.662a(1)). No statewide minimum age or helmet rule for Class 1 or Class 2. MCL text read was compiled through PA 103 of 2026, and § 662a still shows only the 2017 enactment.

label_required.quote: Beginning on January 1, 2018, a manufacturer or distributor of electric bicycles offered for sale or distribution in this state shall permanently affix in a prominent location on the electric bicycle a label

min_age.quote: A class 3 electric bicycle shall not be operated by an individual less than 14 years of age. An individual less than 14 years of age may ride as a passenger
min_age.exceptions: Under 14 may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 designed for passengers.

helmet.quote: An individual less than 18 years of age who operates or rides as a passenger on a class 3 electric bicycle shall wear a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet

license_registration_insurance.quote: Motor vehicle does not include an electric bicycle.

where_allowed.quote: an individual may operate an electric bicycle on any part of a highway that is open to a bicycle, including, but not limited to, a lane designated for the exclusive use of bicycles and the shoulder.
where_allowed.roads: Any part of a highway open to bicycles, including the shoulder. Not allowed in a city that bans nonemergency motor vehicles (Mackinac Island) unless the city allows it, and not in Mackinac Island State Park without a permit (§ 662a(7)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 allowed on paved, crushed-limestone or similar linear trails and rail trails unless the managing agency regulates or bans it. Class 2 and Class 3 allowed on those trails ONLY if the managing agency authorizes it. Natural-surface nonmotorized trails are closed to all e-bikes unless the agency allows them.
