These trail rules do not apply on congressionally authorized trail systems (§ 662a(13)). DNR land use orders govern state land.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No e-bike-specific sidewalk rule. E-bikes follow bicycle rules (§ 662a(1)), and bicycles may use sidewalks unless an official traffic control device prohibits it (MCL 257.660c), with local ordinances able to restrict further.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Operator must be 14 or older. Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a helmet. Class 3 needs agency authorization for paved linear trails and rail trails.

local_authority.quote: A local authority or agency of this state having jurisdiction over a trail described in this subsection may regulate or prohibit the operation of a class 1 electric bicycle on that trail.
local_authority.details: Trail managers may ban or regulate Class 1, and must affirmatively authorize Class 2 and 3, after a public hearing (§ 662a(12)). MCL 257.606(1)(h) lets local authorities engage in 'Regulating the operation of bicycles and requiring the registration and licensing of bicycles' on their streets, and e-bike riders follow bicycle rules. No statute expressly grants or preempts a local e-bike minimum age, so local age rules may exist and are not modeled.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Moped" means a 2- or 3-wheeled vehicle ... equipped with a motor that does not exceed 100 cubic centimeters piston displacement and cannot propel the vehicle at a speed greater than 30 miles per hour on a level surface.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped if it cannot exceed 30 mph and needs no gear shifting. Otherwise motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device over 750 W, without pedals, or modified beyond the § 13e classes is not an e-bike (§ 662a(3)). If it tops out at 30 mph or less with no gear shifting it is a moped: operator needs a driver's license or a special restricted moped license, available at age 15 (MCL 257.312a(2)), and riders under 19 must wear a crash helmet (MCL 257.658(4)). Mopeds are motor vehicles subject to registration (no title needed per MCL 257.216(1)(k)). I did not confirm insurance rules for mopeds. A device faster than 30 mph is a motorcycle needing a motorcycle endorsement (MCL 257.312a(1)), registration and insurance. The 100 cc test does not map cleanly onto electric motors.

pending_changes.signed: no (introduced 9/10/2026, referred to Senate Transportation and Infrastructure)
pending_changes.summary: Amends MCL 257.662a to regulate e-bike use by minors. News reports say it would bar under-14 riders and require parental permission and helmets for ages 14-17. Text not read.

pending_changes.signed: no (introduced 7/3/2026, referred to House Transportation and Infrastructure)
pending_changes.summary: Special operator's license requirements for certain electric mobility devices. Amends MCL 257.32b, 33, 312a, 657, 658, 660, 660d, 661, 662 and 662a. News reports say it adds a helmet rule for under-18 Class 2 riders. Text not read.

pending_changes.signed: no (introduced 9/23/2026, referred to House Transportation and Infrastructure)
pending_changes.summary: New act requiring e-bikes and components to meet certification standards.

open_questions: Three 2026 bills (SB 1156, HB 6165/6166, HB 6339) could add youth age limits, Class 2 helmet rules or licensing in the lame-duck session after the November 2026 election. Re-check before launch.
Sidewalk use depends on local ordinances and signs. Many Michigan cities ban bicycles, and so e-bikes, on downtown sidewalks.
Moped insurance and registration specifics were not verified in statute text.
DNR land use orders for state trails (reported to allow only Class 1, and Class 2 by permit, on some trails) were not read.
MI.verifier_notes: All quotes match MCL (complete through PA 103 of 2026), and public acts through PA 114 of 2026 include no e-bike change. SB 1156, HB 6165, HB 6166 and HB 6339 are all still in committee.

MN.name: Minnesota

definition.quote: "Electric-assisted bicycle" means a bicycle with two or three wheels that: (1) has a saddle and fully operable pedals for human propulsion; ... (3) is equipped with an electric motor that has a power output of not more than 750 watts
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor that has a power output of not more than 750 watts
definition.notes: Read in the 2025 Minnesota Statutes (revisor shows no 2025 or 2026 change to these subdivisions). Subd. 27 also requires CPSC 16 CFR 1512 compliance, a battery or drive system tested to a safety standard by a third-party lab, and fitting a class 1, 2, 3 or 'multiple mode' class. Subd. 27(b)-(c), added by Laws 2024 c 127 art 3 s 40 (no special effective date, so Aug 1, 2024 by default), says a vehicle is NOT an e-bike if it is designed or intended to be configured or modified (switch, button, app, motor change) to exceed its class. Multiple-mode bikes with a throttle may not exceed 20 mph on throttle (§ 169.222, subd. 6b(e)). An e-bike is a 'bicycle' (subd. 4) and is not a 'motor vehicle' (subd. 42) or 'motorized bicycle' (subd. 45). Minimum age 15 applies to ALL classes. No helmet law for e-bikes or bicycles at any age. Sellers must give written disclosures and may not label motorized bicycles or motorcycles as e-bikes (Laws 2024 c 127 art 3, consumer section).

label_required.quote: The manufacturer or distributor of an electric-assisted bicycle must apply a label to the bicycle that is permanently affixed in a prominent location. The label must contain the class number, top assisted speed, and motor wattage

min_age.quote: A person under the age of 15 must not operate an electric-assisted bicycle.
min_age.exceptions: None in statute. Applies to operating, not riding as a passenger. The age-15 rule predates the 2021 three-class law and was reworded in 2024.

license_registration_insurance.quote: Motor vehicle does not include an electric-assisted bicycle, an electric personal assistive mobility device, or a vehicle moved solely by human power.

where_allowed.quote: A person may operate an electric-assisted bicycle in the same manner as provided for operation of other bicycles, including but not limited to operation on the shoulder of a roadway, a bicycle lane, and a bicycle route
where_allowed.roads: Same as bicycles, including shoulders and bicycle routes.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 and 2 may use bicycle paths, bicycle trails and shared use paths with the motor engaged unless restricted under § 85.015 subd. 1d (state trails), § 85.018 subd. 2(d) (local trails) or § 160.263 subd. 2(b) (bikeways). Any e-bike may use a bikeway or bicycle trail with the motor off. Natural-surface nonmotorized trails and bike parks may be regulated by the managing agency.
where_allowed.sidewalks: E-bikes are bicycles, so bicycle sidewalk rules apply: not on sidewalks in a business district unless local authorities permit it, and local authorities may ban bicycles on any sidewalk (§ 169.222, subd. 4(d)). Must yield to pedestrians.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Class 3 and multiple-mode bikes may use bicycle paths, trails and shared use paths with the motor engaged unless the local authority or state agency prohibits it (§ 169.222, subd. 6a(c)). Class 3 must have a speedometer.

local_authority.quote: A governing body may not prohibit or otherwise restrict operation of an electric-assisted bicycle ... on any bikeway, roadway, or shoulder, unless the governing body determines that operation of the electric-assisted bicycle is not consistent with (1) the safety
local_authority.details: Local governments may restrict e-bikes on bikeways, roadways, shoulders and local trails only after finding a safety or general-welfare conflict (or a property conveyance term). They may ban bicycles, and so e-bikes, on sidewalks, and may ban Class 3 on paths. The statute does not expressly authorize or forbid a local minimum age above 15. Some cities may have local e-bike ordinances that the app does not model.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Motorized bicycle" means a bicycle that is propelled by an electric or a liquid fuel motor of ... a maximum of two brake horsepower, which is capable of a maximum speed of not more than 30 miles per hour
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorized bicycle (up to 2 bhp and 30 mph) or, if faster or more powerful, motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A bike over 750 W, without operable pedals and a saddle, or built or sold to be unlocked past its class, is not an e-bike (§ 169.011, subd. 27(b)). If it is limited to about 2 bhp (about 1,491 W) and 30 mph it is a motorized bicycle: needs a driver's license or a motorized bicycle operator's permit or instruction permit, available at age 15 after an exam or safety course (§ 171.02, subd. 3). Helmet required for operators under 18 (§ 169.223, subds. 1-2). No sidewalk riding (subd. 3). Not allowed on bicycle paths or lanes reserved for nonmotorized traffic (subd. 5(c)). Faster devices (e-motos) are motorcycles needing a motorcycle endorsement, registration and insurance. Motorized bicycle registration and insurance rules were not read in statute.

pending_changes.signed: no. HF 3785's motion to suspend the rules failed 65-68 on May 16, 2026, SF 4186 stayed in Senate Rules, and both died when the 2025-2026 biennium ended
pending_changes.summary: Would have clarified that e-motos are not e-bikes. Late amendments added a helmet mandate for ages 15-18, local 20 mph business-district limits and a DPS position. Not enacted. BikeMN warns the amendments are being shared online as if they were law.

pending_changes.signed: no. Passed the Senate 34-33 on May 15, 2026, was referred to a House committee on May 16, 2026, and died when the biennium ended
pending_changes.summary: Would require helmets for e-bike riders under 18.

open_questions: Police and city posts in 2026 cite a helmet rule for e-bike riders 15 to 18 that never passed. The app should say no helmet law, and may want to warn users about this misinformation.
Effective date of the 2024 definition and equipment changes is assumed to be Aug 1, 2024 (Minnesota default for sections without an effective-date line). Not confirmed against a revisor note.
Motorized bicycle registration and insurance requirements were not read in statute.
City-level e-bike ordinances (age limits above 15, trail bans) were not surveyed.
MN.verifier_notes: All quotes match the 2025 Minnesota Statutes, and no 2025 or 2026 session law touched the e-bike subdivisions. Both pending bills died, and their sources now point to the revisor bill status pages.

MO.name: Missouri

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle", a bicycle equipped with fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat for the rider, and an electric motor of less than 750 watts that meets the requirements of one of the following three classes
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than 750 watts
definition.notes: The watt limit is strict. 'Less than 750 watts' means a bike labeled exactly 750 W does NOT qualify. max_motor_watts holds the statute's number (750) and motor_watts_comparison 'less_than' carries the strict test. Added by 2021 SB 176, effective Aug 28, 2021. Definition read in the § 301.010 version effective Aug 28, 2025. § 307.194 shows no version after 2021, and no 2025 or 2026 act touches e-bikes. Electric bicycles are excluded from 'motor vehicle', 'motorized bicycle', 'motortricycle', 'motorcycle' and 'vehicle' in § 301.010. § 307.194.6 says the motor must cut off 'when the rider stops pedaling or when the brakes are applied'. Class 2 still qualifies, because § 301.010(15)(b) lets a Class 2 motor 'be used exclusively to propel the bicycle' and § 307.194.6 is a separate operating rule. E-bikes must meet CPSC 16 CFR 1512 (§ 307.194.5). No statewide helmet rule and no minimum age for Class 1 or 2. Kansas City Ordinance 260508 (July 2026, per news) adds a helmet rule for riders under 18 inside Kansas City.

label_required.quote: Beginning August 28, 2021, manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall apply a permanent label to each electric bicycle.

min_age.quote: No person under sixteen years of age shall operate a class 3 electric bicycle. A person under sixteen years of age may ride as a passenger on a class 3 electric bicycle that is designed to accommodate passengers
min_age.exceptions: Under 16 may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 designed for passengers.

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric bicycle or a person operating an electric bicycle is not subject to provisions of law that are applicable to motor vehicles ... including vehicle registration, certificates of title, drivers' licenses, and financial responsibility.

where_allowed.quote: An electric bicycle may be ridden where bicycles are permitted to travel, subject to the following provisions: (1) An electric bicycle may be ridden on bicycle or multi-use paths where bicycles are permitted
where_allowed.roads: Where bicycles may travel, with all bicycle rights and duties (§ 307.194.1).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Bicycle and multi-use paths allowed where bicycles are. After notice and a public hearing, the agency with jurisdiction may ban Class 1 or 2 on a path for safety or legal reasons. Natural-surface nonmotorized trails may be regulated by the agency.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No e-bike sidewalk rule in § 307.194. E-bikes have bicycle rights and duties. § 300.347 (model traffic ordinance, which applies where a city adopts it) bars bicycles from sidewalks in business districts and bars motorized bicycles from sidewalks. Cities may set their own rules.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Operator must be 16 or older. Path managers may ban Class 3 from a path with no hearing requirement. Class 3 needs a speedometer.

local_authority.quote: A municipality, local authority, or state agency having jurisdiction over a bicycle or multi-use path may prohibit the operation of a class 3 electric bicycle on that path
local_authority.details: Statute gives path-level bans (Class 1 and 2 after notice, hearing and finding. Class 3 without). Cities also adopt their own e-bike ordinances: Kansas City Ordinance 260508 (passed late July 2026, per Hoodline news) requires helmets for riders under 18 and limits e-motos, and several St. Louis suburbs adopted e-bike rules in 2026 (per news). I did not read the ordinances or find a statute that expressly authorizes or preempts local age or helmet rules.

non_ebike_devices.quote: No person shall operate a motorized bicycle on any highway or street in this state unless the person has a valid license to operate a motor vehicle.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorized bicycle (50 cc or less, under 3 gross bhp, 30 mph or less, automatic) or, if bigger or faster, motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A pedal bike at or over 750 W, a bike with no pedals, or one outside the three classes is not an e-bike. If it is under 3 gross bhp (about 2,237 W) and 30 mph or less with an automatic transmission it is a motorized bicycle (§ 301.010(39)): needs a valid driver's license (§ 307.195.1), barred from interstates and, under § 300.347, from sidewalks. The minimum driver's license age was not read in statute, so min_age is null. Faster or more powerful devices (e-motos, electric dirt bikes) are motorcycles needing a motorcycle license or endorsement, registration and insurance. A motorized bicycle is treated as a motor vehicle for homeowners' or renters' insurance (§ 307.180(2)).

open_questions: Resolved by verifier. Class 2 throttle bikes qualify. § 301.010(15)(b) defines Class 2 as a motor that 'may be used exclusively to propel the bicycle', and the cut-off rule in § 307.194.6 does not change that. It sits in a separate operating section, so it does not take Class 2 out of the definition. Read with that definition, a brake cut-off satisfies it. A literal reading leaves a small equipment-citation risk, so no caution is set.
Local ordinances are active in 2026 (Kansas City helmet rule for under 18, St. Louis suburbs). The app may give a wrong answer for riders in those cities unless local rules are added.

Resolved by verifier. The Senate's 2025 and 2026 'Truly Agreed To and Finally Passed' lists, the House bill lists for both years and the revisor's Recent Sections list, which also shows delayed-date sections, contain no e-bike act. § 307.194 is still the 2021 version and § 301.010 the Aug 28, 2025 version.
Missouri driver's license minimum age (needed for motorized bicycles) was not read in statute.

MO.verifier_notes: Statute text matches revisor.mo.gov and no 2025 or 2026 e-bike act exists. Class 2 still qualifies despite the stops-pedaling rule in § 307.194.6, so no caution was added and three notes were updated.

MS.name: Mississippi

definition.citation: Miss. Code Ann. § 63-3-103(l) (as amended by 2021 HB 1195, § 6)
definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a bicycle or tricycle equipped with fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat for the rider, and an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty (750) watts
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty (750) watts
definition.notes: The watt limit is strict. The statute says 'less than' 750 W, so a bike labeled exactly 750 W does NOT qualify. max_motor_watts holds the statute's number (750) and motor_watts_comparison 'less_than' carries the strict test. The classes are Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 with a motor that 'may be used exclusively to propel the bicycle' and stops at 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph. Enacted by 2021 HB 1195 (signed Mar 17, 2021, effective July 1, 2021), creating § 63-3-1315. 2023 HB 1003 (approved Mar 28, 2023) brought § 63-3-103 forward with the same e-bike definition, still lettered (l), and no enacted 2024 to 2026 bill touches § 63-3-103 or § 63-3-1315. An e-bike is a vehicle to the same extent as a bicycle and is not a motor vehicle, motorcycle or motor scooter. § 63-3-1315(6) says the motor must cut off 'when the rider stops pedaling or when the brakes are applied'. Class 2 still qualifies, because that separate operating rule does not change the definition. E-bikes must meet CPSC 16 CFR 1512. Class 3 needs a speedometer. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2. No helmet rule in the e-bike statute.

label_required.quote: On and after January 1, 2022, manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each electric bicycle.

min_age.quote: No person under the age of sixteen (16) may operate a class 3 electric bicycle. A person under the age of sixteen (16) may ride as a passenger on a class 3 electric bicycle that is designed to accommodate passengers.
min_age.exceptions: Under 16 may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 designed for passengers. Applies everywhere, not only on highways.

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric bicycle or a person operating an electric bicycle is not subject to the provisions of this code relating to financial responsibility, driver's licenses, registration, certificates of title ... and license plates. An electric bicycle is not a motor vehicle.

where_allowed.quote: An electric bicycle may be ridden in places where bicycles are permitted, including but not limited to, streets, highways, roadways, bicycle lanes, and bicycle or multi-use paths.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed wherever bicycles are allowed, including streets, highways and roadways.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Bicycle and multi-use paths allowed. After notice and a public hearing, the agency with jurisdiction may ban Class 1 or 2 from a path if needed for safety or legal compliance. Natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized may be regulated by the agency.
where_allowed.sidewalks: Not addressed in § 63-3-1315. § 21-37-3(2) says § 63-3-1315 governs e-bikes on sidewalks, and § 63-3-1315(7) allows e-bikes where bicycles are permitted, so sidewalk use follows local bicycle rules. Treat as unclear.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Operator must be 16 or older. Path managers may ban Class 3 from a path without the notice-and-hearing step. Class 3 must have a speedometer.

local_authority.quote: A municipality, local authority or state agency having jurisdiction over a bicycle or multi-use path may prohibit the operation of a class 3 electric bicycle on that path.
local_authority.details: Path-level bans only: Class 1 and 2 bans need notice, a public hearing and a safety or legal finding. Class 3 bans need neither. Natural-surface trails may be regulated. No statute found that lets locals set a different minimum age. Municipalities keep general jurisdiction over streets and sidewalks (§ 21-37-3(1)), but § 21-37-3(2) points e-bike street and sidewalk rules to § 63-3-1315.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Motorcycle" means every motor vehicle having a saddle for the use of the rider and designed to travel on not more than three (3) wheels in contact with the ground but excluding a tractor.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorcycle (self-propelled two- or three-wheeler with a saddle), which includes motor scooters
non_ebike_devices.notes: A bike at or over 750 W, without pedals or a seat, or outside the three classes is not an e-bike, and a self-propelled vehicle is a 'motor vehicle' (§ 63-3-103(b)). With a saddle and up to three wheels it falls under 'motorcycle', which includes motor scooters. Mississippi DPS says operating a motorcycle or motor scooter needs a driver's license with a motorcycle endorsement, and that the motorcycle learner's permit starts at age 15. I did not read the licensing statute, so min_age is null. Registration, title and insurance would likely apply as for motorcycles.

open_questions: Partly resolved by verifier. The Lexis public-access table of contents lists § 63-3-1315 'Electric bicycles' in Article 27, but the section text sits behind a CAPTCHA, and Justia and FindLaw block automated reads. The latest enactment of § 63-3-103 (2023 HB 1003) repeats the 2021 definition word for word, and a scan of 259 enacted 2024 to 2026 vehicle, traffic and local bills found none that amends § 63-3-103 or § 63-3-1315. A person can open the Lexis page by hand to confirm.

Resolved by verifier. Class 2 throttle bikes qualify. § 63-3-103(l)(ii) defines Class 2 as a motor that 'may be used exclusively to propel the bicycle', and the cut-off rule in § 63-3-1315(6) does not change that. It sits in a separate operating section, so it does not take Class 2 out of the definition. Read with that definition, a brake cut-off satisfies it. A literal reading leaves a small equipment-citation risk, so no caution is set. Enforcement practice is still unknown.
No statewide bicycle helmet law was found, but I did not search the whole code.
Motorcycle license age and moped rules come from DPS pages, not statute.
Sidewalk riding is unclear and depends on local ordinances.

MT.name: Montana

definition.quote: "Electrically assisted bicycle" means a vehicle on which a person may ride that has two tandem wheels and an electric motor capable of propelling the vehicle and a rider who weighs 170 pounds no faster than 20 miles an hour
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor capable of propelling the vehicle and a rider who weighs 170 pounds no faster than 20 miles an hour
definition.notes: NO THREE-CLASS LAW. Montana Code Annotated 2025, the current edition (the Legislature next meets in 2027), uses one speed-based definition: two tandem wheels and a motor that cannot push a 170 lb rider past 20 mph on a paved level surface. No watt cap and no pedal requirement in the definition. 'Bicycle' includes an electrically assisted bicycle (61-8-102(2)), and bicycles are not motor vehicles (61-1-101). So Class 1 and Class 2 bikes (20 mph) are bicycles. A Class 3 bike (28 mph) is NOT an electrically assisted bicycle. If it has pedals, a motor of 2 bhp or less, and cannot exceed 30 mph unassisted, it is a 'moped' (61-8-102(14)). Three-wheeled e-trikes do not meet the 'two tandem wheels' test and were not traced. 2023 HB 261 and 2025 SB 387 tried to add a three-class system and did not pass. No statewide minimum age or helmet rule for e-assisted bicycles. No label requirement found.

label_required.citation: MCA 61-8-102(7) (no label provision found in Title 61)
label_required.quote: "Electrically assisted bicycle" means a vehicle on which a person may ride that has two tandem wheels and an electric motor

license_registration_insurance.quote: The term does not include a bicycle, a motorized scooter, or a moped as defined in 61-8-102

where_allowed.quote: A person may not ride a bicycle, moped, or motorized scooter on and along a sidewalk ... where the use of a bicycle, moped, or motorized scooter is prohibited by official traffic control devices.
where_allowed.roads: As a bicycle: roadways and paved shoulders (61-8-605), with the rights and duties of a vehicle driver (61-8-602).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Bicycle rules apply on paths set aside for bicycles (61-8-601(2)(b)). No e-bike-specific path rule in statute. Land managers (state parks, federal lands) set their own trail rules.
where_allowed.sidewalks: Allowed unless official traffic control devices prohibit it (61-8-608(2)), yielding to pedestrians. Cities may regulate further under 61-12-101(1)(h).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: No Class 3 category. A 28 mph bike is likely a moped: may NOT be ridden under power on sidewalks or bicycle paths (61-8-608(3)(b)), may use highways, bike lanes and shoulders under power (61-8-608(3)(c)), and riders under 18 must wear a helmet on streets and highways (61-9-417).

local_authority.quote: regulating the operation of bicycles or mopeds, as defined in 61-8-102, and requiring the registration and licensing of bicycles or mopeds, including requiring a registration fee
local_authority.details: Local authorities may regulate the operation of bicycles (which include e-assisted bicycles) and mopeds on sidewalks, streets and highways under their jurisdiction, and may require registration and a fee. No statute caps what that regulation can include, so local age limits or sidewalk bans are possible. City ordinances (for example Missoula or Bozeman) were not surveyed.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Moped" means a vehicle equipped with two or three wheels, foot pedals to permit muscular propulsion, and an independent power source providing a maximum of 2 brake horsepower.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (pedals, 2 bhp or less, 30 mph or less unassisted, automatic drive) or motorized scooter (no seat). Otherwise motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: Mopeds and motorized scooters are excluded from 'motor vehicle' (61-1-101(41)(b)), so the driver's license requirement in 61-5-102 does not reach them and no state registration applies (local registration is possible under 61-12-101). Mopeds may not run under power on sidewalks or bicycle paths, and riders and passengers under 18 must wear headgear on streets and highways (61-9-417(1)). Motorized scooter rules were revised by 2025 HB 588 (Ch. 693). A seated, throttle-only device with no pedals that tops 20 mph is neither an e-assisted bicycle nor a moped and is likely a motorcycle needing a license with a motorcycle endorsement, registration and insurance.

open_questions: Montana's definition has no watt cap or pedal requirement, so a throttle-only electric motorbike limited to 20 mph would legally be a 'bicycle'. The app should not call a high-watt bike illegal in Montana on wattage alone, but should treat any bike that can exceed 20 mph on motor power as not an e-bike.
How Montana treats e-trikes (three wheels) is unclear, because the definition requires 'two tandem wheels'.
The effective date of the current e-assisted bicycle definition was not traced to a session law.
The Montana Legislature next meets in January 2027. Watch for a revived three-class bill.

verdict_cautions.reason: Montana's definition caps the motor at 20 mph. A Class 3 bike is likely a moped (no power on sidewalks or bike paths, helmet under 18).

MT.verifier_notes: All quotes match MCA 2025, and SB 387 (2025) failed, so the single 20 mph rule with no watt cap stands. The Class 3 'not an e-bike' caution is confirmed.

NC.name: North Carolina
NC.has_three_class_law_notes: NC has a single 'electric assisted bicycle' category (750 W, 20 mph on motor power alone). Those stand-alone bills stalled, but the same three-class definition, a Class 3 helmet rule for riders under 18 and new city and county e-bike powers were enacted in HB 1094 (S.L. 2026-46, section 19, approved July 7, 2026), effective Dec 1, 2026. Until then the single category applies. UNC School of Government (Nov 5, 2025) reads a 28 mph class 3 bike as a moped under current law.

definition.quote: fully operable pedals for human propulsion, and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, whose maximum speed on a level surface when powered solely by such a motor is no greater than 20 miles per hour.
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of no more than 750 watts
definition.notes: The definition does not separate throttle from pedal assist, so class 1 and class 2 (750 W or less, 20 mph) fit. Class 3 (28 mph assist) is not recognized. UNC SOG treats it as a moped. E-bikes are excluded from 'motor vehicle' (20-4.01(23)) and 'moped' (20-4.01(27)j), and are deemed vehicles whose riders have driver duties (20-4.01(49)). The section's history notes end at S.L. 2024-30, and no 2025 or 2026 amendment was found.

label_required.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. Chapter 20 (no label provision)
label_required.quote: Electric Assisted Bicycle. - A bicycle with two or three wheels that is equipped with a seat or saddle
label_required.notes: A full-text search of Chapter 20 for 'electric assisted bicycle' found only the definitions, the motor vehicle, motorcycle, moped and vehicle exclusions, and 20-171.1. There is no label mandate. Labels would be added by pending SB 576, HB 1084 and SB 970 (not verified in their text).

min_age.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 20-10.1 (mopeds), applied to class 3 per UNC SOG reading
min_age.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person who is under the age of 16 years to operate a moped as defined in G.S. 20-4.01(27)j. upon any highway or public vehicular area of this State.
min_age.exceptions: Applies only if the class 3 bike is a moped, which is UNC SOG's reading and not an express statute. No state minimum age applies to a compliant electric assisted bicycle (class 1 or 2): a full-text search of Chapter 20 found no age rule for e-bikes.

NC.min_age_notes: There is no minimum age for class 1 or class 2. Secondary sites disagree on this (some claim 16), but no such statute exists in current Chapter 20.

helmet.quote: It shall be unlawful for any parent or legal guardian of a person below the age of 16 to knowingly permit that person to operate or be a passenger on a bicycle unless
helmet.notes: Unclear whether this covers e-bikes. 20-171.8 defines 'bicycle' for this Article as 'a human-powered vehicle', but 20-4.01(7a) defines an e-bike as 'A bicycle' and Part 10A (20-171.1) includes e-bikes. Recorded conservatively as applying to class 1 and class 2. The duty falls on the parent, with a fine up to $10.

helmet.quote: It shall be unlawful for any parent or legal guardian of a person below the age of 16 to knowingly permit that person to operate or be a passenger on a bicycle unless
helmet.notes: Same uncertainty as class_1.

helmet.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 20-140.4(a)(2) (mopeds), applied to class 3 per UNC SOG reading
helmet.quote: Unless the operator and all passengers thereon wear on their heads, with a retention strap properly secured, safety helmets of a type that complies with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) 218.
helmet.notes: Moped helmet rule (a DOT motorcycle-type helmet). Applies only if class 3 is a moped.

license_registration_insurance.quote: Except as specifically provided otherwise, this term shall not include mopeds or electric assisted bicycles.
license_registration_insurance.notes: The quote is from the 'motor vehicle' definition. UNC SOG (Nov 2025) confirms compliant e-bikes need no license, registration or insurance. If class 3 is a moped, it needs DMV registration (20-53.4) and liability insurance (20-309(a)) but no driver license. Those moped sections were not read directly.

where_allowed.quote: every rider of a bicycle or an electric assisted bicycle upon a highway shall be subject to the provisions of this Chapter applicable to the driver of a vehicle
where_allowed.roads: Allowed on highways with the rights and duties of a vehicle driver. Bicycle rules in Part 10A include e-bikes (20-171.1).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: No state statute addresses this. Treated as bicycles.
where_allowed.paths_trails: No state statute. Set by the managing agency and local ordinance.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No state statute for bicycles or e-bikes (20-160(b) bans only motor vehicles on sidewalks). Cities may regulate sidewalks (160A-296, 160A-300).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Class 3 (28 mph) is treated as a moped: age 16, helmet, registration, insurance.

local_authority.quote: A city may by ordinance prohibit, regulate, divert, control, and limit pedestrian or vehicular traffic upon the public streets, sidewalks, alleys, and bridges of the city.
local_authority.details: This is general city traffic power, not e-bike-specific. Express e-bike local authority (class restrictions on paths and sidewalks, greenway speed limits, helmet rules for class 1 and 2) comes from new G.S. 160A-300.2 and 153A-245.1 (S.L. 2026-46, section 19), effective Dec 1, 2026. Whether current power extends to age limits is unclear.

non_ebike_devices.quote: Moped. - A vehicle, other than a motor-driven bicycle or electric assisted bicycle, that has two or three wheels, no external shifting device, a motor that does not exceed 50 cubic centimeters piston displacement
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (up to 30 mph) or motor-driven bicycle / motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A moped needs age 16, a helmet, registration and insurance, but no driver license. Over 30 mph it is a motorcycle and needs a license with a motorcycle endorsement. CONFLICT: 20-4.01(27)i defines 'motor-driven bicycle' (pedals, motor that cannot exceed 20 mph, not an e-bike), and (27)h lists motor-driven bicycles as MOTORCYCLES. So a pedal bike over 750 W capped at 20 mph may be a motorcycle, not a moped as UNC SOG says. Treat any over-750 W bike as not legal as an e-bike.

pending_changes.bill: SB 576 (2025-2026), E-Bike Definition and Local Regulation
pending_changes.summary: Would adopt three classes (20/20/28 mph), allow e-bikes on roads, bike lanes and shared-use paths, require helmets for class 3, and add G.S. 160A-300.2 local authority. Committee substitute adopted May 6, 2025, then re-referred to Senate Transportation. No further action.
Similar three-class bill with a class 3 helmet rule for riders under 18 (per secondary summary). Filed Apr 28, 2026 and referred to House Appropriations Apr 30, 2026.

pending_changes.bill: SB 970 (2025-2026), E-Bike Definition and Local Regulation
pending_changes.summary: Senate version filed Apr 30, 2026 and referred to Senate Rules May 4, 2026.

pending_changes.bill: HB 1094, S.L. 2026-46, section 19 (Clarify the Definition of Electric Assisted Bicycle and Authorize Local Government Regulation)
pending_changes.summary: Rewrites G.S. 20-4.01(7a): an e-bike has a seat, operable pedals and a motor of no more than 750 W and meets one of three classes (Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph). The old 'no greater than 20 mph on motor alone' test is struck, so a Class 3 bike becomes an e-bike, not a moped. New G.S. 20-171.3: e-bikes may use all roadways, bicycle lanes and multiuse paths, and riders and passengers under 18 on a Class 3 must wear a helmet. New G.S. 160A-300.2 and 153A-245.1: cities and counties may regulate e-bikes on multiuse paths and sidewalks, restrict classes, set speed limits and require helmets for riders and passengers under 18 on Class 1 and 2. No state minimum age is added. Applies to offenses on or after Dec 1, 2026.

open_questions: Is a class 3 (28 mph pedal-assist, no throttle) bike an electric assisted bicycle? The definition limits speed 'when powered solely by such a motor'. UNC SOG says it is a moped, but no court or DMV ruling was found.
Does the under-16 bicycle helmet law (20-171.9) cover e-bikes? Its Article defines bicycle as 'human-powered'.
Is an over-750 W pedal bike capped at 20 mph a moped or a 'motor-driven bicycle' (motorcycle)? The statute text and UNC SOG point different ways.
Moped registration (20-53.4) and insurance (20-309) sections were not read directly.
Resolved by verifier: the stand-alone bills did not move, but HB 1094 (S.L. 2026-46) enacted the three-class change effective Dec 1, 2026. The engine needs a date switch on that day.

verdict_cautions.reason: Until Dec 1, 2026 the definition requires 20 mph or less on motor power alone, and UNC SOG reads a 28 mph Class 3 as a moped (16+, helmet, registration, insurance). S.L. 2026-46 makes Class 3 an e-bike from Dec 1, 2026.

NC.verifier_notes: Agent missed S.L. 2026-46 (HB 1094), which adopts three classes from Dec 1, 2026. Added as a pending change.

ND.name: North Dakota
ND.has_three_class_law_notes: HB 1148 (2021) took effect Aug 1, 2021, with labels from Jan 1, 2022. No 2023 or 2025 amendment was found. Current Century Code text was read on ndlegis.gov.

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a bicycle equipped with fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat for the rider, and an electric motor of seven hundred fifty or fewer watts which meets the requirements of one of the following three classes:
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of seven hundred fifty or fewer watts
definition.notes: 'Bicycle' (39-01-01(3)) includes electric bicycles. E-bikes are excluded from 'motor vehicle' (47), 'motorcycle' (48), 'motorized bicycle' (49), 'motor-powered recreational vehicle' (50), 'recreational vehicle' (71) and 'vehicle' (104). Equipment must meet 16 CFR 1512. 39-10.1-09(3) requires equipment so the motor 'can be disengaged or cease to function' when the rider stops pedaling or the brakes are applied. Because it says 'can', a Class 2 throttle bike complies, and Class 2 is defined as a motor 'capable of propelling the bicycle without the individual pedaling'. The watt test is 'seven hundred fifty or fewer watts', which means 750 W or less.

label_required.quote: Beginning January 1, 2022, any person that manufacturers or distributes an electric bicycle in this state shall affix a permanent label to the electric bicycle

ND.min_age_notes: No minimum operator age for any class. Chapter 39-10.1 and the definitions were read in full and contain no e-bike age rule. Under-18 riders may ride class 3 but must wear a helmet.

helmet.quote: An individual under the age of eighteen may not operate a class 3 electric bicycle unless the individual is wearing a safety helmet.

ND.helmet_notes: No helmet rule for class 1 or class 2, and no general bicycle helmet law in chapter 39-10.1.

license_registration_insurance.quote: for purposes of motor vehicle registration, title registration, and operator's licenses, motorized bicycles. The term does not include a snowmobile as defined in section 39-24-01, an electric bicycle, or a multipassenger bicycle.
license_registration_insurance.notes: E-bikes are excluded from 'motor vehicle' and 'vehicle', so registration, licensing and insurance rules for motor vehicles do not apply. Bicycle violations, including on e-bikes, add no license points (39-10.1-08).

where_allowed.quote: Unless otherwise prohibited by a governmental entity having jurisdiction, an individual may operate an electric bicycle on any bicycle path or multi-use path.
where_allowed.roads: E-bikes are bicycles. Riders have the rights and duties of drivers on roadways (39-10.1-02), must ride as far right as practicable, and may ride no more than two abreast (39-10.1-05).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Not separately addressed. Bicycle rules apply.
where_allowed.paths_trails: All classes are allowed on bicycle and multi-use paths unless the governing entity prohibits them.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No state statute found in chapters 39-10 or 39-10.1. Set by city ordinance.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: A working speedometer is required (39-10.1-09(6)). Riders under 18 need a helmet. No path restriction beyond local bans.

local_authority.quote: Unless otherwise prohibited by a governmental entity having jurisdiction, an individual may operate an electric bicycle on any bicycle path or multi-use path.
local_authority.details: Governmental entities may prohibit e-bikes on bicycle and multi-use paths. General city police powers (Title 40) were not reviewed, so local age limits are unconfirmed.

non_ebike_devices.quote: a power source providing up to a maximum of two brake horsepower having a maximum piston or rotor displacement of 3.05 cubic inches [49.98 milliliters] if a combustion engine is used
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorized bicycle (up to 2 bhp, up to 30 mph), otherwise motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A motorized bicycle counts as a motor vehicle for registration, title and operator's licenses (39-01-01(47)). It needs an operator's license or a motorized bicycle operator's permit, which is issued from age 14 after a written test (39-06-14.1(3)). An e-bike over 750 W, faster than the class limits or with no pedals (pedals or footrests allowed for motorized bicycles) and up to 30 mph is likely a motorized bicycle. Faster devices are likely motorcycles (class M license). Insurance for motorized bicycles was not verified.

open_questions: Resolved by verifier. The chapter 39-01, 39-06 and 39-10.1 PDFs on ndlegis.gov were generated June 30, 2025, after the 2025 session, and the Legislative Assembly holds no regular session in 2026. No 2025 change to the e-bike text was found.
Sidewalk riding is not addressed in state law. Check major-city ordinances (Fargo, Bismarck) if needed.
Insurance and registration specifics for motorized bicycles were not verified.
Whether cities may set e-bike age limits (Title 40 police powers) was not checked.
ND.verifier_notes: The statute says 'seven hundred fifty or fewer watts', so at_most is right, and the Century Code PDFs date from June 30, 2025. The cut-off rule says the motor 'can be disengaged', so Class 2 is unaffected.

NE.name: Nebraska

definition.quote: Class III electric bicycle means a device with ... (3) Fully operative pedals for propulsion by human power; and (4) An electric motor: (a) Not exceeding seven hundred fifty watts of power; (b) That produces no more than one brake horsepower
definition.motor_watts_basis: (a) Not exceeding seven hundred fifty watts of power; (b) That produces no more than one brake horsepower
definition.notes: Three classes created by Laws 2023, LB 138 §§ 37-41 (approved June 1, 2023). LB 138 § 57 makes those sections operative three calendar months after the session adjourned on June 1, 2023, and the Legislature's 2023 cross-reference table lists that date as Sept 2, 2023. Each class needs 2, 3 or 4 wheels, a saddle or seat, fully operative pedals, and a motor of 750 W or less that also produces no more than 1 bhp. The motor list ends with 'and', so both caps apply. 1 bhp is about 745.7 W, so a 746 to 750 W label fails the literal horsepower test even though the watt clause allows 750 W. Reading the horsepower clause as binding would make the 750 W clause pointless, and federal law equates 750 W with 1 h.p., so such labels stay 'unclear'. Class I pedal assist to 20 mph, Class II power whether or not pedaling to 20 mph, Class III pedal assist to 28 mph. 'Bicycle' includes an electric bicycle (§ 60-611), and electric bicycles are excluded from 'motor-driven cycle' (§ 60-640). Nebraska adopted only the definitions. No label rule, Class 3 age limit, Class 3 path rule, speedometer rule or helmet rule was found. Nebraska did not appear in the PeopleForBikes index.

label_required.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-618.03 (no label provision found in LB 138 or Chapter 60 index)
label_required.quote: Electric bicycle means a Class I electric bicycle, a Class II electric bicycle, and a Class III electric bicycle.

license_registration_insurance.quote: Motor-driven cycle means every motorcycle, including every motor scooter, with a motor which produces not to exceed five brake horsepower ... mopeds, and every bicycle with a motor attached except for an electric bicycle.
license_registration_insurance.notes: 'Bicycle' includes an electric bicycle (60-611(2)). The motor vehicle definitions for registration (60-339), operator's licenses (60-471) and the rules of the road (60-638) all exclude bicycles, so no registration, license or insurance applies. The quote shows an e-bike is also not a motor-driven cycle.

where_allowed.quote: A bicyclist riding a bicycle on a sidewalk or across a roadway or shoulder in a crosswalk shall have all the rights and duties applicable to a pedestrian under the same circumstances but shall yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
where_allowed.roads: As a bicycle, with the rights and duties of a vehicle driver (§ 60-6,314). Bicycles may use paved shoulders of state highways under § 60-6,142.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Bicycle rules apply on paths set aside for bicycles (§ 60-6,314(2)). The state and any political subdivision may permit, prohibit or control e-bike use in areas under its control (§ 60-678).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Allowed as a bicycle with pedestrian duties and yielding to pedestrians (§ 60-6,317(4)), unless a local ordinance restricts it (§ 60-6,317(5)).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: None in state statute. Class III is treated like Class I and II.

local_authority.quote: A local authority may by ordinance further regulate the operation of bicycles and may provide for the registration and inspection of bicycles.
local_authority.details: Local authorities may further regulate bicycles, which include e-bikes, by ordinance. § 60-678(1) lets the state or any governmental subdivision enact regulations 'permitting, prohibiting, and controlling the use of ... electric bicycles' in its jurisdiction, with a Class III misdemeanor for violations. So city age limits, helmet rules or bans are possible and are not modeled.

non_ebike_devices.quote: No person shall operate a moped upon a highway unless such person has a valid operator's license.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motor-driven cycle (any bicycle with a motor attached that is not an electric bicycle, up to 5 bhp) or moped. Above that, motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A bike over 750 W or 1 bhp, without operative pedals or a seat, or able to assist past 20/28 mph is not an electric bicycle. It becomes a 'motor-driven cycle' (§ 60-640), which includes 'every bicycle with a motor attached except for an electric bicycle'. A moped (pedals, automatic, 50 cc or less, 2 bhp or less, 30 mph max, § 60-637) needs a valid operator's license (§ 60-6,310), and moped operators must wear a DOT helmet unless 21+ with a Class M license and a safety course, plus eye protection (§ 60-6,279). The license class needed for an electric motor-driven cycle, and registration and insurance rules, were not read in statute.

open_questions: Resolved by verifier. The Legislature's 2023 cross-reference table lists LB 138 §§ 37-41 as operative Sept 2, 2023.

Partly checked by verifier. The statute pages for §§ 60-611 and 60-614.02 to 60-618.03 show no amendment after LB 138, and the site includes at least 2024 laws (LB 1004 in § 60-6,279). The agent's note that LB 23 (bike-share grants) was indefinitely postponed on 2026-04-17 was not re-checked. A full check of the 109th Legislature bill list is still open.
City ordinances (Omaha, Lincoln) that restrict e-bikes on sidewalks or trails or add age or helmet rules were not surveyed.
License class, registration and insurance for an electric 'motor-driven cycle' (an over-limit e-bike) were not confirmed.

verdict_cautions.reason: Each Nebraska class also requires a motor that 'produces no more than one brake horsepower' (about 745.7 W), so a 746 to 750 W label may fail.

NE.verifier_notes: Each class requires both 750 W or less and no more than 1 bhp (about 745.7 W), so the 'unclear' caution for 746 W and up stays. LB 138's Sept 2, 2023 operative date is confirmed, and the license citation now points to the motor vehicle definitions.

NH.name: New Hampshire

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" shall mean a pedaled vehicle equipped with an electric motor of less than 750 watts that falls within one of the following 3 classes
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than 750 watts
definition.notes: The watt limit is strict. 'Less than 750 watts' means a bike labeled exactly 750 W does NOT qualify. max_motor_watts holds the statute's number (750) and motor_watts_comparison 'less_than' carries the strict test. Enacted by 2019 c. 93 (HB 148), approved June 19, 2019, effective Aug 18, 2019. Current RSA text shows no later amendment, and the official docket shows no 2025 or 2026 e-bike bill passed. 'Bicycle' includes an electric bicycle (RSA 259:6), so the general bicycle helmet rule (under 16) applies. E-bikes are excluded from 'moped', 'motorcycle' and 'motor-driven cycle'. RSA 265:144-a, VI requires the motor to cut off 'when the rider stops pedaling or when the brakes are applied'. Class 2 still qualifies, because RSA 259:27-a lets a Class 2 motor 'be used exclusively to propel the bicycle' and RSA 265:144-a, VI is a separate operating rule. E-bikes must meet CPSC 16 CFR 1512. Class 3 needs a speedometer. No minimum age for Class 1 or 2.

label_required.quote: On and after January 1, 2020, manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each electric bicycle.

min_age.quote: No person less than 16 years of age may operate a class 3 electric bicycle. A person less than 16 years of age may ride as a passenger on a class 3 electric bicycle that is designed to accommodate passengers.
min_age.exceptions: Under 16 may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 designed for passengers.

helmet.quote: No person less than 16 years of age may operate or ride upon a bicycle on a public way unless he or she wears protective headgear of a type approved by the commissioner of health and human services.
No person less than 18 years of age may ride or sit as a passenger on a class 3 electric bicycle unless he or she wears a properly-fitted and fastened bicycle helmet

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric bicycle or a person operating an electric bicycle shall not be subject to the provisions of this title relating to financial responsibility, drivers' licenses, registration, certificates of title, off highway recreational vehicles, and license plates.

where_allowed.quote: An electric bicycle may be operated wherever a bicycle may be operated, subject to the following limitations
where_allowed.roads: Wherever a bicycle may be operated, with the rights and duties of a vehicle driver (RSA 265:143).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 and 2 may use bicycle paths and multi-use paths where bicycles are allowed, but the city, town or state agency with jurisdiction may prohibit them. Natural-surface nonmotorized trails may be regulated by the agency.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No statewide e-bike sidewalk rule found. Towns and cities regulate bicycle use on their ways by ordinance (RSA 265:149). Sidewalk parking is allowed unless a traffic control device prohibits it (RSA 265:152).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Class 3 may NOT use a bicycle or multi-use path unless the path is within or adjacent to a highway or roadway, or the agency with jurisdiction allows Class 3. Operator must be 16+. Riders under 18 must wear a helmet. Speedometer required.

local_authority.quote: Any city or town shall have the power to make ordinances, bylaws or regulations respecting the use and equipment of bicycles, except mopeds as defined in RSA 259:57, on its ways
local_authority.details: Towns and cities may regulate the use and equipment of bicycles (which include e-bikes) on their ways and may require bicycle licensing for a reasonable fee. They may ban Class 1 and 2 from paths they control and may open paths to Class 3. No statute expressly limits local age rules. Local ordinances were not surveyed.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Motor-driven cycle" shall mean any motorcycle or motor scooter with a motor which produces not to exceed 5 horse-power, and any bicycle with motor attached except any electric bicycle.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motor-driven cycle (any bicycle with a motor that is not an e-bike, up to 5 hp). A moped if it cannot exceed 30 mph in one mile. Above 5 hp, motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A pedal bike at or over 750 W, or one that assists past 20/28 mph, is not an e-bike and is a 'motor-driven cycle' (RSA 259:65). If its speed attainable in one mile is 30 mph or less it is also a 'moped' (RSA 259:57). Mopeds need a current driver's license, a motorcycle license or a restricted moped license (RSA 263:33, 263:33-a) and must be registered with a moped plate (RSA 261:80). Motor-driven cycles above moped limits are motorcycles needing a motorcycle license, registration and insurance. Moped license age and helmet rules were not read in statute, so min_age is null.

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.has_three_class_law_notes: P.L.2025, c.285 (S4834/A6235, approved Jan 19, 2026) removed the 2019 class 1/2/3 scheme. Only a pedal-assist bike that cuts out at 20 mph is a 'low-speed electric bicycle'. Class 2 (throttle) and class 3 (28 mph assist) bikes are now 'motorized bicycles' (moped rules). The label section still mentions a 'classification number'.

definition.citation: N.J.S.A. 39:1-1 (as amended by P.L.2025, c.285, s.1)
definition.quote: a two-wheeled vehicle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor that provides assistance only when the rider is pedaling, and that ceases to provide assistance when the bicycle reaches the speed of 20 miles per hour.
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor that provides assistance only when the rider is pedaling, and that ceases to provide assistance when the bicycle reaches the speed of 20 miles per hour
definition.notes: Low-speed electric bicycle = class 1 only, with no watt cap in the new text. 'Motorized bicycle' (39:1-1) now covers: (2) an electric motor giving pedal assist, or throttle-only propulsion up to 15 mph, (3) pedal assist with a max speed between 21 and 28 mph, (4) throttle above 15 mph with a max of 28 mph, plus gas helper motors under 50 cc. So a class 2 (20 mph throttle) bike and a class 3 (28 mph assist) bike are motorized bicycles. 'Electric motorized bicycle' (pedals, motor over 750 W AND able to exceed 28 mph) is listed inside the 'motorcycle' definition. E-trikes are outside the law per the MVC advisory of June 23, 2026.

label_required.quote: On and after January 1, 2019, manufacturers and distributors of low-speed electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each low-speed electric bicycle. The label shall contain the classification number, top assisted speed,

min_age.quote: No person who is under 15 years of age shall be permitted to operate a low-speed electric bicycle or motorized bicycle.
min_age.exceptions: Ages 15 and 16 need a motorized bicycle (moped, class F) license or permit. 17 and older need a basic driver's license or a moped license or permit. Shared-fleet rentals of low-speed electric bicycles under a local-government contract need no license if the company requires riders to be 16 or older (39:4-14.3(c)(4)). E-trikes are exempt per MVC.

helmet.citation: N.J.S.A. 39:4-10.1, applied to low-speed electric bicycles by N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.16(g)
helmet.quote: A person under 17 years of age shall not operate, or ride upon a bicycle as a passenger
helmet.notes: Read on FindLaw (current as of Jan 1, 2024), not the official NJ site. The full sentence requires a properly fitted and fastened ANSI or Snell helmet, including for passengers in child seats and trailers. 39:4-10.1 defines bicycle as human-powered, but 39:4-14.16(g) expressly applies statutes for bicycles 'as defined in section 1 of P.L.1991, c.465 (C.39:4-10.1)' to low-speed e-bikes. Municipalities may exempt car-free paths and roads (39:4-10.1(c)).

helmet.quote: No person shall operate a motorized bicycle unless he wears a protective helmet of a type approved by the director.
helmet.notes: Class 2 bikes are motorized bicycles after P.L.2025, c.285. Text read on FindLaw (current as of Jan 1, 2024), not the official site. c.285 did not amend this section.

helmet.quote: No person shall operate a motorized bicycle unless he wears a protective helmet of a type approved by the director.
helmet.notes: Class 3 bikes are motorized bicycles after P.L.2025, c.285.

license_registration_insurance.quote: The operator of a low-speed electric bicycle shall be required to register the low-speed electric bicycle and have a driver's license to operate the low-speed electric bicycle
license_registration_insurance.notes: Compliance grace period ended July 19, 2026 (six months after enactment, s.11). MVC began issuing e-bike licenses and registrations June 26, 2026. Registration gives two fork stickers. Fees waived for one year from Jan 19, 2026 (s.10). Insurance: 39:4-14.3e requires liability insurance for motorized bicycles. The MVC advisory (June 23, 2026) and DOBI Bulletin 26-03 (June 15, 2026) both say low-speed electric bicycles do NOT need insurance. 39:4-14.3(e) still says the insurance card must be carried when operating a low-speed electric bicycle, which is why the top-level flag is null.

where_allowed.quote: Motorized bicycles shall not be operated upon interstate highways or upon public highways divided by a grass or concrete median or highways with posted speed limits in excess of 50 miles per hour
where_allowed.roads: Low-speed electric bicycles (class 1): streets, highways, roadways and bicycle paths, under bicycle rules. Motorized bicycles (class 2 and 3): banned from interstates, median-divided highways, roads posted over 50 mph, railroad rights-of-way, and public land where the agency prohibits them.
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Bicycle rules apply to low-speed electric bicycles (39:4-14.16(g)) and to motorized bicycles unless the commissioner decides otherwise (39:4-14.3(f)). Not addressed separately.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Low-speed electric bicycles may use bicycle paths unless a local or State agency bans them. Natural-surface non-motorized trails are off limits unless the agency allows it (39:4-14.16(d),(e)). Path access for motorized bicycles is not stated in c.285.
where_allowed.sidewalks: c.285 only allows low-speed e-bikes and scooters to be PARKED on a sidewalk if they do not impede pedestrians. Sidewalk riding is not authorized by state law and is set by local ordinance.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Class 3 is a motorized bicycle: license, registration, insurance, helmet at all ages, and the road limits above.

local_authority.quote: a local government entity or State agency may prohibit the operation of low-speed electric bicycles or low-speed electric scooters on bicycle paths under its jurisdiction.
local_authority.details: Locals may ban low-speed e-bikes from bicycle paths and natural-surface trails. 39:4-14.3(b) bars municipalities from restricting motorized bicycles on public roads contrary to the act. No express state grant to add age limits.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Electric motorized bicycle" means any two-wheeled vehicle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor capable of greater than 750 watts that is capable of reaching a speed greater than 28 miles per hour.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: 'Motorcycle' now includes electric motorized bicycles, so a pedal bike over 750 W that can exceed 28 mph needs motorcycle license, registration and insurance. A bike with no pedals is not a low-speed e-bike or a motorized bicycle (both require pedals) and falls under motorcycle or 'motorized scooter' rules. Gap: a bike at or under 750 W that exceeds 28 mph fits neither the motorized bicycle nor the electric motorized bicycle text, so treat it as not legal as an e-bike. Online sale of electric motorized bicycles is banned until Jan 19, 2027 (s.12). Selling kits that turn a low-speed e-bike into a motorized bicycle is banned (39:4-14.16(j)). Motorcycle license minimum age not verified here.

pending_changes.summary: Riders of bicycles and low-speed electric bicycles count as 'pedestrians' for PIP auto insurance. A pedestrian hurt in a crash is covered by their own PIP coverage. Effective date per the act (first day of the 12th month after enactment) and DOBI Bulletin 26-03.
Temporary one-year ban on Internet sales of electric motorized bicycles, which ends about Jan 19, 2027.

Gap: a bike with pedals, 750 W or less, that can exceed 28 mph fits no category in the definitions.
Is sidewalk riding by low-speed e-bikes set only by local ordinance? c.285 addresses only parking.
Class 1 bikes that also have a 15 mph throttle are motorized bicycles under definition (2). The app must treat any throttle as motorized bicycle.

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.has_three_class_law_notes: SB 69 (2023) was signed April 4, 2023 as Laws 2023, Chapter 93, and took effect July 1, 2023. 2024 SB 88 re-enacted § 66-1-4.5 with the same e-bike text (it only added electronic-credential definitions), and 2025 SB 73 (Laws 2025, ch. 22) changed only how bicyclists treat stop and yield signs. No 2024 to 2026 act changed the e-bike rules.

definition.quote: "electric-assisted bicycle" means a vehicle having two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and an electric motor.
definition.motor_watts_basis: not exceeding seven hundred fifty watts of power
definition.notes: Each class is defined with a motor 'not exceeding seven hundred fifty watts of power'. Two or three wheels are allowed. E-bikes must meet 16 CFR 1512 (66-3-708(C)). A class 2 motor must cut out when the brakes are applied. Class 1 and 3 need a cutoff, which cannot be bypassed, when pedaling stops. Class 3 needs a speedometer (66-3-708(D),(E)). E-bikes are excluded from 'motor vehicle' (66-1-4.11(H)) and 'off-highway motor vehicle' (66-1-4.13(B)).

label_required.quote: Every manufacturer or distributor of new electric-assisted bicycles intended for sale or distribution in New Mexico shall permanently affix to each electric-assisted bicycle, in a prominent location, a label

min_age.quote: A person under sixteen years of age shall not operate a class 3 electric-assisted bicycle upon any street, highway or bicycle or pedestrian path
min_age.exceptions: A person under 16 may ride as a passenger on a class 3 e-bike designed to carry passengers. No state minimum age for class 1 or class 2.

helmet.citation: NMSA 1978 § 32A-24-3(A), § 32A-24-2(A),(C) (Child Helmet Safety Act, as amended by Laws 2023, ch. 93, s.1)
helmet.quote: It is unlawful for a parent or legal guardian of a minor to knowingly permit that minor to operate or be a passenger on a bicycle, skates, scooter or skateboard unless that minor wears a well-fitted protective bicycle helmet
helmet.notes: The 2023 law changed the Act's definition of 'bicycle' to include an electric-assisted bicycle. 'Minor' means under 18. The duty falls on the parent or guardian, with a civil penalty up to $10. The quoted operative text is from the 2007 enacted bill (SB 397). The current codified text was not read on an official site.

license_registration_insurance.quote: including an electric mobility device, but does not include an electric-assisted bicycle
license_registration_insurance.notes: The quote is from the 'motor vehicle' definition. 66-3-1(A)(12) lists 'an electric-assisted bicycle' as exempt from registration and title. Driver license and mandatory insurance rules attach to motor vehicles, so they do not apply. Those license and insurance sections were not separately read.

where_allowed.quote: A person may ride a class 1 electric-assisted bicycle on a bicycle or pedestrian path where bicycles are authorized to travel; provided that a political subdivision of the state may prohibit
where_allowed.roads: Not expressly addressed in SB 69. E-bikes are not motor vehicles. Bicycle-on-road rules were not separately verified.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 is allowed on bicycle or pedestrian paths unless a political subdivision bans it. Class 2 and 3 are banned from paths unless the path is within a street or highway, or a political subdivision allows them. Natural-surface non-motorized trails are outside 66-3-709 and may be regulated by the managing agency.
where_allowed.sidewalks: Not addressed in SB 69. Left to local ordinance (not verified).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Minimum age 16 (passengers under 16 are allowed on bikes built for passengers). A speedometer is required. Same path limits as class 2.

local_authority.quote: a political subdivision of the state permits the operation of a class 2 or class 3 electric-assisted bicycle on a path under its jurisdiction.
local_authority.details: Political subdivisions may ban class 1 from paths, open paths to class 2 and 3, and regulate e-bikes on natural-surface trails. No express power to add age limits was found.

non_ebike_devices.quote: a two- or three-wheel vehicle with an electric motor for propulsion that does not meet the definition of an electric-assisted bicycle and is capable of exceeding a speed of twenty miles per hour on motor power alone
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: Without operable pedals and able to exceed 20 mph on motor power alone, it is an electric mobility device, which is expressly a motor vehicle. With operable pedals and 2 or 3 wheels but over 750 W or outside the class speeds, it is still an 'electric-assisted bicycle' under the general definition in 66-1-4.5(A) but in no class, so its status is unclear
non_ebike_devices.notes: The general definition in 66-1-4.5(A) has no watt or speed cap. Each class adds a 750 W cap and a speed cut-off. An 'electric mobility device' must fail that general definition, so a pedal bike over 750 W is a classless 'electric-assisted bicycle', not a motor vehicle, and the class rules (paths, Class 3 age) do not clearly reach it. Treat it as unclear. A device without pedals that can exceed 20 mph on motor power alone is an electric mobility device and so a motor vehicle, presumably needing registration, a license and insurance (those sections were not read). A device without pedals that cannot exceed 20 mph fits neither term.

open_questions: Resolved by verifier. The nmlegis.gov legislation lists for the 2024, 2025 and 2026 regular sessions and the 2024 and 2025 special sessions show no enacted e-bike bill. 2024 SB 88 re-enacted § 66-1-4.5 unchanged for e-bikes, and 2025 SB 73 covers bicycle stops only.
Road and bike-lane rules for e-bikes (whether e-bikes get bicycle rights under 66-3-701 et seq.) were not verified.
The Child Helmet Safety Act operative text was read from the 2007 enacted bill, not current NMSA. It puts the duty on parents, not riders.
License, registration and insurance requirements for 'electric mobility devices' were not traced.
Status of a device that is not an e-bike but cannot exceed 20 mph on motor power alone is unclear.
NM.verifier_notes: All quotes match the enacted SB 69 and the 2007 helmet act, and no 2024 to 2026 act changed the e-bike rules. Notes now say a pedal bike over 750 W is a classless e-assisted bicycle with unclear status, not a motor vehicle.

NV.name: Nevada

definition.quote: Electric bicycle means a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ... that has fully operable pedals, a seat or saddle for the rider, an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts
definition.notes: Three classes added by 2021 SB 383 (Statutes of Nevada 2021, p. 1743). SB 383 has no effective-date section, so it took effect Oct 1, 2021 under NRS 218D.330(1), which matches NRS 484B.784(2). NRS 484B (revised Sept 9, 2026) shows no 2025 or later change to the e-bike sections. The term does not include a moped or an electric scooter. E-bikes are excluded from 'vehicle' (NRS 484A.320, 482.135) and 'motor vehicle' (NRS 484A.130), and exempt from registration (NRS 482.210(1)(d)). NRS 484B.784(3) requires equipment that stops the motor when the rider stops pedaling or the brakes are applied. Class 2 still qualifies, because NRS 484B.017 lets a Class 2 motor 'be used exclusively to propel the bicycle' and NRS 484B.784(3) is a separate equipment rule. No statewide minimum age and no statewide helmet rule for any class. Clark County reportedly requires helmets for riders under 18 by local ordinance (news report, not verified).

label_required.quote: On and after January 1, 2022, a manufacturer or distributor of electric bicycles in this State shall apply a label that is permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each electric bicycle

license_registration_insurance.quote: The provisions of this chapter requiring the registration of certain vehicles do not apply to: ... (d) Electric bicycles.

where_allowed.quote: an electric bicycle may be ridden in places where bicycles are allowed, including, without limitation, streets, highways, roads, roadways, bicycle lanes, bicycle paths and shared-use paths.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed where bicycles are, with the rights and duties of a vehicle driver (NRS 484B.763). Ride as far right as practicable unless keeping up with traffic or unsafe (NRS 484B.777).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Bicycle paths and shared-use paths allowed unless a local ordinance (or a state agency after notice and a hearing) bans e-bikes or a class for health, safety or legal reasons. Natural-surface nonmotorized trails may be regulated by the agency with jurisdiction.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No statewide rule on riding bicycles or e-bikes on sidewalks was found. The sidewalk ban in NRS 484B.117 applies to drivers of 'vehicles', and e-bikes are excluded from 'vehicle'. Parking on sidewalks is allowed if it does not block pedestrians (NRS 484B.450(3)). Local ordinances likely control.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: None beyond a required speedometer (NRS 484B.784(5)). No Class 3 age limit.

local_authority.quote: A local authority, by ordinance, or a state agency, after notice and a hearing, may prohibit the operation of an electric bicycle or a class of electric bicycles on a bicycle path or shared-use path over which it has jurisdiction
local_authority.details: Path bans by class are allowed with a health, safety or legal finding. NRS 484A.400(2) lets local authorities enact traffic ordinances on the same subjects as state law if they do not conflict, and lets them require bicycle registration and licensing. Locals may not govern vehicle registration or driver licensing (484A.400(3)). News reports say Clark County restricts e-bikes in parks and requires helmets for riders under 18. Ordinance text not read.

non_ebike_devices.quote: Moped means a motor-driven scooter, motor-driven cycle or similar vehicle that is propelled by a small engine which produces not more than 2 gross brake horsepower ... or produces not more than 1500 watts final output
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (up to 1,500 W final output and 30 mph) or, above that, motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A bike over 750 W, without operable pedals or a seat, or outside the three classes is not an e-bike. If it produces 1,500 W or less and cannot exceed 30 mph it is a moped (no pedals required). Moped drivers and passengers must wear protective headgear (NRS 486.231). Nevada DMV materials say mopeds need a driver's license of any class and must be registered. I did not read those statutes, so min_age is null. Above 1,500 W or 30 mph the device is a motorcycle needing a motorcycle license or endorsement (NRS 486.061), registration and insurance.

pending_changes.bill: ACR 4, 36th Special Session (2025), interim study of e-bikes, e-motorcycles and e-scooters
pending_changes.signed: resolution adopted in the 36th Special Session (2025), effective on adoption. Study began March 2026
pending_changes.summary: Directs the Joint Interim Standing Committee on the Judiciary to review e-bike, e-motorcycle and e-scooter laws, school-zone penalties and local powers during the 2025-2026 interim and report to the 84th Session (February 2027). It may lead to a 2027 bill on age limits, helmets, training, locations and fines. No rule change yet.

NRS 484B.017(2) defines Class 2 as a motor that 'may be used exclusively to propel the bicycle', and the cut-off rule in NRS 484B.784(3) does not change that. It sits in a separate operating section, so it does not take Class 2 out of the definition. Read with that definition, a brake cut-off satisfies it. A literal reading leaves a small equipment-citation risk, so no caution is set.
Sidewalk riding is not addressed by state law for e-bikes. Clark County, Las Vegas, Reno and Henderson ordinances were not read.
Clark County's reported helmet rule for riders under 18 was seen only in news coverage.
Moped license, age and registration rules were not confirmed in statute.
Resolved by verifier. SB 383 (2021) has no effective-date section, so NRS 218D.330(1) makes it effective Oct 1, 2021.

NY.name: New York
NY.has_three_class_law_notes: A modified three-class law (2020 budget, Part XX of Ch.58 L.2020). Class 3 tops out at 25 mph, not 28 mph, and is legal only in a city of 1 million or more (in practice New York City).

definition.quote: A bicycle which is no more than thirty-six inches wide and has an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty watts
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty watts
definition.notes: The motor must be LESS than 750 W, so a bike labeled exactly 750 W does not fit the text. Other requirements: no more than 36 inches wide, operable pedals, and the CPSC bicycle standard (16 CFR 1512.1 et seq.). Class 3 exists 'Solely within a city having a population of one million or more'. It is defined as a motor that 'may be used exclusively to propel' the bike, with assistance ending at 25 mph. A class 3 bike labeled 28 mph exceeds NY's 25 mph class 3 cap. A pedal-assist-only class 3 (no throttle) does not literally match the 'used exclusively to propel' wording. Text last revised 2020-04-17, full text read on nysenate.gov in a browser.

label_required.quote: has permanently affixed thereto, in a prominent location, a manufacturer's label
label_required.notes: The label shows class, top motor-assisted speed and wattage. Since June 1, 2022, riding an unlabeled e-bike on a public highway carries a civil fine up to $50, waived for a first offense if the label is fixed before the court date (summary of the nysenate.gov text).

min_age.quote: No person less than sixteen years of age shall operate a bicycle with electric assist
min_age.exceptions: None found. Police may summons a parent or guardian 18 or older only when the violation happens in their presence (1242(13)).

helmet.quote: No person shall ride upon, propel or otherwise operate a class three bicycle with electric assist
helmet.notes: The quote is the opening of 5-c. The rest of the subdivision requires wearing a helmet.

helmet.quote: shall operate a bicycle unless such person is wearing a helmet
helmet.notes: No statewide helmet rule for adult class 1 or class 2 riders. Riders must be 16+, so the under-14 operator rule in 1238(5)(b) is moot. Passengers are covered: 1242(1) applies all Article 34 bicycle rules to e-bikes, so passengers aged 5 to 13 need a helmet (1238(5)(a)), and passengers aged 1 to 4 need a helmet and a separate child seat (1238(2)). No passengers under 1 (1238(1)). Locals may require helmets (1242(3), 1238(9)). The same applies to class_2.

helmet.quote: shall operate a bicycle unless such person is wearing a helmet
helmet.notes: Same as class_1: no adult helmet rule, passenger helmet rules for under 14 apply, and local helmet rules are allowed.

license_registration_insurance.quote: (e) bicycles with electric assist as defined in section one hundred two-c of this article
license_registration_insurance.notes: The quote is from the list of exclusions in the 'motor vehicle' definition. Because e-bikes are not motor vehicles, the license, registration and insurance rules for motor vehicles do not apply. A WAMC report (May 25, 2026) confirms riders need no license or registration and that no registration bill will move until 2027.

where_allowed.quote: may only be operated on highways with a posted speed limit of thirty miles per hour or less
where_allowed.roads: Only on highways posted 30 mph or less (including private roads open to motor vehicles), unless local law says otherwise. Riders must ride single file. Speed caps: class 1 and 2 at 20 mph, class 3 at 25 mph (1242(9)). NYC set a 15 mph e-bike limit in 2025 (local rule, secondary source).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Allowed in designated bicycle or in-line skate lanes (1242(8)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Banned on public lands and property other than highways, and greenways next to or connected with highways count as banned too, unless a state agency or locality designates and posts the land for e-bikes (1242(4)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Banned unless a local law authorizes it: 'No bicycle with electric assist shall be operated on a sidewalk, except as may be authorized by a local law'. Parking that does not block pedestrians is allowed.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Class 3 is illegal outside a city of 1 million or more (in practice only NYC) per 1242(10). Class 3 riders need a helmet at all ages and are capped at 25 mph.

local_authority.quote: Except as provided in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this subdivision, the governing body of any city, town or village
local_authority.details: Cities, towns and villages may regulate time, place and manner (including max speed, helmets and reflective clothing), limit or ban e-bikes in specified areas, or 'prohibit entirely' the use of e-bikes, if signs are posted (1242(3)(a)). In Nassau and Suffolk (cities, towns, villages) and Westchester (towns, villages), speed, helmet and clothing rules need a county law first, but area bans and total bans do not. No express age-limit power, though a total ban is allowed.

non_ebike_devices.quote: A limited use vehicle having only two or three wheels, with a seat or saddle for the operator.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: limited use motorcycle (moped), class A (30 to 40 mph), B (20 to 30 mph) or C (20 mph or less)
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device that fails § 102-c (motor 750 W or more, wider than 36 inches, no operable pedals, or a class 3 bike over 25 mph or outside NYC) is not a bicycle with electric assist. Per the nysenate.gov summary it falls under the limited-use motorcycle (moped) classes. Mopeds need DMV registration, an operator license and, for some classes, insurance. A 2024 law requires dealers to register mopeds at point of sale. Exact moped license and insurance rules by class and the minimum age were not verified.

NY.pending_changes_notes: About four dozen e-bike bills (registration, ID, safety course) were pending in the Assembly Transportation Committee in 2026. The chair said there would be no major action until 2027 (WAMC, May 25, 2026).
