The July 2024 laws (lithium-ion battery standards, moped point-of-sale registration) are in force and do not change e-bike legality.
open_questions: A pedal-assist-only bike with a 25 mph cutoff does not literally match NY's class 3 wording ('may be used exclusively to propel'). Treat a pedal-only class 3 in NYC as unclear.
A 750 W labeled motor fails the 'less than 750 watts' test on a strict reading. Decide whether the app flags a 750 W label as not legal or as unclear.
A class 3 label of 28 mph exceeds NY's 25 mph class 3 definition, even in NYC. The likely result is a moped (limited use motorcycle class B), but no court or DMV guidance was found.
Moped (limited use motorcycle) license class, insurance by class and minimum age were not verified.
NYC's 15 mph e-bike speed limit (2025) and other NYC local rules are outside this state table.
The effective_date of 2020-04-17 is the revision date nysenate.gov shows, not a verified effective-date clause in the 2020 budget bill.

verdict_cautions.reason: New York's Class 3 exists only in cities of 1 million or more, must be throttle-capable and stops at 25 mph. A Class 3 label of 28 mph fits no New York class.

NY.verifier_notes: 102-c, 1238 and 1242 re-read on nysenate.gov. No 2026 amendment found. No corrections.

OH.name: Ohio
OH.has_three_class_law_notes: HB 250 (132nd GA), effective March 8, 2019, created the three classes. HB 295 (133rd GA) amended them, effective April 15, 2021. 4511.01 was last amended by HB 96 (Sept 30, 2025), but the e-bike definitions were unchanged. SB 477, introduced Oct 7, 2026, is pending.

definition.quote: "Class 1 electric bicycle" means a bicycle that is equipped with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty watts that provides assistance only when the rider is pedaling
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty watts
definition.notes: Each class requires a motor of LESS than 750 W, so a bike labeled exactly 750 W fails a strict reading. 'Bicycle' includes an electric bicycle (4511.01(G)). An e-bike is a 'vehicle' (A) but not a 'motor vehicle' (B) or a 'motorized bicycle'/'moped' (H). Equipment must meet 16 CFR 1512. Class 1 and 3 motors must cut out when pedaling stops, and class 2 when the brakes or a switch are used. Class 3 needs a speedometer (4511.522(B)).

label_required.quote: On and after January 1, 2020, manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall permanently affix a label, in a prominent location, to each electric bicycle.

min_age.quote: No person under sixteen years of age shall operate a class 3 electric bicycle; however, a person under sixteen years of age may ride as a passenger on a class 3 electric bicycle that is designed to accommodate passengers.
min_age.exceptions: Passengers under 16 are allowed on class 3 bikes built for passengers. No state minimum age for class 1 or class 2.

helmet.quote: No person shall operate or be a passenger on a class 3 electric bicycle unless the person is wearing a protective helmet that meets the standards established by the consumer product safety commission

OH.helmet_notes: No statewide helmet rule for class 1 or class 2. Local ordinances may require one.

license_registration_insurance.quote: "Motor vehicle" means every vehicle propelled or drawn by power other than muscular power or power collected from overhead electric trolley wires, except motorized bicycles, electric bicycles,
license_registration_insurance.notes: E-bikes are not motor vehicles, so no state license, registration or insurance applies. Local authorities MAY require registration and licensing of bicycles (4511.07(A)(9)), and 'bicycle' includes e-bikes, so some cities can require e-bike registration.

where_allowed.quote: No person shall operate a class 3 electric bicycle on a path set aside for the exclusive use of bicycles or a shared-use path unless that path is within or adjacent to a highway
where_allowed.roads: E-bikes are bicycles and vehicles, so they may use roads with bicycle rights and duties. Local authorities may not prohibit bicycles on public streets except as 4511.051 allows (4511.07(A)(8)).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Not separately restricted. Bicycle rules apply.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 and 2 are allowed on bike-only and shared-use paths unless the managing authority bans them. Class 3 is banned from those paths unless the path is within or next to a highway or the authority allows it. All classes are banned from mountain-bike, hiking, equestrian and natural-surface non-motorized trails unless authorized (4511.522(C)(3)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Sidewalk riding is allowed only with the motor NOT engaged: no vehicle 'other than a bicycle or an electric bicycle if the motor is not engaged' on sidewalks (4511.711(A)). Locals may regulate further.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Minimum age 16. Helmet required for operators and passengers. Speedometer required. Paths restricted as above.

local_authority.quote: Regulating the operation of bicycles; provided that no such regulation shall be fundamentally inconsistent with the uniform rules of the road prescribed by this chapter
local_authority.details: Locals may regulate bicycle operation (which includes e-bikes), require bicycle registration and licensing, and ban or allow e-bike classes on paths and trails. They may not ban bicycles from public streets (except under 4511.051) or require sidewalk riding. Whether a local age limit is 'fundamentally inconsistent' with state law is untested.

non_ebike_devices.quote: equipped with a helper motor of not more than fifty cubic centimeters piston displacement that produces not more than one brake horsepower and is capable of propelling the vehicle at a speed of not greater than twenty miles per hour
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorized bicycle/moped (up to 1 bhp, up to 20 mph, pedalable) or else motorcycle/motor vehicle
non_ebike_devices.notes: Moped rules (4511.521): ages 14 and 15 need a probationary motorized bicycle license, and 16+ need a driver's or motorized bicycle license. Riders under 18 need a helmet and a rear-view mirror. No passengers. A device that is not an e-bike (750 W or more, no pedals, or over class speeds) and exceeds moped limits is a motor vehicle (likely a motorcycle needing an endorsement, registration and insurance). Note that 1 bhp is about 746 W, so a 750 W+ electric bike may exceed the moped power limit. Registration and insurance for mopeds were not verified.

pending_changes.bill: SB 477 (136th General Assembly), sponsor Sen. William DeMora
pending_changes.summary: Bill text read (As Introduced PDF). It would bar riders under 14 from every e-bike, keep Class 3 for ages 16 and up, require a helmet for every e-bike rider and passenger at any age, bar riders under 18 from carrying passengers or renting an e-bike, cap motor-on speed on shared-use paths at 10 mph, and require $25 BMV registration for e-bikes used on public roads from six months after it takes effect, with proof of a license, permit or approved safety course. Introduced Oct 7, 2026, with no committee referral shown on Oct 16, 2026. Not law.

pending_changes.bill: HB 948 (136th General Assembly), Reps. Andrea White and Kevin D. Miller
pending_changes.summary: Would have ODOT and DPS publish an e-bike law summary and videos, require retailers to give each buyer an education leaflet, add sharing the road with e-bikes to online driver education, and order a DPS study of e-bike, e-moto and mini-bike rules, including Class 3 training. It does not change ages, helmets or the definition. Introduced May 19, 2026 and referred to House Transportation May 20, 2026. Not law.

open_questions: SB 477 (introduced Oct 7, 2026) would add an under-14 ban, an all-ages helmet rule and BMV registration for every e-bike (bill text read by the verifier). It is not law. Watch it through the lame-duck session, since bills not passed by the end of 2026 die.
A 750 W label fails the 'less than seven hundred fifty watts' definition on a strict reading.
Whether a 750 W+ electric bike capped at 20 mph is a moped (1 bhp is about 746 W) or a motorcycle is unclear.
Moped registration and insurance rules were not verified.
Many Ohio cities have local bicycle ordinances (registration, sidewalk bans) that are outside this state table.
OH.verifier_notes: Less than 750 W definition, Class 3 age 16, Class 3 helmet and local powers confirmed on codes.ohio.gov. SB 477 and HB 948 are pending only, and no 2025 or 2026 e-bike act was found in the Legislature's search.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.has_three_class_law_notes: Laws 2019, c.43 (HB 1265), effective Nov 1, 2019. 11-1209 was amended by Laws 2021, c.398 (SB 184, path access), effective Nov 1, 2021. Text read from the Legislature's complete Title 47 file, which includes 2025 session laws. No 2026 e-bike law was found. SB 51 (e-bike tax credit) was introduced in 2025 with no enactment shown.

definition.quote: Fully operative pedals for human propulsion and equipped with an electric motor with a power output of not more than seven hundred fifty (750) watts that meets the requirements of one of the following three classes:
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor with a power output of not more than seven hundred fifty (750) watts
definition.notes: Two or three wheels. Must meet CPSC bicycle requirements. The motor must disengage when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes (1-104(B)). 'Bicycle' includes e-bikes (1-104(D)). E-bikes are excluded from 'motor vehicle' (1-134(B)(5)) and 'motorized scooter' (1-133.3(B)).

label_required.quote: On and after January 1, 2020, manufacturers and distributors of electric-assisted bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed in a prominent location to each electric-assisted bicycle.

min_age.quote: No person under sixteen (16) years of age may operate a Class 3 electric-assisted bicycle.
min_age.exceptions: Riders under 16 may be passengers on a class 3 bike built for passengers. No state minimum age for class 1 or class 2.

OK.helmet_notes: No e-bike helmet requirement in 11-1209. Title 47 helmet rules cover only ATVs and motorcycles for riders under 18. Some retailer sites claim a class 3 helmet rule for under-18 riders, but it is not in the statute text.

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric-assisted bicycle or a person operating an electric-assisted bicycle is not subject to the Oklahoma statutory provisions relating to financial responsibility, vehicle insurance, driver licenses, vehicle registration or certificates of title.
license_registration_insurance.notes: Local authorities may require registration and licensing of bicycles (15-102(A)(8)), and 'bicycle' includes e-bikes.

where_allowed.quote: A Class 1, Class 2 or Class 3 electric-assisted bicycle may be ridden on bicycle or multiuse paths where bicycles are permitted.
where_allowed.roads: Wherever bicycles may travel, with bicycle rights and duties (11-1209(A),(E)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: All three classes are allowed on bicycle and multiuse paths unless the local authority or state agency bans them. Natural-surface non-motorized trails are outside this rule and may be regulated by the agency.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No state statute found. Set by local ordinance.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Minimum age 16 (passengers excepted). A speedometer is required. Same path access as class 1 and 2. E-bikes may not lane-split (11-1103(D)).

local_authority.quote: Regulating the operating of bicycles and requiring the registration and licensing of same, including the requirement of a registration fee;
local_authority.details: Locals may regulate bicycle operation (which includes e-bikes), require bicycle registration and licensing, and ban any class from paths and trails. Edmond, for example, has an e-bike ordinance. Express age-limit power is not stated.

non_ebike_devices.quote: If the power source is an electric motor, the motor shall not exceed seven hundred fifty (750) watts.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped, motorized scooter, or motor-driven cycle/motorcycle depending on specs
non_ebike_devices.notes: An electric moped's motor may not exceed 750 W (1-133.2), so a pedal bike over 750 W is not a moped. A 'motorized scooter' (up to 3 wheels, handlebars, a seat or foot support, electric and programmed to 35 mph or less) needs no registration, license or insurance unless a local ordinance says so, and its minimum age is 14 (1-133.3). Whether a non-conforming pedal e-bike counts as a motorized scooter or a motor-driven cycle is unresolved. Mopeds must be registered and may use streets only where a city ordinance or county board authorizes them (11-1116(E)). Moped license rules were not verified. Two more definitions matter. A 'motor-driven cycle' (1-136) is a motor vehicle with a seat whose electric power source puts out less than 1,000 W, and a 'motorcycle' (1-135) has an electric motor of 1,000 W or more. So a pedal bike over 750 W and under 1,000 W fits the motor-driven cycle definition and may also fit the motorized scooter one.

open_questions: Partly resolved by the verifier. OSCN's 2026 statutes already carry 2026 session laws that take effect Nov 1, 2026 (for example 47 O.S. 11-902, Laws 2026 c. 437), and they show no 2026 change to 1-104 or 11-1209 and no new e-bike section in Title 47. The Legislature's text search host did not resolve and its bill search needs a form, so neither was run. SB 51 (e-bike tax credit) never got past committee referral in 2025.
Is a non-conforming electric pedal bike (over 750 W, 35 mph or less) a 'motorized scooter' (age 14, no license) or a motor-driven cycle/motorcycle?
Moped licensing and age rules were not traced.
Sidewalk riding is not addressed in state law.

1-104(B) says the motor must cut out 'when the rider stops pedaling or the brakes are applied'. The same section defines Class 2 as a throttle class, so Class 2 is kept legal, as round 1 did for similar states. No court or agency ruling was found.
OK.verifier_notes: Not more than 750 W definition, Class 3 age 16, no helmet rule and local powers confirmed in the Title 47 file and on OSCN 2026. No 2026 change was found, but the Legislature's own bill search could not be run.

OR.name: Oregon
OR.has_three_class_law_notes: HB 4103 (2024 Or. Laws ch.12), approved Mar 20, 2024 and effective Jan 1, 2025, replaced the old single definition (1,000 W, 20 mph) with three classes and NO wattage cap. HB 4007 (2026 Or. Laws ch.101), approved Apr 7, 2026 and effective June 5, 2026, changes ages and helmets OPERATIVE Jan 1, 2027 (see pending_changes).

definition.quote: "Electric assisted bicycle" means a bicycle that is equipped with an electric motor and that is a Class 1 electric assisted bicycle, a Class 2 electric assisted bicycle or a Class 3 electric assisted bicycle.
definition.motor_watts_basis: “Electric assisted bicycle” means a bicycle that is equipped with an electric motor and that is a Class 1 electric assisted bicycle
definition.notes: There is NO wattage limit after 2025 (the old 1,000 W cap was deleted). Class 3 must have a speedometer. 'Bicycle' (ORS 801.150) needs a seat, no more than 3 wheels, pedals, and every wheel over 14 inches (or two tandem wheels, either over 14 inches). Small-wheel bikes (14 inches or less) therefore may not qualify. 801.150 still says 'propelled exclusively by human power', but 814.405 treats an e-bike as a bicycle rather than a motor vehicle.

label_required.quote: As an electric assisted bicycle and the vehicle does not fit the definition of an electric assisted bicycle as defined in ORS 801.258;
label_required.notes: No manufacturer label requirement was found in ORS 801, 807, 811, 814 or 815. From Jan 1, 2027, selling a vehicle as an e-bike that doesn't meet 801.258, or that is built to be modified out of its class, is a Class D violation and an unlawful trade practice. From the same date, batteries must carry a testing-lab certification mark (ch.101 §19).

min_age.quote: without any grant of driving privileges if the person is 16 years of age or older: (a) A Class 1 electric assisted bicycle; (b) A Class 2 electric assisted bicycle; or (c) A Class 3 electric assisted bicycle.
min_age.exceptions: In force through Dec 31, 2026. Under 16 needs a 'grant of driving privileges' (a license or permit), which in practice bars young riders. From Jan 1, 2027, class 1 drops to age 14, class 2 and 3 stay at 16, and class 1 and 2 riders of any age may ride in a bicycle safety program under ORS 802.325 (HB 4007).

helmet.quote: if the person is under 16 years of age, operates or rides on a bicycle on a highway or on premises open to the public and is not wearing protective headgear
helmet.notes: This covers e-bikes because 814.405 treats them as bicycles. It matters mainly for passengers under 16 until 2027, and for class 1 riders aged 14 and 15 from Jan 1, 2027. HB 4007 repeals 814.485 from Jan 1, 2027 and moves the duty to the carrier, parent or guardian under amended 814.486, still for anyone under 16 on a bicycle. There is a religious exemption.

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric assisted bicycle shall be considered a bicycle, rather than a motor vehicle, for purposes of the Oregon Vehicle Code, except when otherwise specifically provided by statute.
license_registration_insurance.notes: No license for riders who meet the age rules. Bicycles are exempt from title and registration (803.030, and HB 4007's version of 803.305). Insurance applies to motor vehicles only.

where_allowed.quote: Operates an electric assisted bicycle on a sidewalk.
where_allowed.roads: Bicycle rules apply (814.405). Where a jurisdiction finds a bike lane or path suitable, riders must use it (814.420).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Allowed, as bicycles. Motorists must yield to e-bike riders in bike lanes (811.050).
where_allowed.paths_trails: No e-bike-specific state statute was found. Path and trail rules are set by the managing agency (Oregon State Parks rulemaking in 2024 to 2025, not verified).
where_allowed.sidewalks: BANNED statewide. Riding an e-bike on a sidewalk is 'unsafe operation of a bicycle on a sidewalk', a Class D violation (814.410(1)(e)).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: A speedometer is required. Age 16+ (same as other classes until 2027).

local_authority.quote: A person is not required to comply with this section unless the state or local authority with jurisdiction over the roadway finds, after public hearing, that the bicycle lane or bicycle path is suitable
local_authority.details: No express state grant or preemption on local e-bike age limits or bans was found. HB 4007 §4 gives locals express power to ban or regulate 'powered micromobility devices', which excludes e-bikes, on lanes, paths, sidewalks and trails. Oregon cities have broad home-rule power, but whether they can set e-bike age limits was not verified.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Moped" means a vehicle, including any bicycle equipped with a power source, other than an electric assisted bicycle as defined in ORS 801.258 or a motor assisted scooter as defined in ORS 801.348,
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (independent power source, 30 mph or less), otherwise motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A powered bicycle outside the three classes (e.g. throttle above 20 mph, or assist above 28 mph) is a moped if it is capable of 30 mph or less unassisted. Mopeds are banned from sidewalks, bike paths and bike lanes (814.210), require a motorcycle-type helmet (814.260), and need a license and registration (licensing details not verified). Over 30 mph it is a motorcycle. Watts do not matter after 2025. From Jan 1, 2027, a 'powered micromobility device' (28 mph max, under 100 lb, not an e-bike) gets bicycle rights, which may catch some non-class devices.

pending_changes.summary: Operative Jan 1, 2027. Class 1 minimum age drops from 16 to 14, while class 2 and 3 stay at 16. Class 1 and 2 riders of any age may ride in a bicycle safety program. The bicycle helmet offense 814.485 is repealed, and amended 814.486 makes carriers, parents and guardians liable for under-16 riders without helmets. It creates a 'powered micromobility device' class with local ban powers, offenses for impostor e-bikes and uncertified batteries, and lowers the motor assisted scooter age to 14 (20 mph cap). The act itself took effect June 5, 2026.

open_questions: The rules engine needs a date switch on Jan 1, 2027 for the class 1 age (16 to 14) and the helmet rule rewrite.
No wattage cap: a 1,500 W bike that meets the class speed limits is a legal Oregon e-bike. This is a surprise compared with other states.
Wheel size: 'bicycle' needs wheels over 14 inches, so small-wheel folding e-bikes may not qualify (then a moped or, from 2027, possibly a powered micromobility device).
Local power to set e-bike age limits or path bans was not verified. Oregon State Parks e-bike trail rules were not checked.
Moped license and registration specifics were not verified.
OR.verifier_notes: 801.258 (no watt cap), 807.020(15) and 2026 Or. Laws ch. 101 operative dates confirmed. No corrections.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.has_three_class_law_notes: PA has a single 'pedalcycle with electric assist' category (Act 154 of 2014) with a 750 W motor rating, 20 mph on motor power alone and a 100 lb maximum. A three-class bill, HB 2703 (Rep. Cooper), and a study resolution, SR 322, are in the Transportation committees (palegis.us, referred July 15 and May 20, 2026).

definition.quote: A vehicle weighing not more than 100 pounds with two or three wheels more than 11 inches in diameter, manufactured or assembled with an electric motor system rated at not more than 750 watts and equipped with operable pedals
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor system rated at not more than 750 watts
definition.notes: The definition ends with 'capable of a speed not more than 20 miles per hour on a level surface when powered by the motor source only.' It adds two limits beyond the federal class model, a 100 lb maximum weight and wheels over 11 inches. 'Pedalcycle' includes a pedalcycle with electric assist, so all pedalcycle rules apply. Class 3 (28 mph assist) is not named. A pedal-only Class 3 meets the 'motor source only' test literally, but no official source confirms it, so its status is unclear (see verdict_cautions). It cannot be a motorized pedalcycle, whose design speed is capped at 25 mph. The legislative mirror page shows amendments through 2026.

label_required.citation: 75 Pa.C.S. Chapter 35 Subchapter A (no label provision)
label_required.quote: No person under 16 years of age shall operate a pedalcycle with electric assist.
label_required.notes: No e-bike label mandate exists in Title 75 §§ 102 and 3501-3514. The quote is the only e-bike operating rule, shown for context. Pending HB 2703 would likely add PeopleForBikes model labels (not verified).

min_age.quote: No person under 16 years of age shall operate a pedalcycle with electric assist.
min_age.exceptions: None in the statute.

helmet.quote: A person under 12 years of age shall not operate a pedalcycle or ride as a passenger on a pedalcycle unless the person is wearing a pedalcycle helmet
helmet.notes: 'Pedalcycle' includes e-assist bikes. Because operators must be 16+, this matters only for passengers under 12, including those in child seats and trailers. There is a religious exemption.

license_registration_insurance.citation: 75 Pa.C.S. § 102, PennDOT Driver and Vehicle Services Bulletin 14-21 (Dec 2014)
license_registration_insurance.quote: Pedalcycles with electric assist do not require titling, registration or insurance. The operator does not require a driver's license, but must be at least 16 years of age.
license_registration_insurance.notes: The quote is PennDOT guidance, not statute text. The statute reaches this result by classing e-assist bikes as pedalcycles. Local authorities may require registration of pedalcycles (§ 6109(a)(8)), which may reach e-bikes.

where_allowed.quote: A person shall not ride a pedalcycle upon a sidewalk in a business district unless permitted by official traffic-control devices, nor when a usable pedalcycle-only lane has been provided adjacent to the sidewalk.
where_allowed.roads: Pedalcycle rights and duties on roadways (§ 3501). Banned on freeways except by permit or designation (§ 3511).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Allowed on pedalcycle paths, yielding to pedestrians (§ 3508(a)). Trail access on DCNR and other lands is set by the land manager (not verified).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Allowed outside business districts, yielding to pedestrians and signaling before passing. In business districts only where signs permit, and not where a usable bike-only lane is next to the sidewalk (§ 3508).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Class 3 status is unclear (see verdict_cautions). If it counts as a pedalcycle with electric assist, the rules for other e-bikes apply, including the 16 and older age rule. If not, it is most likely a motor-driven cycle (license, registration, insurance).

local_authority.quote: Regulating the operation of pedalcycles and requiring their registration and inspection, and the payment of a reasonable registration fee.
local_authority.details: Locals may regulate pedalcycle operation and require registration. But § 6101 makes Title 75 uniform and bars local ordinances on matters it covers, so local age limits or bans that differ from state law are doubtful. HB 2703 would expressly let municipalities adopt e-bike ordinances. Some Pittsburgh suburbs adopted e-bike rules in 2026 (Hoodline, secondary).

non_ebike_devices.quote: an electric motor-driven cycle equipped with operable pedals and an automatic transmission powered by an electric battery or battery pack-powered electric motor with a maximum design speed of no more than 25 miles per hour.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorized pedalcycle (electric, pedals, 25 mph or less) or motor-driven cycle/motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: Per PennDOT Pub 944 (2-26 and 8-26), a motorized pedalcycle needs a Class C license, and motor-driven cycle rules apply, so it also needs registration and insurance (the 2-26 sheet marks both 'Yes'). No helmet is required. It is banned from limited-access highways, the minimum age is 16 and the design speed is capped at 25 mph. Over 25 mph it is a motor-driven cycle, which needs a Class M license (Class C if automatic and 50 cc or less), registration, insurance, and a helmet under 21. Over 750 W, over 100 lb, or no pedals likewise falls outside the e-bike definition. PennDOT warns that devices not defined in the Vehicle Code may not be legally operated on highways, sidewalks or bike lanes.

pending_changes.summary: Would replace the single definition with three classes (Class 3 is 28 mph pedal assist) and add a seat requirement, raise e-bike fines to $50 ($100 to $250 for careless injury), let PennDOT and local authorities limit or prohibit e-bikes on any highway or sidewalk, and bar license, registration or insurance mandates. It would take effect 60 days after enactment. Introduced July 14, 2026 and referred to House Transportation July 15, 2026, its last action as of Oct 16, 2026. Bills not passed by Nov 30, 2026 die.

Study resolution directing the Joint State Government Commission to study e-bikes and recommend an updated statutory and regulatory framework. Referred to Senate Transportation May 20, 2026, its last action as of Oct 16, 2026. A resolution cannot change the Vehicle Code.

open_questions: Class 3 status is unsettled. The 'motor source only' text literally admits a pedal-only 28 mph bike, and PennDOT's crash manual codes Class 3 as a bicycle, but secondary guides call it unrecognized. Treat it as unclear until PennDOT or a court rules or HB 2703 passes.
The statute text came from the legislature's legacy mirror (legis.state.pa.us/WU01), which shows 2026 amendments. The verifier read bill status on palegis.us.
Resolved by verifier. HB 2703 and SR 322 are still in the Transportation committees on palegis.us (referred July 15 and May 20, 2026).
How far local ordinances can go under § 6101 uniformity is unclear.

verdict_cautions.reason: Pennsylvania's one category tests speed only 'when powered by the motor source only' (20 mph or less). A pedal-only 28 mph Class 3 meets that text literally, and PennDOT's crash manual (Pub 153, 07-26) codes Class 1 to 3 as bicycles, but no statute, rule or PennDOT ruling says a 28 mph assist bike is a pedalcycle with electric assist. One whose throttle goes above 20 mph fails. Return unclear, never legal.

The definition covers only a vehicle 'weighing not more than 100 pounds' with wheels 'more than 11 inches in diameter'. Heavy family cargo e-bikes over 100 lb are not pedalcycles with electric assist. One capped at 25 mph is likely a motorized pedalcycle (Class C license, registration, insurance, 16 and older). If the weight of a cargo or long-tail bike is unknown, return unclear.

PA.verifier_notes: Class 1 and 2 are e-bikes for riders 16 and older if the bike weighs 100 lb or less and has wheels over 11 inches. Class 3 changed from not an e-bike to unclear, and a weight and wheel caution was added.

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.has_three_class_law_notes: P.L. 2024, ch.172 (H 7713A) and ch.173 (S 2829A), signed about June 17-18, 2024 and effective July 1, 2024, created chapter 31-19.7 (three classes, helmets under 21, Class 1 on state bike paths). The older 'electric motorized bicycle' definition in 31-1-3(g) (2 SAE hp) was kept and raised to 28 mph. No 2025 or 2026 amendment was found.

definition.quote: may be propelled by human power or electric motor power, or by both, with an electric motor rated not more than two (2) (S.A.E.) horsepower, that is capable of a maximum speed of not more than twenty-eight miles per hour
definition.motor_watts_basis: with an electric motor rated not more than two (2) (S.A.E.) horsepower
definition.notes: The statute caps power at 2 SAE horsepower, not watts. The 1,491 W figure is my conversion at 745.7 W per hp, not statute text. Two wheels only, and pedals are not expressly required. 31-19.7-1 classes: class 1 is pedal-assist to 20 mph, class 2 is 'throttle-actuated' to 20 mph, class 3 is pedal-assist to 28 mph. A throttle bike above 20 mph but at or under 28 mph fits 31-1-3(g) but no class. 'Motor vehicle' excludes electric motorized bicycles (31-1-3(u)).

label_required.citation: R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 31-19.7 (no label provision)
label_required.quote: There shall be three (3) classes of electric bicycles:
label_required.notes: Chapter 31-19.7 has only three sections (classes, state properties, helmets). No label mandate.

min_age.quote: provided, however, that an EPAMD and/or electric motorized bicycles shall not be operated in this state by a person under the age of sixteen (16) years.
min_age.exceptions: None stated. Applies to every 'electric motorized bicycle', which 31-1-3(g) equates with 'electric bicycle'.

helmet.quote: Any person under age twenty-one (21) who is operating or is a passenger on an electric bicycle on a public highway, bicycle trail or path, shared use path, park and/or recreational area, school property,
helmet.notes: Covers operators and passengers. The helmet must meet the CPSC standard. Separately, 31-19-2.1 requires helmets for bicycle riders 15 and younger.

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric personal assistive mobility device ("EPAMD") and electric motorized bicycles shall not be required to register under this chapter;
license_registration_insurance.notes: No registration. E-bikes are excluded from 'motor vehicle', so licensing and insurance laws for motor vehicles do not apply. The license rule in 31-19.1-1 covers 'motorized bicycle or motor scooter', a separate defined term (31-1-3(p)), not electric motorized bicycles.

where_allowed.quote: provided, however, that Class 1 electric bicycles shall be allowable on state bicycle trails or paths as defined by § 31-1-23.
where_allowed.roads: Not addressed in chapter 31-19.7. E-bikes are not motor vehicles. Whether chapter 31-19 bicycle rules apply was not verified.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 is allowed by statute on state bicycle trails and paths. DEM may regulate other uses on its properties (DEM proposed state-park rule amendments in March 2025, not read). Class 2 and 3 access to state paths depends on DEM rules.
where_allowed.sidewalks: Not addressed in the sections read.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Not expressly allowed on state bike paths (only class 1 is guaranteed). Otherwise the same as the other classes.

local_authority.quote: The department of environmental management may, by regulation, determine allowable uses of electric bicycles at properties under the department's jurisdiction;
local_authority.details: This is DEM (state) power over its properties. Municipal e-bike authority was not found in the sections read. 31-3-2.2(b) gives cities express power only over EPAMDs.

non_ebike_devices.quote: No person shall operate a motorized bicycle or motor scooter upon a highway in this state unless the person has a valid license as an operator
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorized bicycle (up to 4.9 hp, 50 cc or less, 30 mph or less) or motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A 'motorized bicycle' (31-1-3(p)) needs an operator license, age 16+, and registration (31-3-2.2(a)). It is banned from interstates (31-19.1-2). An electric two-wheeler over 2 SAE hp or over 28 mph is not an electric motorized bicycle. Whether it is a 'motorized bicycle' (whose definition mentions 50 cc) or a motorcycle is unclear. Three-wheel e-trikes fall outside the two-wheel e-bike definition ('motorized tricycles', 31-1-3(q), 1.5 bhp and 30 mph).

open_questions: Pedals are not expressly required by the RI definition. A pedal-less two-wheeler at 2 hp or less and 28 mph or less might count as an 'electric motorized bicycle' on a literal reading. Flag it, don't approve it.
A throttle bike above 20 mph (and at or under 28 mph) fits 31-1-3(g) but no class in 31-19.7-1. The legal effect is unclear.
DEM state-park e-bike rules (250-RICR-100-00-7, amended about 2025) were not read. Class 2 and 3 access to state bike paths depends on them. A press report mentioned bike-path limits.
Whether chapter 31-19 bicycle rules (roads, sidewalks) apply to e-bikes was not verified.

Resolved by verifier: 2026 H 7789 Sub A (retailer notice plus an under-16 road ban) passed the House but was held for further study in Senate Judiciary when the session ended June 11, 2026, so it is not law. No 2025 or 2026 e-bike act was found.
normalization_notes: definition.max_motor_watts 1491 -> null (the statute states no watt figure; see motor_watts_basis and max_motor_hp)
RI.verifier_notes: All quotes found. H 7789 Sub A died in the Senate. Two citation letter fixes.

SC.name: South Carolina

definition.quote: low-speed electrically assisted bicycles with two or three wheels, each having fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, or one horsepower, and a top motor-powered speed of less than twenty miles an hour
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, or one horsepower
definition.notes: No class system. One category, 'electric-assist bicycles' / 'bicycles with helper motors'. Requirements: fully operable pedals, motor no more than 750 W, top motor-powered speed LESS THAN 20 mph (a bike rated at exactly 20 mph does not literally meet this), must meet 16 C.F.R. Part 1512, and the motor must disengage or cease to function 'when their brakes are applied or the rider stops pedaling'. That last clause reads as pedal-assist only, so a Class 2 throttle bike that drives without pedaling, and any Class 3 (28 mph) bike, appear to fall OUTSIDE the definition. Statute says these bikes 'are not mopeds'. Added by 2020 Act No. 114 (H.3174).

label_required.quote: Manufacturers and distributors of electric-assist bicycles shall apply a label that is affixed permanently, in a prominent location, to each electric-assist bicycle, indicating its wattage and maximum electrically assisted speed.

license_registration_insurance.quote: Electric-assist bicycles and bicycles with helper motors are not mopeds.

where_allowed.quote: A person riding a bicycle upon a roadway must be granted all of the rights and is subject to all of the duties applicable to the driver of a vehicle by this chapter
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. Riders follow the bicycle rules (§ 56-5-3520 points to § 56-5-3420). Ride as far right as practicable (§ 56-5-3430). Freeway main lanes are closed to bicycles and 'a bicycle with motor attached'. Some non-interstate freeways can be opened by local ordinance (§ 56-5-3860).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Allowed. Bicyclists must use an adjacent bicycle lane when one is provided, with exceptions for passing and obstructions (§ 56-5-3425(B)(2)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: No statewide e-bike rule found for paths or trails. Land managers and local governments set their own rules.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No statewide e-bike or bicycle sidewalk rule found. § 56-5-3835 bars driving 'any vehicle' on a sidewalk. Whether an e-bike is a 'vehicle' under § 56-1-10(28) (which excludes devices moved by human power) is unclear. Local ordinances apply.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: SC has no Class 3 category. A 28 mph Class 3 bike does not meet the § 56-1-10(29) definition (top motor-powered speed must be less than 20 mph).

local_authority.quote: regulating the operation of bicycles and requiring the registration and licensing of them, including the requirement of a registration fee;
local_authority.details: Local authorities may regulate bicycle operation and require bicycle registration and licensing on streets under their jurisdiction. Because § 56-5-3520 applies bicycle law to e-bikes, this power appears to reach e-bikes. Several coastal towns (for example Hilton Head Island) have their own e-bike pathway rules. The power to set age limits is inferred from 'regulating the operation', not stated.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Moped" means a cycle, defined as a motor vehicle, with or without pedals, to permit propulsion by human power, that travels on not more than three wheels
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (electric input over 750 W up to 1500 W), otherwise motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: An electric cycle 'designed to have an input exceeding 750 watts and no more than 1500 watts' is a moped, with or without pedals. A moped needs a driver's license or a moped operator's license (issuable at 15, and under 16 limited to daylight unless accompanied) under § 56-1-1720, must be registered (Chapter 3 of Title 56 sets a biennial moped registration fee, § 56-3-760), and riders under 21 must wear an approved helmet on any 'two-wheeled motorized vehicle' (§ 56-5-3660). Above 1500 W it is a motorcycle. GAP: a bike at or under 750 W that has no pedals, has a throttle that works without pedaling, or reaches 20 mph or more under motor power fits neither the e-bike nor the moped definition. Because 'motor vehicle' covers every self-propelled vehicle (56-1-10(7)) and 'motorcycle' excludes only tractors and mopeds (56-1-10(8)), a two-wheeled one most likely counts as a motorcycle (license, registration, insurance). The app should not call it legal.

open_questions: Class 2 throttle bikes: the § 56-1-10(29) requirement that the motor cease when 'the rider stops pedaling' seems to exclude throttle-on-demand bikes. Need a DPS or court reading before the app treats a Class 2 bike as an electric-assist bicycle in SC.
Top speed is 'less than twenty miles an hour'. A Class 1 bike labeled 20 mph is at the limit, not under it. Need to decide how the engine treats exactly 20 mph.
Class 3 (28 mph) and >=20 mph or no-pedal bikes at or under 750 W fit neither the e-bike nor the moped definition. Classification unknown.

Helmet: no statewide helmet rule for electric-assist bicycles found, so helmet is []. But § 56-5-3660 requires a helmet under 21 on any 'two-wheeled motorized vehicle', while § 56-5-3520 says e-bike riders follow bicycle law. Not confirmed whether 3660 can reach a two-wheeled e-bike. The app could suggest a helmet for riders under 21 as a precaution.
Sidewalks: unclear whether an e-bike is a 'vehicle' barred from sidewalks by § 56-5-3835.

Could not run the SC Legislature's bill search (it needs a form POST). Secondary sources dated 2026 report no e-bike bill enacted in 2025-2026, and the official code pages show no 2025 or 2026 changes to §§ 56-1-10(29) or 56-5-3520. Confirm on scstatehouse.gov before launch.
SC.never_return_legal_reason: South Carolina's only category needs a top motor-powered speed of less than 20 mph and a motor that cuts out when the rider stops pedaling. Class 2 throttles and all Class 3 bikes fall outside it, a standard 20 mph Class 1 label does not literally meet 'less than twenty', and a two-wheeler that fails the definition most likely counts as a motorcycle (56-1-10(8)).
SC.verifier_notes: Definition confirmed. Set never_return_legal and an unknown helmet status (56-5-3660 under-21 rule).

SD.name: South Dakota

definition.quote: the term, electric bicycle, means a bicycle or a tricycle that is equipped with a seat or saddle, with operable pedals for propulsion, and with an electric motor of seven hundred fifty watts or less.
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of seven hundred fifty watts or less
definition.notes: Class I: assist only while pedaling, stops at 20 mph. Class II: motor can propel without pedaling, stops at 20 mph. Class III: assist only while pedaling, stops at 28 mph (SL 2019, ch 135). Electric bicycles are excluded from 'motor vehicle', 'moped', 'motorcycle' and 'off-road vehicle' (§§ 32-3-1, 32-14-1, 32-20-1). Odd text: § 32-20B-11 says every electric bicycle must be equipped so the motor 'is disengaged or ceases to function when the person stops pedaling or when the brakes are applied', which on its face conflicts with the Class II throttle definition.

label_required.quote: Beginning January 1, 2020, any person who manufacturers or distributes an electric bicycle in this state shall permanently affix to the electric bicycle a label that contains the following information:

min_age.quote: To operate a Class III electric bicycle in this state, a person shall be at least sixteen years of age.
min_age.exceptions: A person under 16 may ride as a passenger on a Class III bike designed to carry a passenger. No statewide minimum age for Class I or II.

helmet.quote: Any person who is less than eighteen years of age and operating a Class III electric bicycle ... shall wear a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet.
helmet.notes: Passengers on a Class III must also wear a helmet at any age. Operators 18 and older need none.

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric bicycle, as defined in § 32-20B-9, is exempt from this chapter.

where_allowed.quote: Unless otherwise prohibited by a governmental entity having jurisdiction, a person may operate a Class I or Class II electric bicycle on any bicycle path or multi-use path in this state.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. Electric bicycles are 'vehicles' (§ 32-14-1(39)) but not 'motor vehicles' (§ 32-14-1(17)), and bicycle rules in Chapter 32-20B apply (ride near the right edge, § 32-20B-5).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: No e-bike-specific bike lane rule found. Bicycle rules apply.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class I and II allowed on any bicycle or multi-use path unless the managing entity prohibits it. Class III allowed on natural-surface nonmotorized trails unless the managing entity prohibits it. George S. Mickelson Trail: only Class I is allowed. Other motorized vehicles, including Class II and III, are prohibited (§ 41-17-27(6), SL 2025, ch 178).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Chapter 32-20B allows bicycles on sidewalks with pedestrian rights and a duty to yield and give an audible signal (§§ 32-20B-2, 32-20B-3). Not confirmed whether 'bicycle' in those sections includes electric bicycles. Municipal ordinances may bar sidewalk riding.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Class III not allowed on a bicycle path or multi-use path unless it is within or adjacent to a highway or roadway, or the managing entity expressly permits it (§ 32-20B-12). Riders must be 16+ (§ 32-20B-13), riders under 18 and all passengers need a helmet (§ 32-20B-14), and the bike needs a working speedometer (§ 32-20B-15).

local_authority.quote: Unless otherwise prohibited by a governmental entity having jurisdiction, a person may operate a Class I or Class II electric bicycle on any bicycle path or multi-use path in this state.
local_authority.details: Governmental entities with jurisdiction over a path or trail can prohibit Class I and II there, and can permit Class III on paths not next to a road. No statute found that expressly lets local governments add e-bike age limits. City ordinances (for example Sioux Falls) may add rules.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Motorcycle," includes motorcycles, motorbikes, mopeds, bicycles with motor attached, and all motor operated vehicles of the bicycle or tricycle type
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motorcycle (a moped is a subtype of motorcycle)
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device that fails § 32-20B-9 (over 750 W, no operable pedals) is not an electric bicycle, so the exclusions fall away and it is a 'bicycle with motor attached', moped or motorcycle. That needs a motorcycle license or permit (motorcycle instruction permit from age 14, § 32-12-11.1), title and registration under Chapter 32-3, and riders under 18 must wear a DOT helmet (§ 32-20-4). Speed is not part of the base definition, so a 750 W bike whose assist goes past 28 mph has no class but is still arguably an 'electric bicycle'. That edge case is unresolved.

open_questions: § 32-20B-11 requires every electric bicycle's motor to stop 'when the person stops pedaling', which seems to clash with the Class II throttle definition in § 32-20B-9. No guidance found on how this is enforced.
A bike under 750 W with pedals but assist above 28 mph fits the base definition but no class. Status unclear.
Unclear whether the sidewalk rules for 'bicycles' in §§ 32-20B-2 and 32-20B-3 cover electric bicycles.

Resolved by verifier. The Legislature's bill list (api/Bills/Session/71) shows no 2026 e-bike bill. In 2025 only SB 79 (Mickelson Trail, enacted as SL 2025, ch 178) and HB 1125 (a share-the-road plate) touched bicycles.
SD.verifier_notes: Definition (750 W or less), Class III age 16 and the Class III helmet rule confirmed on sdlegislature.gov. No 2026 e-bike bill appears in the Legislature's bill list.

TN.name: Tennessee

definition.quote: equipped with two (2) or three (3) wheels, any of which is twenty inches (20") or more in diameter, fully operable pedals for human propulsion, and an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty (750) watts
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty (750) watts
definition.notes: Motor must be LESS THAN 750 W, so a bike labeled exactly 750 W does not literally qualify. At least one wheel must be 20 inches or more in diameter, so many kids' e-bikes with 16 inch wheels fall outside the definition. Class 1: assist only while pedaling, stops at 20 mph. Class 2: motor may propel the bike alone, no assist at 20 mph. Class 3: assist only while pedaling, stops at 28 mph. Enacted by 2016 Pub. Ch. 823 (SB 1705), codified §§ 55-8-301 to -307. Text read from the enrolled 2016 act and the TDOT bicycle-law page, which reproduces the code. The official Lexis code and Justia could not be opened (Lexis needs a terms click, Justia blocks bots).

label_required.quote: every manufacturer or distributor of new electric bicycles intended for sale or distribution in this state shall permanently affix, in a prominent location, to the electric bicycle a label that contains the classification number, top assisted speed, and motor wattage

min_age.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. § 55-8-307(a), as amended by 2026 Pub. Ch. 651 § 2
min_age.quote: Section 55-8-307(a), is amended by deleting the language "under fourteen (14) years of age" and substituting instead the language "under sixteen (16) years of age".
min_age.exceptions: Applies to operating a Class 3 bike 'upon any street or highway'. A younger person may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 bike designed for passengers. Violation is a delinquent act with a fine of no more than $50. Before July 1, 2026 the age was 14. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2.

helmet.quote: The operator and all passengers of a class 3 electric bicycle, regardless of age, shall wear a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet

helmet.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. § 55-52-105(1), applied to e-bikes through § 55-8-302
helmet.quote: For any person under sixteen (16) years of age to operate or be a passenger on a bicycle unless at all times when so engaged the person wears a protective bicycle helmet

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric bicycle and any person operating an electric bicycle is not subject to any requirements or laws applicable to motor vehicles, including the Tennessee Financial Responsibility Law of 1977

where_allowed.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. § 55-8-306(a), as amended by 2026 Pub. Ch. 651 § 1
where_allowed.quote: A class 1 electric bicycle or a class 2 electric bicycle may be operated on any part of a street or highway where bicycles are authorized to travel.
where_allowed.roads: Class 1 and 2 allowed anywhere bicycles may travel, but since April 1, 2026 a local government (by ordinance) or a state agency (by rule) may regulate or prohibit Class 1 and 2 on any part of a street or highway where bicycles travel, including state highways, for public safety. Class 3 needs a speedometer to be on a street or highway (§ 55-8-305(b)). Bicycle traffic rules apply (§ 55-8-172).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Class 1 and 2 allowed (bike lanes are part of 'any part of a street or highway where bicycles are authorized to travel'), subject to local or state-agency restriction. Class 3 allowed in bike lanes and on shoulders within or next to the street.
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 and 2 allowed on paths and trails intended for bicyclists unless a local government or state agency restricts them. Class 3 barred from paths and trails unless the path is within or adjacent to a street or highway or the local government or state agency permits it.
where_allowed.sidewalks: No electric bicycle on a sidewalk unless the local government or state agency authorizes bicycles on that sidewalk AND the electric motor is disabled (§ 55-8-306(a)(4), 2016 text, not changed by Pub. Ch. 651).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Not on paths or trails unless next to a road or permitted. Operator 16+ on streets and highways from July 1, 2026. Helmet for operator and all passengers at any age. Speedometer required.

local_authority.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. § 55-8-306(a)(2)(A), as amended by 2026 Pub. Ch. 651 § 1
local_authority.quote: A local government may regulate or prohibit, by resolution or ordinance, the operation of a class 1 electric bicycle or class 2 electric bicycle on any part of a street or highway where bicycles are authorized to travel
local_authority.details: Since April 1, 2026 local governments can regulate or ban Class 1 and 2 on any street, highway (including state highways), bike lane, shoulder, path or trail in their jurisdiction if needed for public safety. State agencies (for example state parks) can do the same by rule or policy. Local rules must use the state class definitions (§ 55-8-306(a)(5)). On roadways, e-bikes may be restricted to the same extent as bicycles (§ 55-8-306(b)). 'Regulate' plausibly includes age limits, but no statute names age limits expressly.

non_ebike_devices.quote: Yes, provided that the electric bicycle is self-propelled and is operated upon a highway.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motor vehicle (possibly motor-driven cycle or motorcycle)
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device that misses § 55-8-301(4) (motor 750 W or more, no wheel of at least 20 inches, no operable pedals, or no class) loses the § 55-8-302 exemption from motor-vehicle law. The 2014 AG opinion, written before the 2016 e-bike law, concluded that a self-propelled electric bicycle is a 'motor vehicle', needs a driver's license on a highway, and is a 'motor-driven cycle' only if it can keep up with posted highway speeds. The 'motorized bicycle' category is defined by engine cylinder capacity, so the AG said it does not fit electric motors. Registration, insurance and age then follow motor-vehicle law. The exact license class and minimum age were not confirmed.

pending_changes.effective_date: 2026-04-01 (Section 1, local and state-agency regulation, Class 3 path rule), 2026-07-01 (Section 2, Class 3 age 16)
pending_changes.summary: Already in force as of Oct 16, 2026. Lets local governments and state agencies regulate or ban Class 1 and 2 on any part of a street or highway where bicycles travel, restates the Class 3 path and trail limit, and raises the Class 3 minimum age from 14 to 16.

open_questions: Watt limit is 'less than' 750 W. Need a rule for bikes labeled exactly 750 W. Literal reading says they are not electric bicycles in TN.
Wheel-size rule (one wheel 20 inches or more) excludes small-wheel kids' e-bikes. The vision model must extract wheel size for TN, or the engine should return 'unclear'.

Under-16 helmet for Class 1 and 2: § 55-52-105 covers a 'bicycle' defined as 'human-powered' (§ 55-52-103). § 55-8-302 says bicycle laws in Title 55 apply to e-bikes. Recorded as applying, which is the cautious reading, but no court or agency ruling found.

The verifier did not open Lexis either. General Assembly records show only Pub. Ch. 388 (2019, scooters, which amended 55-8-101 and not the e-bike definition) and Pub. Ch. 651 (2026) touching these sections since 2016, so the 2016 text of 55-8-301(4), with 'less than' 750 W and the 20 inch wheel rule, is very likely current.
Exact license class and minimum age for a non-qualifying electric device were not confirmed.
Many cities (for example Nashville, Spring Hill, Collierville) may adopt new ordinances under the 2026 local-authority power. The app should warn that local rules may be stricter.

verdict_cautions.reason: Tennessee's definition needs two or three wheels 'any of which is twenty inches (20") or more in diameter'. A kids' e-bike with 12 to 18 inch wheels is not an electric bicycle in Tennessee and loses the exemption from motor-vehicle law. If wheel size is unknown for a youth or compact bike, return unclear.

TN.verifier_notes: Less than 750 W, the 20 inch wheel rule, Class 3 age 16 and the new local ban power confirmed in the enrolled acts. Pub. Ch. 651 was signed April 1, not April 6, 2026, and a wheel-size caution was added.

TX.name: Texas

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a bicycle: (A) equipped with: (i) fully operable pedals; and (ii) an electric motor of fewer than 750 watts; and (B) with a top assisted speed of 28 miles per hour or less.
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of fewer than 750 watts
definition.notes: Motor must be FEWER THAN 750 W, so a bike labeled exactly 750 W does not literally qualify. Class 1: pedal assist only, top assisted speed 20 mph or less. Class 2: motor may propel without pedaling, 20 mph or less. Class 3: pedal assist only, top assisted speed 'more than 20 but less than 28' mph, so a bike assisting to exactly 28 mph is an electric bicycle but fits no class. An e-bike must first be a 'bicycle' (§ 541.201(2)), which requires at least one wheel more than 14 inches in diameter. Electric bicycles are excluded from 'motor vehicle' (§ 541.201(11)). Enacted by HB 2188 (2019). § 551.107(b) also requires the motor to stop when the operator stops pedaling OR when the brakes are applied.

label_required.quote: A person who manufactures or sells an electric bicycle shall apply a permanent label to the electric bicycle in a prominent location that shows in Arial font in at least 9-point type:

min_age.quote: A person may not operate a Class 3 electric bicycle, as defined by Section 664.001, unless the person is at least 15 years of age.
min_age.exceptions: A person under 15 may ride a Class 3 bike as a passenger. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2.

license_registration_insurance.quote: Subtitles A, B, and D and Chapter 551A do not apply to the operation of an electric bicycle.

where_allowed.quote: may not prohibit the operation of an electric bicycle: (1) on a highway that is used primarily by motor vehicles; or (2) in an area in which the operation of a nonelectric bicycle is permitted
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. Bicycle rules apply to electric bicycles (§ 551.002). TxDOT and local authorities may not ban e-bikes from highways used mainly by motor vehicles.
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Allowed wherever regular bicycles are allowed (§ 551.106(a)(2)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: All classes allowed wherever regular bicycles are allowed, except that TxDOT or a local authority may ban e-bikes on a path that is closed to motor vehicles and has a natural-surface tread made by clearing and grading native soil. No separate statewide Class 3 path ban. State parks and federal land may have their own rules (not researched).
where_allowed.sidewalks: No statewide ban. TxDOT or a local authority may prohibit bicycles (and so e-bikes) on sidewalks (§ 551.106(b)(1)). Many cities do so in business districts.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Operator must be 15+ (§ 551.107(c)). Seller or manufacturer must equip a speedometer (§ 664.004). No statewide Class 3 path restriction beyond the natural-surface trail rule that applies to all e-bikes.

local_authority.quote: The department or a local authority may: (1) prohibit the operation of a bicycle on a sidewalk; and (2) establish speed limits for bicycles on paths
local_authority.details: Narrow. Local authorities may NOT prohibit e-bikes on highways or anywhere nonelectric bicycles are allowed, except natural-surface trails closed to motor vehicles. They may ban bicycle (and e-bike) riding on sidewalks and set bicycle speed limits on paths. No statute found that lets cities set e-bike age limits, and § 551.106(a) arguably preempts outright local e-bike bans.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Moped" means a motor vehicle that is equipped with a rider's saddle ... that cannot attain a speed in one mile of more than 30 miles per hour
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (cannot exceed 30 mph, motor of 5 brake horsepower or less) or motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device with a motor of 750 W or more, assist above 28 mph, or no operable pedals is not an electric bicycle, so it is a 'motor vehicle'. If it cannot go over 30 mph and the motor makes no more than 5 brake horsepower it is a moped. Otherwise it is a motorcycle (§ 541.201(9)). Mopeds and motorcycles need a driver's license (Chapter 521), title and registration, and liability insurance (Chapter 601). Small seated no-pedal devices with an electric motor that are not designed for highway use can be 'pocket bikes or minimotorbikes' (§ 551.351(2)), which Chapter 551 does not authorize on roads, bicycle paths or sidewalks (§ 551.353). The license class and minimum age for a moped were not verified from statute here.

open_questions: Watt limit is 'fewer than 750 watts'. Need a rule for bikes labeled exactly 750 W. Literal reading says they are not electric bicycles in Texas.
A bike assisting to exactly 28 mph is an electric bicycle (28 or less) but not a Class 3 ('less than 28'). How the age-15 rule applies to it is unclear. Cautious reading: treat it as Class 3.
Bicycle definition needs a wheel over 14 inches. Small-wheel kids' e-bikes may not be electric bicycles.
§ 551.107(b) says the motor must stop when the operator stops pedaling or when the brakes are applied. A Class 2 throttle bike must therefore have a brake cutoff.

Texas has no regular session in 2026. Confirmed on capitol.texas.gov that SB 1865 (referred to Transportation Mar 17, 2025) and HB 4089 (left pending in committee May 8, 2025) died. Chapters 551 and 664 show no 2025 amendments. SB 2039 (2025) only defined 'sidewalk user' (541.001), which includes bicycle riders on sidewalks.
State park, river authority and city trail rules can differ. Not researched.

verdict_cautions.reason: An electric bicycle must first be a 'bicycle', which needs a wheel 'more than 14 inches in diameter' (541.201(2)). E-balance bikes and compact folders whose wheels are all 14 inches or smaller are not electric bicycles in Texas and lose the e-bike exemptions. If wheel size is unknown for a small bike, return unclear.

TX.verifier_notes: Fewer than 750 W, Class 3 age 15 and the narrow local powers confirmed on the official statutes, with no 2025 change. Added a caution because a bike needs a wheel over 14 inches to count.

UT.name: Utah

definition.quote: "Electric assisted bicycle" means a bicycle with an electric motor that: (i) has a power output of not more than 750 watts; (ii) has fully operable pedals;
definition.motor_watts_basis: has a power output of not more than 750 watts
definition.notes: Version in force since Oct 1, 2026 (amended by 2026 HB 381, Laws 2026 ch. 334, eff. May 6, 2026, and again by Laws 2026 ch. 292, eff. Oct 1, 2026). Also must be fully operable as a bicycle without the motor and be Class 1, 2, 3 or a 'programmable electric assisted bicycle' (switchable between classes, conforming to each class in that mode). Class 3 must have a speedometer. EXCLUDED: mopeds, motor assisted scooters, electric motorcycles, motorcycles, and any vehicle that is designed, advertised, modifiable or modified to reach '20 miles per hour or greater on motor power alone', has continuous rated power over 750 W, has foot pegs, needs a pedal kit, or has a throttle mode over 20 mph. A 'bicycle' needs wheels at least 14 inches in diameter (§ 41-6a-102(7)). A tampered or modified e-bike becomes a 'high power electric device'.

label_required.quote: Beginning January 1, 2017, each Utah-based manufacturer of an electric assisted bicycle and each distributor of an electric assisted bicycle in Utah shall permanently affix a label in a prominent location on the electric assisted bicycle.

min_age.quote: An individual under 16 years old may not operate a class 3 electric assisted bicycle.
min_age.exceptions: None stated. This subsection is dropped from the version that takes effect May 5, 2027.

min_age.quote: An individual under 14 years old may not operate an electric assisted bicycle with the electric motor engaged on any public property, highway, path, or sidewalk unless the individual is under the direct supervision of the individual's parent or guardian.
min_age.exceptions: Ages 8 to 13 may ride with the motor engaged only under the direct supervision of a parent or guardian. Riding with the motor off is not restricted.

min_age.quote: An individual under eight years old may not operate an electric assisted bicycle with the electric motor engaged on any public property, highway, path, or sidewalk.
min_age.exceptions: No supervision exception. Applies only with the electric motor engaged on public property, highways, paths or sidewalks.

helmet.quote: An individual under 21 years old may not operate or ride the following on a highway unless the individual is wearing protective headgear that complies with specifications adopted under Subsection (4): (a) a motorcycle; (b) an electric assisted bicycle;
helmet.notes: Applies on highways. Riders of a Class 1 e-bike rented from a business are exempt (41-6a-1505(3)).

license_registration_insurance.quote: "Motor vehicle" does not include: (i) vehicles moved solely by human power; (ii) motorized wheelchairs; (iii) an electric personal assistive mobility device; (iv) an electric assisted bicycle;

where_allowed.quote: An individual may operate an electric assisted bicycle on a path or trail designated for the use of a bicycle.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. An electric assisted bicycle follows the bicycle rules in Chapter 6a (§ 41-6a-1115.5(1)). Helmet required under 21 on a highway. Open-container rule of § 41-6a-526 applies.
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Allowed. 'Bicycle lane' is defined to include electric assisted bicycle traffic (§ 41-6a-102(8)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Allowed on paths and trails designated for bicycles, unless a local authority or state agency restricts e-bikes or a class there (§ 41-6a-1115.5(3)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Bicycle sidewalk rules apply: yield to pedestrians, give an audible signal, ride at a prudent speed. Riders 18+ may not ride where a sign or ordinance prohibits it (§ 41-6a-1106). Local authorities may separately regulate or restrict e-bikes on sidewalks (§ 41-6a-1115.5(3)).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Operator must be 16+ (until May 5, 2027). Speedometer required by definition. No statewide Class 3 path ban, but locals and state agencies may restrict a specific class on sidewalks, paths and trails.

local_authority.quote: A local authority or state agency may adopt an ordinance or rule to regulate or restrict the use of an electric assisted bicycle, or a specific classification of an electric assisted bicycle, on a sidewalk, path, or trail
local_authority.details: Local authorities and state agencies may regulate or restrict e-bikes, or one class, on sidewalks, paths and trails. No matching power found for roadways. 'Regulate or restrict' plausibly covers age limits, but age is not named.

non_ebike_devices.quote: An individual operating a high power electric device, including an electric motorcycle, has all rights and is subject to all provisions of this chapter applicable to an operator of a motorcycle.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: high power electric device or electric motorcycle (motorcycle rules apply)
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device that can exceed 20 mph on motor power alone is a 'high power electric device'. That includes an e-bike tampered with or modified to change speed or power. One over 750 W or able to exceed 20 mph on the motor alone can be an 'electric motorcycle'. Under 16 may not operate a high power electric device on a highway (§ 41-6a-1511(3)). No freeway use. Riders under 21 need a DOT (49 C.F.R. 571.218) helmet (§ 41-6a-1505). A high power electric device without a VIN that is not a motorcycle is exempt from liability insurance (§ 41-6a-1511(1)(b)). Whether a motorcycle license or endorsement and registration are required for each kind of device was not confirmed, so license_needed is null. Sellers must give a 'not an electric assisted bicycle' disclosure.

pending_changes.bill: HB 381 (2026), Electric Mobility Device Amendments, Laws of Utah 2026 ch. 334, delayed sections
pending_changes.summary: Rewrites § 41-6a-1115.5. Ages 8 to 15 may ride an e-bike with the motor engaged on a highway only with direct supervision of a parent or responsible adult OR a state personal electric vehicle safety certificate (new § 41-6a-1512, online course). Age 16+ may ride unsupervised. Under 8 barred on highways. The separate 'under 16 may not operate a class 3' rule is dropped from § 41-6a-1115.5. Under 16 barred from freeways. Officers may hold a minor's device. Most other HB 381 sections (helmet under 21, high power electric device rules, definitions) already took effect May 6, 2026.

open_questions: Class 2 throttle at exactly 20 mph: the § 41-6a-102(21)(b)(v)(A) exclusion covers a vehicle able to reach '20 miles per hour or greater on motor power alone'. A Class 2 bike whose throttle tops out at 20 mph may fall into the exclusion. Need DPS guidance. Until then the engine should not call a Class 2 bike legal in Utah without a caveat.
Class 3 bikes with a throttle that works above 20 mph are excluded (§ 41-6a-102(21)(b)(v)(D)). The vision model needs to capture throttle limits.
Helmet exception: § 41-6a-1505(3) exempts riders of a rented Class 1 e-bike. Not modeled in the helmet object.

Resolved by verifier. Laws of Utah 2026 ch. 292 is HB 22, Vintage Vehicle Amendments (effective Oct 1, 2026). Its subject is vintage vehicles, and the Oct 1, 2026 text of the e-bike definitions matches the one recorded here.
License and registration duties for high power electric devices and electric motorcycles were not confirmed.
From May 5, 2027 the Class 3 age-16 rule disappears from § 41-6a-1115.5. Confirm it is not restated elsewhere before updating the table.

verdict_cautions.reason: The definition excludes any vehicle able to reach '20 miles per hour or greater on motor power alone', which may catch a Class 2 throttle that tops out at exactly 20 mph.

Utah's 'bicycle' must have wheels 'not less than 14 inches in diameter', and an electric assisted bicycle must be a bicycle. A 12 inch e-balance bike is not an e-bike in Utah. If wheel size is unknown for a small bike, return unclear.

The definition excludes a bike with foot pegs at manufacture, one that needs a pedal kit, and a multi-mode throttle bike with any mode above 20 mph on motor power alone. A throttle that tops out at exactly 20 mph is the Class 2 gray zone, which has its own line for Class 2. A class label does not show these, so the app asks before it can say yes.

UT.verifier_notes: HB 381 helmet rule (under 21 on highways), the current age rules and the May 5, 2027 changes confirmed on le.utah.gov, and ch. 292 is a vintage-vehicle bill. Added wheel-size and throttle cautions.

VA.name: Virginia

definition.quote: equipped with (i) pedals that allow propulsion by human power, (ii) a seat for the use of the rider, and (iii) an electric motor with an input of no more than 750 watts.
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor with an input of no more than 750 watts
definition.notes: Class one: pedal assist only, stops at 20 mph. Class two: motor may propel the bike alone, stops at 20 mph. Class three: pedal assist only, stops at 28 mph. Not a motor vehicle (§ 46.2-100 'Motor vehicle'). Three-class scheme from 2020 Acts cc. 59, 260 (HB 543 / SB 662). § 46.2-904.1(E) also requires the motor to stop 'when the rider stops pedaling or when the brakes are applied'. § 46.2-908.1 requires spill-proof, sealed or gelled batteries. § 46.2-100 was last amended in 2025 (cc. 163, 177), not on e-bike points as far as checked.

label_required.quote: On and after January 1, 2021, manufacturers and distributors of electric power-assisted bicycles shall permanently affix a label, in a prominent location, to each electric power-assisted bicycle that they manufacture or distribute.

min_age.quote: No person less than 14 years old shall drive any electric personal assistive mobility device, motorized skateboard or scooter, or class three electric power-assisted bicycle unless under the immediate supervision of a person who is at least 18 years old.
min_age.exceptions: Under 14 may ride a Class 3 bike under the immediate supervision of a person 18 or older. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2.

helmet.quote: Each operator and passenger of a class three electric power-assisted bicycle shall wear a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet

license_registration_insurance.quote: An electric power-assisted bicycle or person operating an electric power-assisted bicycle is not subject to the provisions of this Code relating to requirements for driver's licenses, registration, certificates of title, financial responsibility

where_allowed.quote: an electric power-assisted bicycle may be ridden in places where bicycles are allowed, including streets, highways, roads, shoulders, bicycle lanes, and bicycle or shared-use paths.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed wherever bicycles are allowed. Banned on Interstate Highway System components except barrier-separated facilities the Commonwealth Transportation Board approves (§ 46.2-908.1).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Allowed on bicycle and shared-use paths. After notice and a public hearing, a locality or state agency may ban Class 1 or 2 on a path for public safety or legal compliance. It may ban Class 3 on a path without that process. Natural-surface nonmotorized trails may be regulated by the managing body (§ 46.2-904.1(F)(1)-(3)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Allowed. § 46.2-903 exempts electric power-assisted bicycles from the ban on vehicles on sidewalks. Riders must yield to pedestrians and give an audible signal before passing. Localities may ban riding on designated sidewalks and crosswalks by ordinance with posted signs (§ 46.2-904).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Under 14 only with immediate supervision by someone 18+. Helmet for every operator and passenger. Speedometer required (§ 46.2-904.1(C)(3)). A locality or state agency may ban Class 3 on any bicycle or shared-use path.

local_authority.quote: The governing body of any county, city, or town may, by ordinance, provide that every person 14 years of age or younger shall wear a protective helmet
local_authority.details: Localities may (1) require helmets for riders 14 and under on any e-bike on highways, sidewalks and public bicycle paths (§ 46.2-906.1, last amended 2026 c. 114), (2) ban e-bike riding on designated sidewalks and crosswalks (§ 46.2-904), and (3) ban Class 3 on paths, and Class 1 and 2 on paths after a hearing (§ 46.2-904.1(F)). Several Northern Virginia localities (for example Fairfax, Loudoun) have helmet ordinances. No statute found letting localities set e-bike minimum ages. The July 1, 2026 effective date for c. 114 is the usual Virginia date and was not confirmed in the act.

non_ebike_devices.quote: No moped shall be driven on any highway by any person under the age of 16, and every person driving a moped shall carry with him a government-issued form of photo identification
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (electric motor up to 1500 W, seat at least 24 inches, not over 35 mph), motorcycle if faster, possibly 'motorized skateboard or scooter' if under 100 lb, no VIN, 20 mph or less
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device over 750 W, or without pedals, is not an electric power-assisted bicycle. With a seat 24 inches or higher, an electric motor of 1500 W or less and use at 35 mph or less, it is a moped: no one under 16 on highways, photo ID required, no Interstates (§ 46.2-914). Over 35 mph it is treated as a motorcycle needing a motorcycle license, registration and insurance. A light (<100 lb), VIN-less electric device capped at 20 mph that lets the rider sit or stand can be a 'motorized skateboard or scooter' (under 14 needs supervision). Moped registration, insurance and helmet duties were not checked in statute here.

open_questions: Partly resolved by the verifier. LIS lists 46.2-906.1 (c. 114) as the only 2026 change among the e-bike sections, and its current text still lets localities require helmets for e-bike riders 14 and under. The 2026 update list shows no change to 46.2-100, 46.2-904.1 or 46.2-908.1.
§ 46.2-904.1(E) requires the motor to stop when the rider stops pedaling or when the brakes are applied. A Class 2 throttle bike needs a brake cutoff.
Moped registration, insurance and helmet rules were not verified for the non-e-bike case.
Local helmet ordinances (14 and under) vary by county and city. The app should prompt for locality in Northern Virginia.
Effective dates of 2020 Acts cc. 59 and 260 are recorded as July 1, 2020, Virginia's default date for regular-session acts (Va. Const. art. IV, § 13). Not confirmed from the chapter text.
VA.verifier_notes: Definition (no more than 750 W input), Class 3 rules, sidewalk rules and the local helmet power confirmed on law.lis.virginia.gov. The e-bike sections read as recorded, and the only 2026 change among them is c. 114 on local helmet ordinances.

VT.name: Vermont

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a bicycle equipped with fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat for the rider, and an electric motor of less than 750 watts that meets the requirements of one of the following three classes:
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than 750 watts
definition.notes: Motor must be LESS THAN 750 W, so a bike labeled exactly 750 W does not literally qualify. Class 1: pedal assist only, stops at 20 mph. Class 2: motor may propel the bike alone, no assist at 20 mph. Class 3: pedal assist only, stops at 28 mph. An electric bicycle 'is not a motor vehicle' (§ 4(46)(B)). Added by 2021 Act No. 40 (S.66). § 1136a(c) also says the motor must disengage 'when the operator stops pedaling or applies the brakes'. 2021 Act No. 40 Sec. 10 makes all sections effective July 1, 2021, except the labeling rules (Sec. 7), effective January 1, 2022.

label_required.quote: Manufacturers and distributors of electric bicycles shall apply a label that is permanently affixed, in a prominent location, to each electric bicycle.

min_age.quote: An individual under 16 years of age shall not operate a class 3 electric bicycle but may ride as a passenger on a class 3 electric bicycle that is designed to accommodate passengers.
min_age.exceptions: Under 16 may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 bike designed for passengers. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2.

license_registration_insurance.quote: Electric bicycles and their operators shall be exempt from: (1) motor vehicle registration, inspection, and certificate of title requirements

where_allowed.quote: An electric bicycle may be ridden in places where bicycles are allowed, including highways, bicycle lanes, and bicycle or multiuse paths.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. E-bikes are governed as bicycles and riders have bicyclists' rights and duties (§ 1136a(a)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Allowed on bicycle and multiuse paths. After notice and a public hearing, the managing municipality, local authority or State agency may ban Class 1 or 2 on a path for safety or legal reasons. It may ban Class 3 on a path without that process. On natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized, the path rules do not apply and the managing body may regulate e-bikes (§ 1136a(e)(2)-(4)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: No statewide e-bike or bicycle sidewalk ban found. § 1132 bars only motor vehicles from sidewalks, and e-bikes are not motor vehicles. Municipal ordinances may regulate.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Operator must be 16+. Must have a speedometer (§ 1136a(d)). The managing body may ban Class 3 from any bicycle or multiuse path.

local_authority.quote: A municipality, local authority, or State agency having jurisdiction over a bicycle or multiuse path may prohibit the operation of a class 3 electric bicycle on that path.
local_authority.details: Path-level bans: Class 3 at will, Class 1 and 2 only after notice, public hearing and a safety or legal finding. Natural-surface nonmotorized trails may be regulated freely. General municipal power over bicycles under 24 V.S.A. § 2291 was not reviewed. No statute expressly lets towns add e-bike age limits.

non_ebike_devices.quote: A person under 16 years of age shall not operate a motor-assisted bicycle on a highway in Vermont.
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: motor-assisted bicycle (up to 1,000 W and 20 mph, not in a class); above that a motor-driven cycle or motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: An electric bike with pedals, a motor up to 1,000 W and a motor-only top speed of no more than 20 mph that does not meet a class (for example 750 W or more) is a 'motor-assisted bicycle'. It is governed as a bicycle with no registration, inspection or license, but may not be ridden on a sidewalk and under-16s may not ride it on a highway.
