Anything faster or stronger is a 'motor-driven cycle' (up to 2 brake horsepower and 30 mph) or a 'motorcycle', which are motor vehicles needing a license, registration and insurance. license_needed=false and min_age=16 describe the motor-assisted bicycle tier only.

open_questions: Watt limit is 'less than 750 watts'. Need a rule for bikes labeled exactly 750 W. Literal reading puts them in the 'motor-assisted bicycle' tier (no sidewalks, 16+ on highways).
Helmet: no Vermont statute requiring bicycle or e-bike helmets was found in Chapter 13, subchapter 12. One secondary site claims an under-16 helmet rule. Recorded as no statewide requirement.
§ 1136a(c) motor cutoff 'when the operator stops pedaling or applies the brakes'. A Class 2 throttle bike needs a brake cutoff.
No 2025-2026 e-bike changes found. 2026 Act No. 153 (S.326) amended § 4 for kei vehicles, not e-bikes.
VT.verifier_notes: 1136a, 1136 and 4(45)-(46) confirmed. No 2025 or 2026 e-bike change found. No corrections.

WA.name: Washington

definition.quote: "Electric-assisted bicycle" does not include: (a) Any vehicle capable of exceeding 20 miles per hour on solely its electric motor; or (b) Any vehicle that is designed, manufactured, or intended by the manufacturer or seller to be easily configured
definition.motor_watts_basis: The electric-assisted bicycle's electric motor must have a power output of no more than 750 watts.
definition.notes: Base definition (2018 c 60): a bicycle with two or three wheels, a saddle, fully operative pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 W, meeting one of three classes. Class 1: pedal assist only, stops at 20 mph. Class 2: motor may propel alone, no assist at 20 mph. Class 3: pedal assist only, stops at 28 mph, must have a speedometer. Since June 11, 2026 (2026 c 159, ESSB 6110) the definition excludes any vehicle able to exceed 20 mph on the motor alone (so a Class 3 bike with a throttle that works above 20 mph is out) and any vehicle designed or sold to be easily switched (button, software, app) out of the e-bike limits. The legislature noted that excluded vehicles often meet the 'moped' or 'motorcycle' definitions.

label_required.quote: Beginning July 1, 2018, permanently affix, in a prominent location, a label printed in arial font and at least nine-point type that contains the classification number, top assisted speed, and motor wattage;

min_age.quote: No driver's license is required for operation of an electric-assisted bicycle. Persons under sixteen years of age may not operate a class 3 electric-assisted bicycle.
min_age.exceptions: None stated. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2.

license_registration_insurance.quote: Subsections (1), (2), and (4) of this section do not apply to electric-assisted bicycles.

where_allowed.quote: Class 3 electric-assisted bicycles may not be operated on a shared-use path, except where local jurisdictions may allow the use of class 3 electric-assisted bicycles.
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. E-bikes may use highways and park to the same extent as bicycles (RCW 46.61.710(6)). Bicycle rules apply (RCW 46.37.690(3)).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Class 1 and 2 allowed on any part of a highway designated for bicycles. Class 3 allowed on facilities within or adjacent to a highway (RCW 46.61.710(7)-(8)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 and 2 allowed on shared-use paths unless a local jurisdiction or state agency restricts them. Class 3 barred from shared-use paths unless the local jurisdiction allows it. ALL classes barred from natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized unless the managing authority allows them (RCW 46.61.710(9)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Class 3 barred from sidewalks unless there is no alternative as part of a bicycle or pedestrian path, or a local ordinance authorizes it (RCW 46.61.710(3), 46.61.715). No statewide sidewalk ban for Class 1 or 2 found. Local rules apply.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Operator 16+. Speedometer required by definition. No shared-use paths or sidewalks unless locally allowed.

local_authority.quote: local jurisdictions or state agencies may restrict or otherwise limit the access of electric-assisted bicycles and motorized foot scooters
local_authority.details: Local jurisdictions and state agencies may restrict, limit or regulate Class 1 and 2 on facilities, properties and rights-of-way they control, and regulate Class 3 on their facilities. Local rules on a shared-use path crossing several jurisdictions must be consistent along the whole path (except rules in effect Jan 1, 2018). Bicycle helmet rules are local in Washington, and e-bike riders must follow 'all laws and regulations related to the use of bicycle helmets' (RCW 46.37.530(1)(c)). 'Regulate' plausibly covers age limits but age is not named.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Moped" means a motorized device designed to travel with not more than three wheels in contact with the ground and having an electric or a liquid fuel motor
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (electric, no more than 2 gross brake horsepower and 30 mph) or motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device that misses RCW 46.04.169 (over 750 W, can exceed 20 mph on motor alone, easily reconfigurable, no operative pedals) is not an e-bike. If its motor makes no more than 2 gross brake horsepower and it cannot exceed 30 mph it is a moped: a valid driver's license of any class is needed, so in practice 16+ (RCW 46.20.500(2)), moped registration and permit (RCW 46.61.710(1)), a motorcycle helmet (RCW 46.37.530), no sidewalks and no bicycle paths or trails. Otherwise it is a motorcycle needing a motorcycle endorsement. A Department of Licensing work group (2026 c 159 § 3) is studying a new framework for electric motorcycles. Interim report due Dec 15, 2026.

pending_changes.effective_date: 2026-03-23 (work group), and the definition change took effect 2026-06-11
pending_changes.summary: Definition change is already in force (see definition). The DOL work group must send an interim report with draft legislation on electric motorcycle classification by Dec 15, 2026 and a final report by Oct 31, 2027. Expect new e-motorcycle and possibly e-bike age or licensing bills in the 2027 session.

WA.pending_changes_notes: HB 2374 (2026), 'Concerning electric-assisted bicycle and electric motorcycle regulation', died in House Rules when the 2026 session ended. No Washington e-bike law with a future effective date exists. Changes would come in the 2027 session, which starts in January, likely from the DOL work group's draft legislation.
open_questions: Class 2 throttle at exactly 20 mph: excluded only if 'capable of exceeding 20 miles per hour on solely its electric motor'. A bike capped at 20 mph is not excluded. Bikes with 'off-road' or unlocked modes are excluded under (2)(b).
Effective date for RCW 46.61.710 recorded as July 28, 2019 (90 days after the 2019 session). 2019 c 214 has its own effective-date note that was not opened.

No statewide helmet law. Some Washington cities and counties have had bicycle helmet ordinances, and RCW 46.37.530(1)(c) makes e-bike riders follow them. Which ones are in force now was not checked (King County's all-ages rule was reported repealed in 2022, unverified). The app needs local data.
Class 1 and 2 sidewalk riding is not addressed statewide for e-bikes. Local ordinances control.

verdict_cautions.reason: An electric-assisted bicycle must be a 'bicycle', and RCW 46.04.071 needs two tandem wheels 'either of which is sixteen inches or more', or three wheels with one of 20 inches or more. A 12 or 14 inch kids' e-bike likely counts as a moped (driver's license, moped permit). If wheel size is unknown for a small bike, return unclear.

Since June 11, 2026 the definition excludes any vehicle that can exceed 20 mph on its motor alone and any bike sold to be easily switched out of the class limits by a button, setting or app. A Class 2 or 3 label does not show this, so the app asks before it can say yes.

WA.verifier_notes: ESSB 6110 definition change (June 11, 2026), the Class 3 age 16 and path rules confirmed on the RCW site. The only pending item is the DOL work group report due Dec 15, 2026, and wheel and motor-only speed cautions were added.

WI.name: Wisconsin

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a bicycle that is equipped with fully operative pedals for propulsion by human power and an electric motor of 750 watts or less and that meets the requirements of any of the following classifications:
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of 750 watts or less
definition.notes: Class 1: pedal assist only, stops at 20 mph. Class 2: may be powered solely by the motor, no assist at 20 mph. Class 3: pedal assist only, stops at 28 mph, speedometer required to operate (§ 347.489(3m)(d)). Not a 'motor vehicle', 'moped' or 'motor bicycle' (§ 340.01(29m)(bm), (30), (35)). Created by 2019 Wis. Act 34. Statute PDFs are the official 2023-24 Wis. Stats. updated through 2025 Wis. Act 247, published Oct 1, 2026. § 347.489(3m)(c) says the motor must stop when the brakes are applied OR when the rider stops pedaling.

label_required.quote: After January 1, 2018, a manufacturer or distributor of electric bicycles shall permanently affix to the electric bicycle a label containing all of the following information in Arial font of a minimum size of 9 point:

min_age.quote: No person under the age of 16 years may operate a class 3 electric bicycle. A person under the age of 16 years may ride as a passenger on a class 3 electric bicycle that is designed to accommodate passengers.
min_age.exceptions: Under 16 may ride as a passenger on a Class 3 bike designed for passengers. No statewide minimum age for Class 1 or 2.

license_registration_insurance.quote: A person operating an electric bicycle is not subject to the provisions under ch. 341, 342, 343, or 344 relating to financial responsibility, operator's licenses, registration, or certificates of title.

where_allowed.quote: A person may ride, with the power unit in operation, an electric bicycle upon a bikeway, as defined under s. 84.60 (1) (a), under the jurisdiction of the department of natural resources, subject to any restrictions
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. E-bikes have the same rights and duties as bicycles under chs. 340-351 (§ 346.806(1)), and bicycle provisions of ch. 346 apply to e-bikes (§ 346.02(4)(a)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: All classes may ride with the motor on along bikeways (as defined in § 84.60(1)(a)) run by DNR, DOT, a municipality or a county, subject to their rules. A municipality or county may ban powered e-bike use on its bikeways by ordinance, and DNR may do so by rule (§ 349.18(4)). No separate statewide Class 3 path ban found.
where_allowed.sidewalks: Not allowed unless local authorities permit it. The operator of a vehicle may not drive on a sidewalk unless permitted by local authorities (§ 346.94(1)), and an e-bike is a vehicle to the same extent as a bicycle. Where permitted, riders must yield to pedestrians (§ 346.804).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Operator 16+. Must have a working speedometer to be operated (§ 347.489(3m)(d)).

local_authority.quote: The governing body of a municipality or county may by ordinance prohibit the operation, with the power unit in operation, of electric bicycles on bikeways, as defined under s. 84.60 (1) (a), under its jurisdiction.
local_authority.details: Cities, towns and villages may regulate bicycles by ordinance (§ 349.18(2)), which reaches e-bikes through § 346.806(1). Municipalities and counties may ban powered e-bikes on their bikeways (§ 349.18(4)(a)), and DNR may by rule (§ 349.18(4)(b)). Local authorities decide whether bicycles may use sidewalks. The statutes' annotation cites a 1977 AG opinion that cities cannot license bicyclists without express legislative authority. No statute expressly authorizes local e-bike age limits.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Moped" means any of the following motor vehicles capable of speeds of not more than 30 miles per hour with a 150-pound rider on a dry, level, hard surface with no wind
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (integral motor, pedals, up to 30 mph) or motor bicycle (add-on power unit, up to 30 mph), and faster devices are motorcycles
non_ebike_devices.notes: A pedal bike over 750 W, or one not meeting a class, with an integral power source and a top speed of 30 mph or less is a moped (a motor vehicle). A bicycle with an added, non-integral power unit capped at 30 mph is a 'motor bicycle', which follows bicycle rules but is not an e-bike. Faster devices are motorcycles needing a Class M license, registration and insurance. Moped license, registration and age rules in chs. 341 and 343 were not checked here, so those fields are null.

open_questions: Effective dates: 2019 Wis. Act 34 created these sections. The act's effective date was not confirmed, so effective_date is null.
Sidewalk default: § 346.94(1) bars any 'vehicle' from sidewalks unless local authorities permit it. Applied to e-bikes through § 346.806(1). Confirm with WisDOT guidance.
Moped and motor bicycle license, registration and age rules not verified.
No 2025-2026 e-bike statute changes found in the code updated through 2025 Wis. Act 247.
WI.verifier_notes: 340, 346, 347 and 349 PDFs (updated through 2025 Act 247) confirm all quotes. No corrections.

WV.name: West Virginia

definition.quote: the term "electric bicycle" means a two or three wheeled vehicle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of fewer than 750 watts.
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of fewer than 750 watts
definition.notes: Motor must be FEWER THAN 750 W, so a bike labeled exactly 750 W does not literally qualify. Class 1: pedal assist only, stops at 20 mph. Class 2: motor may propel alone, no assist at 20 mph, throttle expressly permitted (§ 17C-11-8(g)). Class 3: pedal assist only, stops at 28 mph, speedometer required (§ 17C-11-8(f)). Current text from 2023 HB 2062 (passed Feb 27, 2023, 'in effect ninety days from passage', so about May 28, 2023). If an e-bike's motor is modified past a § 17C-1-70 limit, it 'is no longer an electric bicycle' (§ 17C-11-8(c)). § 17C-11-8(e) says the motor must stop when the operator stops pedaling, or applies the brakes and stops pedaling, which sits awkwardly with the Class 2 throttle permission.

label_required.quote: A person may not tamper with or modify an electric bicycle so as to change the motor-powered speed capability or motor engagement between pedal-assist and throttle-assist types of engagement.
label_required.quote_note: No labeling clause exists in W. Va. Code 17C-1-70 or 17C-11-8 (verifier read both on Oct 16, 2026). The quote is the anti-tampering clause. It does not itself show the absence of a label rule.

helmet.quote: A person under 15 years of age who is an operator or passenger on an electric bicycle shall wear a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet, pursuant to the Child Bicycle Safety Act

license_registration_insurance.quote: A person owning or operating an electric bicycle is not subject to the provisions of §17A-1-1 et seq., §17B-1-1 et seq., or §17D-1-1 et seq. of this code, relating to registration, title, driver's license, and financial responsibility requirements.

where_allowed.quote: A Class 3 electric bicycle may not be operated on a bicycle path, multiuse trail, or single-use trail unless it is within a highway or roadway
where_allowed.roads: Allowed. The operator has the rights and duties of the driver of a vehicle under Chapter 17C (§ 17C-11-8(a)). Class 1 and 2 have the same rights as regular bicycles on roads and trails where regular bicycles may go (§ 17C-11-8(h)(1)).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: Allowed. Bicyclists must use a marked bicycle lane when riding slower than traffic, with exceptions (§ 17C-11-5(a)).
where_allowed.paths_trails: Class 1 and 2 allowed wherever regular bicycles are allowed, including trails on public lands. Class 3 barred from bicycle paths, multiuse trails and single-use trails unless within a highway or roadway or the managing municipality, local authority or state agency expressly permits it. No e-bike may go where regular bicycles are banned (§ 17C-11-8(h)(2)-(3)).
where_allowed.sidewalks: No statewide e-bike or bicycle sidewalk rule found. Municipalities regulate bicycle operation under § 17C-2-8(a)(8).
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: Not on bicycle paths or trails unless within a roadway or expressly permitted. Speedometer required. No statewide Class 3 minimum age in the current text (see open_questions).

local_authority.quote: Regulating the operation of bicycles and requiring the registration and licensing of same, including the requirement of a registration fee;
local_authority.details: Local authorities may regulate bicycle operation on their streets and require bicycle registration (§ 17C-2-8(a)(8)), and municipalities may enact helmet ordinances (§ 17C-11A-8). Path managers may permit Class 3 on paths (§ 17C-11-8(h)(2)). Whether 'regulating the operation of bicycles' reaches e-bikes and lets a city set age limits is not stated. Several city codes (for example Wheeling, Star City, Point Pleasant) still carry an under-16 Class 3 rule copied from the pre-2023 state law.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Moped" means every motorcycle or motor-driven cycle unless otherwise specified in this chapter, which is equipped with two or three wheels, foot pedals to permit muscular propulsion, and an independent power source providing a maximum of two-brake horsepower
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: moped (pedals, up to 2 brake horsepower, up to 30 mph), otherwise motor-driven cycle or motorcycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A bike with a motor of 750 W or more, or modified past a class limit, is not an electric bicycle (§ 17C-11-8(c)). With pedals, no more than 2 brake horsepower and a motor-only top speed of 30 mph or less it is a moped, which is a type of motorcycle or motor-driven cycle. Without pedals it is a motor-driven cycle or motorcycle. License, registration, insurance and age rules for mopeds in Chapters 17A and 17B were not checked here, so those fields are null.

open_questions: Class 3 minimum age: the 2020 and 2022 law said a person under 16 may not operate a Class 3 bike. The 2023 enrolled HB 2062 and the current official code list § 17C-11-8(i) with only a subdivision '(2)' (the helmet rule) and no '(1)'. The age rule appears to have been deleted, so there is no statewide Class 3 minimum age now. The skipped number looks like a drafting artifact. Recommend the app return 'unclear' rather than 'legal' for riders under 16 on Class 3 in West Virginia until the Legislature or DMV confirms.
No label requirement found in the current e-bike sections. The vision model may not find a class label on bikes sold in WV.
Watt limit is 'fewer than 750 watts'. Need a rule for bikes labeled exactly 750 W.
Effective date of 2023 HB 2062 computed as 90 days from passage (Feb 27, 2023), about May 28, 2023.
Moped license, registration and age rules not verified.
Some municipal codes still contain the old under-16 Class 3 rule. Local rules may be stricter than state law.

verdict_cautions.reason: The enacted 2023 text (HB 2062) dropped the under-16 Class 3 rule, while the introduced bill kept it and renumbered only the passenger rule. Likely a drafting error, and several city codes still carry the under-16 rule.

WV.verifier_notes: Enacted HB 2062 (2023) has no 17C-11-8(i)(1). Code site shows no later amendment. Added an under-16 Class 3 caution.

WY.name: Wyoming

definition.quote: "Electric bicycle" means a bicycle or tricycle equipped with fully operable pedals, a seat or saddle for the rider's use and an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty (750) watts
definition.motor_watts_basis: an electric motor of less than seven hundred fifty (750) watts
definition.notes: Motor must be LESS THAN 750 W, so a bike labeled exactly 750 W does not literally qualify. Class 1: pedal assist only, stops at 20 mph. Class 2: may propel without pedaling, no assist at 20 mph. Class 3: pedal assist only, stops at 28 mph. An electric bicycle 'shall not be a motor vehicle' (§ 31-5-707(a)) and is excluded from 'moped'. Enacted by 2019 SF 81 (effective July 1, 2019). Source PDF is the Legislature's Title 31 compilation dated May 8, 2026. Wyoming's law has NO Class 3 speedometer rule, NO age limits and NO helmet rule.

label_required.quote: On and after January 1, 2020, every manufacturer or distributor of an electric bicycle shall ensure that a label is permanently affixed in a prominent location on each electric bicycle sold or distributed

license_registration_insurance.quote: is not subject to the provisions of this title relating to financial responsibility, driver's licenses, registration, certificates of title or off-road recreational vehicles. An electric bicycle shall not be a motor vehicle.

where_allowed.quote: Every person propelling a vehicle by human power or riding a bicycle or electric bicycle has all of the rights and all of the duties applicable to the driver of any vehicle under this act
where_allowed.roads: Allowed with the rights and duties of a vehicle driver (§ 31-5-702).
where_allowed.bike_lanes: No e-bike-specific bike lane rule found. Bicycle rules apply.
where_allowed.paths_trails: No statewide path ban for any class. A local authority or state agency with jurisdiction may regulate any class on trails it manages, including natural-surface nonmotorized trails (§ 31-5-707(f)). Wyoming State Parks has its own e-bike trail rules (not reviewed).
where_allowed.sidewalks: Likely not allowed under motor power. § 31-5-120 bars driving 'any vehicle except motorized wheelchairs other than by human power upon a sidewalk'. Pedaling with the motor off appears allowed. Local ordinances may differ.
where_allowed.class3_restrictions: None at state level beyond what trail managers set.

local_authority.quote: Regulating the operation of bicycles and electric bicycles and requiring the registration and licensing of bicycles and electric bicycles, including the requirement of a registration fee;
local_authority.details: Local authorities may regulate e-bike operation and even require e-bike registration and licensing on streets under their jurisdiction (§ 31-5-109(a)(vii)). Local authorities and state agencies may regulate any class on trails they manage (§ 31-5-707(f)). Age limits are not named but 'regulating the operation' is broad. Expect city rules in places like Jackson and Cheyenne.

non_ebike_devices.quote: "Moped" means a vehicle equipped with two (2) or three (3) wheels, foot pedals to permit muscular propulsion by human power, an automatic transmission and a motor with cylinder capacity not exceeding fifty (50) cubic centimeters
non_ebike_devices.treated_as: unclear: likely motorcycle or motor-driven cycle
non_ebike_devices.notes: A device with a motor of 750 W or more, no pedals, or no class is not an electric bicycle. The moped definition is written around engine cylinder capacity, so an electric device may not fit it. It would then likely be a motorcycle or motor-driven cycle, which is a motor vehicle needing a license with motorcycle endorsement, registration and insurance. This mapping was not confirmed from statute or WYDOT guidance.

open_questions: Watt limit is 'less than 750 watts'. Need a rule for bikes labeled exactly 750 W.
No statewide age or helmet rule for any class. The app should still surface local rules, since § 31-5-109 lets towns regulate and license e-bikes.
Sidewalk use under motor power appears barred by § 31-5-120. No WYDOT guidance found.
Classification of over-limit electric devices (moped vs motorcycle vs motor-driven cycle) not confirmed.
Confirmed by the verifier. The Legislature's 2025 and 2026 bill lists contain no e-bike bill, and the May 8, 2026 Title 31 compilation, made after the 2026 session, shows the 2019 text unchanged.
WY.verifier_notes: Less than 750 W, no state age or helmet rule and the local power to license e-bikes confirmed in the May 8, 2026 Title 31 file. The Legislature's 2025 and 2026 bill lists contain no e-bike bill.
